~~~text
independent policy dates. The effective calendar determines whether uncertainty is driven by
branches, common dates or both. Forecasting can be
valuable in its own right, but a forecast response to an input change does not
by itself justify changing a pricing rule. A new native implementation should
be considered only after the instrument and dependence comparison changes a
specific decision about the first prototype.

\subsection{12. Networks and spillovers}
Contacting one member of a household can affect another; a branch campaign can
shift business across nearby branches. The inspected MossSpider and
inferference sources implement different network and grouped-allocation
constructions. Their eligible populations, exposure definitions and uncertainty
calculations cannot be harmonised by renaming columns.
\citep{exec24_interference_mossspider,exec24_interference_inferference}

An initial study needs one economic exposure and a defensible assignment
mechanism. The population whose outcomes matter can differ from the population
of possible recipients. The matching statistical method can be compared
with a deliberately restrictive no-spillover analysis. Generic Java
or C++ network libraries can represent relationships or simulate a supplied
process; that is not evidence that they identify an effect in the observed
bank network. Connectivity alone therefore does not resolve interference.
The highest-value missing information is often the assignment mechanism and
the economically relevant links, not a faster graph traversal.

\subsection{13. Mechanisms, mediation and sensitivity}
A policy may improve repayment through contact, understanding and a revised
payment plan. The total effect of the policy and the effect of intervening on
one of those mechanisms are different quantities. The retained R mediation
paper explicitly distinguishes the additional assumptions needed for causal
mediation; randomising treatment alone does not settle them. The source also
distinguishes model and inference routes.
\citep{exec24_mediation_original,exec24_mediation_sources}

A specified mechanism question determines which mediation procedure and
sensitivity analysis are meaningful. Controlled and natural effects describe
different interventions. A commercial mediation command is a useful
comparator only after the treatment, mediator, population and scale are aligned.
\citep{exec13_ci_stata_mediate,exec20_med_stata_multiple}
A predictive-score decomposition has no automatic causal-mechanism interpretation.
For the investment decision, ask whether the mechanism would change what the
bank funds. If the same action is preferred across the credible sensitivity
range, a more elaborate decomposition may have little immediate value.

\subsection{14. Transfer, selection and missing observations}
Successful results from one branch need not transfer to another. Causal
transport requires assumptions linking the source and target populations;
filling missing values within the source population is a separate task.
The retained transportability argument and commercial imputation manuals
support this distinction.
\citep{pearltransport2014,exec21_transport_stata_mi,
exec21_transport_sas_mi_intro,exec21_transport_sas_mianalyze_intro}

Imputation and target-population weighting require separate justifications.
Those arguments depend on which outcome and assignment information is
missing and why it is believed recoverable. An imputed column does not recover
an unrecorded treatment policy or the potential outcome of a systematically
excluded population. Adverse sensitivity results change the decision just as favourable ones do.
Commercial systems
already provide substantial missing-data facilities; the proposed service's
candidate advantage is a clearer causal interpretation and repeatable
comparison, which still needs evaluation. No new universal solution to
unmeasured selection is claimed.

\section{Computation and the observations on which inference rests}

\subsection{15. Bayesian and hidden-state models}
Posterior computation is valuable when an economic model distinguishes hidden
credit condition from noisy observations. It quantifies uncertainty conditional
on the model and prior. It does not establish the restrictions that give a
policy intervention its meaning. The inspected Bayesian and factor-inference
sources therefore belong in a different category from observational graph
identification.
\citep{exec23_pymc_sources,exec25_bsw_stan,exec24_libdai_source,
exec22_state_stata_bayesmh,exec22_state_stata_sspace_post}

A mature inference engine can evaluate an economically specified model.
Its result still needs prior sensitivity, convergence diagnostics, observation
timing and an account of structural uncertainty. A posterior with narrow intervals can remain
conditional on restrictions the bank cannot verify. Prefer established R,
Python or C++ computation over a new sampler unless the model demands an
unavailable operation. Commercial graphical engines remain conditional
comparators, with numerical inference and causal identification assessed
separately.

\subsection{16. Identity, ownership and information dates}
Before a policy effect is estimated, records must represent the intended
customer, institution and decision date. The retained DuckDB, Feast and Polars
sources provide useful tools for queries, historical features and joins.
Their technical functionality cannot establish that a record was available
to a decision-maker merely because its economic event date is earlier.
\citep{exec19_duckdb_source,exec19_feast_source,exec23_polars_sources}

Data-processing components can preserve event time, publication time and
the availability of revisions. Ownership changes and identity links must
represent the economic unit required by the particular target. A rare incorrect link can have
a large monetary consequence if it involves a large exposure. The existing
public-data survey makes UCI Bank Marketing useful for a timing example:
call duration is unavailable when deciding whether to place the call. It does
not establish an effect of calling from a representative untreated group.
\citep{pd15_uci_bank}
Retrospective access to later information would change the historical
decision being evaluated. The unresolved requirement is credible observation history, not a
missing SQL function.

\subsection{17. Numerical computation and a reproducible study}
Java regression libraries, C++ numerical kernels and other-language panel
packages can reduce development effort. Their statistical surroundings matter.
The inspected C++ panel sources sit inside procedures that select samples,
define effects and scale uncertainty; a coefficient solver alone does not
preserve those steps. A Julia suite and its individual components likewise
must not be counted as independent corroborating implementations.
\citep{exec25_paneljava_commons,exec25_panelcxx_fixest,
exec25_panelcxx_xhdfe,exec25_panelother_julia}

A numerical component answers a computational need; a complete statistical
procedure also determines the sample and inference. A port is justified when
a measured constraint makes its expected benefit exceed development, comparison
and maintenance costs. A study run
through a library, a command line or an assistant should preserve the same
question and result. Agent frameworks and vendor service clients may help
conduct the work, but a completed call is not evidence that a causal
interpretation is justified.
\citep{exec24_framework_contracts,exec23_workflow_sasctl}

\input{writing-repair/2026-10-29/src/301406daaa5228ef.tex}

\section{What the commercial comparison changes}
Commercial statistical packages are credible alternatives, not an empty space
waiting for the proposed service. The inspected Stata procedures cover distinct
treatment, panel, survival and structural questions; the SAS sources distinguish
statistical procedures from service access. The bank may already possess
trained staff and relevant entitlements. A proposal that ignores those assets
overstates the saving from a new platform.
\citep{exec13_ci_stata_causal_intro,exec18_gp_stata_xthdid,
exec14_survival_stata,exec13_ivrd_sas,exec23_workflow_sasctl}

Compare three feasible alternatives: improve existing analytical practice;
connect a small set of existing procedures; or build a broader common service.
For each study, distinguish a vendor-authored procedure, a community extension
inside a commercial host, an open client to a licensed server, and a general
numerical component. They have different support and cost implications. The
comparison has not established exact current prices, complete entitlements,
performance at the bank's scale or the absence of equivalent features in all
competitors. Those are unresolved commercial questions, not findings of
technical superiority.

The proposed investment is therefore conditional. Its candidate contribution
is a disciplined connection between the business question, assumptions,
software choices and financial interpretation. Fund a narrow comparison that
can show whether that connection prevents material errors or saves analyst
time. If the existing estate achieves the same result more cheaply, retain it.
If differences in estimands, graph interpretation or information dates repeatedly
change decisions, a shared service becomes more persuasive.

\input{writing-repair/2026-10-29/src/72f64a0c152b5f00.tex}
\input{writing-repair/2026-10-29/src/626099247fe4b6ef.tex}

\section{What remains to be learned}
The seventeen areas now lead to explicit provisional choices, but this synthesis
does not complete the underlying census. There is no claim that every
language--area pair has been exhaustively searched or that every candidate has
been executed. Complete dated source and capability comparisons where a missing
candidate could change the preferred route. Compare actual implementations on
matched questions before claiming numerical agreement. Obtain edition,
entitlement and price information before a purchase recommendation. Investigate
transitive numerical details only where they could change the inference or
the selected integration.

Some limits require new information rather than more programming: unidentified
effects under unrestricted confounding, absent support for a proposed action,
unknown assignment histories and uncertain transfer to a new population. State
the restrictions or data that would narrow each limit. These findings can
support a useful proposal even when they do not support a universal product.
~~~

~~~text
nor certify their adapters. The commercial source follow-up narrows two

can reveal a material analytical benefit.
~~~

After:
~~~text
The useful comparison asks whether an existing procedure answers the bank's
question and what additional work preserves its assumptions. Three choices
illustrate why conditional reuse can be justified before a new product is
built, while the meaning of a reported effect must be settled immediately.

\subsection{Reuse the estimator after choosing the population}
For an offer made once to each customer, the relevant average may cover all
eligible customers or only those who actually received the offer. DoubleML's
inspected Python interactive-regression implementation distinguishes these
targets, checks for a single binary treatment, and directs instrumental-variable
data to a different model. It forms separate predictions under treatment and
control, processes the propensity estimates, and constructs the corresponding
score. These are useful reasons to integrate the selected original procedure
instead of writing another implementation merely to change language.
The inspected revision is 6884b5f, dated 23 September 2026; its declared
BSD-3-Clause licence and dependencies are recorded separately from the earlier
installed-version observation. \citep{exec23_doubleml_reuse_source}

The recommendation is conditional integration of a specified model, with an
unadjusted or transparent adjusted comparison retained. Neither the choice of
predictor nor clipping a propensity establishes that every customer had a
realistic chance of receiving each action. Sampling dependence, permissible
covariates, target weights and the uncertainty calculation must agree with the
study. The full distribution and matched adverse-data trials belong in the
prototype comparison. Porting is justified only if a measured platform or
cost constraint outweighs the burden of maintaining the statistical procedure.

For phased adoption across branches, \texttt{did} offers a different target:
effects for an adoption cohort at a particular date, followed by an explicitly
chosen aggregation. The newly retrieved DESCRIPTION comes from the same
74b88eb commit as the retained API source. It identifies version 2.5.1.902,
R at least 4.1.0, a GPL-3 declaration and dependencies including DRDID.
Its bytes match the earlier mutable description, closing that specific
identity uncertainty. This is a repository version, not evidence of a stable
published release or of a complete deployment entitlement. A request for a
separate LICENSE file returned 404; that does not cancel the declaration.
\citep{survey29did,exec24_panelr_did}

The source's treatment of time-varying weights matters economically. In a
balanced panel the default comparison uses the earlier period's weights;
choosing varying weights switches to the repeated-cross-section estimator.
In an unbalanced panel, fixing weights at an anchor date restricts the sample
to units observed then. Thus two analysts can agree on the branch records yet
answer different questions after selecting different weighting rules. Imagine
two equally weighted customer groups with hypothetical effects of 10 and
$-10$ units. Their equally weighted effect is zero. If the analysis gives
the first group weight three and the second weight one, the weighted effect
is $(3\times10-10)/4=5$. This is a constructed arithmetic example, not a
\texttt{did} run: changing weights alone changes the population conclusion.
\citep{survey29didapi}

The appropriate proposal choice is an original R procedure with explicit
cohort, calendar, weighting and confidence-band definitions. A Python or
commercial comparison is useful when it implements the same target. The
selected API also distinguishes point estimates alone from influence-function
output required for inference and aggregation. Saving computation by requesting
only coefficients would therefore remove information needed for the proposed
investment decision. \citep{survey29didapi}

\subsection{Identification and numerical estimation do different jobs}
The inspected \texttt{causaleffect} documentation describes a symbolic answer
for an intervention distribution, optionally conditional on specified variables.
It returns a formula or structured probability expression when the query is
identified under the supplied graph; a nonidentification path reports the
graphical obstruction. The graph convention represents hidden common causes
through specially marked edges. Its selected source is version 1.3.17 at
ff6059f; the package Date field and commit timestamp disagree, so that
revision is described by its exact saved identity. \citep{exec18_rid_causaleffect}

This supports a bounded role as an identification reference alongside the
chosen graph representation. It does not choose the bank's causal graph,
estimate the formula from customer records, or produce a sampling interval.
Those tasks need separate evidence. Before accepting an implementation, compare
an adjustment case, a genuinely nonidentified case and a conditional query;
preserve variable names, hidden-edge marks and the distinction between an
unidentified effect and a computation that failed. Ananke or aGrUM can remain
alternatives where their documented query and hidden-variable semantics match.
There is no scientific reason to port the symbolic algorithm until a concrete
constraint makes the original implementation unsuitable.

\subsection{Compare with a named commercial service}
The current causaLens pages identify a specific service to compare: Digital
Workers assembled through the Digital Worker Factory, with the System of Work
for management and monitoring. The pages describe portable containers,
connections to existing business systems, human review and escalation, and
advertise human-guided causal discovery, causal model building, root-cause
analysis and intervention optimisation. These observations were made on
29 October 2026; no pre-cutoff availability or equivalence to an earlier
DecisionOS offering is inferred. \citep{survey29causalens}

This changes the commercial comparison. A proposal based only on graph editing,
ordinary system connections or automated reports cannot treat those functions
as unserved demand. The useful question is whether the proposed combination
improves the formulation of an economic choice, the treatment of identifying
assumptions, uncertainty and the analyst's time at a competitive total cost.
The vendor's pages establish advertised scope. They do not expose, in the
inspected material, a versioned causal-estimation specification, an independently
reconstructable comparison, a price or the bank's contractual rights.
Consequently their performance multipliers and return claims are not used as
measured advantages in this proposal. \citep{survey29causalens}

A fair later comparison would give both approaches the same information about
an offer or servicing decision, including a case with an omitted cause and a
case with outcome-dependent loss of records. It would evaluate the target
chosen, assumptions stated, consequential errors, uncertainty, time and full
cost. Correctly requesting missing information can be a better answer than a
confident numerical recommendation. The current source evidence supports
including the named commercial service in that comparison; actual superiority,
licensing and adoption remain to be established.
~~~

## Edit 114

docs/causal_banking_integrated_argument_2026-10-29.tex

Supply the assembled temporal chapter with an economic question and a route through its actual studies.

Substantive destination: All original thirteen studies, equations, calculations, limitations and alternatives remain in the chapter.

Before:
~~~text
\chapter{Learning relationships over time}
~~~
After:
~~~text
\chapter{Learning relationships over time}

A funding decision has a date, an information set and an outcome horizon.
A learned temporal relationship has these attributes only if the observation
and estimation procedure preserve them. Yesterday's rate may predict tomorrow's
balance because the rate changes retention, because both respond to a shared
liquidity shock, or because aggregation conceals their within-day order. The
useful question is what the observed sequence and any intervention information
allow the bank to distinguish.

The first comparisons follow that question through R, Python, Java, native
engines, Julia, Rust and MATLAB. They distinguish temporal restrictions,
structural innovations, supplied dynamic models, predictive information and
changing mechanisms. The detailed Tigramite study examines how statistics,
endpoints, intervention contrasts and resampling can change meaning within
one package. The later studies examine discovery delegates, reinforcement and
attention-based search, evaluation truth and discrete score helpers. They
connect a method's mathematical claim to the inputs and results that an
implementation actually preserves. Throughout, the worked examples keep
monetary consequences visible while distinguishing an exact construction,
a source finding and an executed experiment.

~~~

## Edit 121

docs/writing-repair/2026-10-29/src/877d9634b7a31a4b.tex

Repair missing word and punctuation spacing in the reinforcement-search exposition.

Substantive destination: All claims, mathematics, cited works, examples and adoption conditions retained; changes only restore word separation.

Before:
~~~text
\section[Reinforcement search and discovery contracts]{Reinforcement search and discovery contracts}
\label{sec:exec28-rl}
Reinforcement learning can search for a causal graph without establishing that the graph is identified.
For a bank considering early reminders, the graph-search problem is to compare possible relations
among eligibility,reminder assignment,repayment and recorded customer characteristics. This is
different from learning a servicing policy that will act on customers. In the discovery methods
reviewed here, the reinforcement learner is an optimizer: its actions generate graphs or variable
orders, and a statistical score supplies a reward. A better search can improve a score while
leaving the information needed for a causal effect unchanged. Public or generated data can test
the search and interface contracts before costly bank experiments, provided the score's assumptions
and the target graph are declared separately.~\citep{exec28_rl_zhu,exec28_rl_wang}

\subsection{Graph search versus ordering search}
Zhu,Ng and Chen formulate discovery as a search over directed graphs with a score and acyclicity
penalties. Their model discussion assumes scalar structural equations with jointly independent
additive noises,causal minimality and independently sampled observations. The paper explicitly
recognizes that further restrictions are needed for unique graph identification; its selected
experiments use identifiable families. Its encoder-decoder proposes adjacency matrices,and the
best-scoring sampled graph is the output of the search. Those statements do not establish validity
under a latent common cause,a persistent panel or unmeasured selection into reminders. In a
banking application, such features must be represented or restricted before the graph score can
be interpreted scientifically.~\citep{exec28_rl_zhu}

Wang and coauthors instead search variable orderings. Each complete ordering defines a fully
connected acyclic candidate; variable selection subsequently removes edges. Their sequential
decoder masks previously selected nodes,and the paper distinguishes episodic and dense rewards.
The consistency discussion assumes an identifiable structural equation model and a suitable
distribution family. Its proposition explains why an ordering-compatible model reproducing the
same distribution must cover the true graph under those assumptions. It does not guarantee
global optimization by policy gradients; the paper explicitly discusses local convergence and
approximation. Ordering removes a combinatorial acyclicity burden from the candidate construction,
but does not remove misspecification,finite-sample selection error or causal nonidentification.
Attention in an encoder is a representation mechanism,not an edge-confidence or identification
certificate.~\citep{exec28_rl_wang}

\subsection{A precise qualification at the penalty boundary}
For a graph $G$ with binary adjacency matrix $A$,write $S(G)$ for the score to minimize and
$h(A)=\operatorname{tr}(e^A)-d$ for the nonnegative cycle measure on $d$ nodes. The graph-search
formulation adds $\lambda_1\mathbf{1}\{G\notin\mathcal D\}+\lambda_2h(A)$,where $\mathcal D$
is the set of DAGs. Proposition1 in the inspected Zhu preprint gives the non-strict condition
\[
 \lambda_1+\lambda_2h_{\min}\geq S_U-S_L,
\]
with $S_L$ a lower bound on all graph scores,$S_U$ an upper bound on the optimum DAG score,and
$h_{\min}>0$ the smallest cycle measure over cyclic candidates. Its proof establishes that an
optimal DAG cannot be beaten by a cyclic candidate under this bound. At equality,however,that
argument need not exclude a cyclic candidate tied with the optimal DAG. The reverse proof uses
a strict improvement that does not follow from being a distinct tied minimizer. The distinction
matters if an implementation returns any maximizer of reward.~\citep{exec28_rl_zhu}

An exact project construction isolates the boundary without making a claim about the paper's
empirical BIC results. Enumerate the four loopless directed graphs on two nodes. Assign score1
to each of the three DAGs and score0 to the two-cycle. Set $S_L=0$, $S_U=1$,
$\lambda_1=1$ and $\lambda_2=0$. The displayed condition holds with equality,and every penalized
score is1. The cyclic graph is therefore also a minimizer. The optimal value still equals the
DAG-constrained optimum,and an optimal DAG remains available; what fails is the stronger
conclusion that every unconstrained minimizer is acyclic.~\citep{exec28_rl_reference}

A sufficient repair for that stronger conclusion is strict domination,
$\lambda_1+\lambda_2h_{\min}>S_U-S_L$. Then every cyclic penalized score is strictly greater
than $S_U$,whereas some optimal DAG has score at most $S_U$. Alternatively,an exact optimizer
can explicitly prefer a DAG among tied optimal candidates,if such a candidate is available.
In the finite witness,$\lambda_1=3/2$ makes the cyclic score $3/2$ and leaves the DAG scores1.
Neither repair proves that a practical policy-gradient search finds the global optimum or samples
a DAG. A returned candidate must still pass an independent acyclicity check,and approximate
cycle thresholds need a declared tolerance policy. The construction qualifies the stated general
score condition; it does not assert a failure rate for the original experiments.
\citep{exec28_rl_reference}

\subsection{What the selected implementation supports}
The selected gCastle source gives concrete contracts beyond the algorithm names. The RL reward
has BIC and unequal-variance variants,regression choices,and a cycle threshold of $10^{-5}$.
Its positive-$\ell_1$ branch refers to \texttt{l1\_grapha\_reg},whereas initialization stores
\texttt{l1\_graph\_reg}. Under the ordinary constructor path without an injected extra attribute,
that branch requires correction or a demonstrated supported alternative before enablement.
The selected normal-equation regression and median-scaled Gaussian-process paths also motivate
rank and scale fixtures. These are static source findings,not observed runtime error counts.
\citep{exec28_rl_gcastle}

The selected CORL entrypoint documents a \texttt{dag\_mask} keyword but retrieves it using
attribute lookup on the keyword dictionary. A plain Python dictionary does not expose a key
through that attribute lookup. The authored witness supplies an all-zero mask by key and obtains
the default through attribute lookup,while key lookup retrieves the mask. The next integration
must demonstrate that forbidden-edge constraints actually reach the graph constructor.
The inspected constructor builds order-consistent entries and multiplies by a mask; its pruning
routine treats row-selected columns as predictors of each variable,and the search returns a
transpose. This complete conversion needs a declared endpoint convention and a labelled
round-trip fixture. A high score cannot compensate for a reversed named edge.
\citep{exec28_rl_gcastle,exec28_rl_reference}

The reward comparison requires similar care. CORL's selected score branches omit the displayed
edge-count penalties,whereas the RL score includes them. That observation alone does not prove
incorrect ordering rankings: fully connected candidates of the same dimension have the same
number of edges before pruning. The correct comparison must trace which candidate is scored,
which regression family is fitted,and when pruning occurs. Its Transformer source normalizes
the attention scores along dimension1 and calls functional dropout without an explicit training
argument. A pinned tensor-library profile and repeated evaluation fixture should establish the
intended normalization and evaluation behavior before this path is adopted. These source details
do not turn an attention matrix into a causal graph.~\citep{exec28_rl_gcastle}

\subsection{Dependency profiles and a finite public qualification}
The complementary CDT inspection shows why listing dependencies is insufficient. The selected
Python and R requirement files list package names without versions. Python setup and requirements
also differ: torch is listed in one route,while skrebate is included in setup. Container recipes use
mutable base-image tags and unpinned package installation. The default interpreter is
\texttt{Rscript},resolved from the environment unless overridden; the availability template calls
\texttt{library} rather than querying versions. A repository MIT notice and Apache2 setup metadata
remain different declarations,so neither should be silently promoted to a complete distribution
rights decision. A proposed reproducible environment must be selected and recorded explicitly;
these manifests cannot reconstruct an exact historical installation by themselves.
\citep{exec28_rl_cdt}

A finite public prototype can address these known interfaces without requiring bank truth.
First,bind one package/build/dependency route and its component terms. Second,use labelled
generated variables to test permutation,mask and endpoint preservation,including forbidden edges
and ambiguous graph output. Third,separate equality and strict-penalty examples from finite search
tests,retaining every failed or nonacyclic candidate in the denominator. Fourth,exercise constant,
collinear and nonfinite data and repeated evaluation under the selected regression and tensor
profile. Finally,inject failed children,large diagnostics,partial files and interruption into the
R boundary. Each fixture needs an independently declared expected result; a numerical output is
not automatically success. These are proposed conformance tests,not trials performed by this review.

Conditional reuse remains the defensible product decision. A narrow discovery adapter can retain
upstream search mechanics while imposing explicit variable,score,constraint and failure contracts.
A direct R route or a separately implemented ordering search may be preferable when those
contracts are easier to verify than a broad wrapper. Porting requires an additional equivalence
argument and maintenance budget. The two primary papers and selected code paths strengthen the
proposal's mechanism-level comparison,but do not exhaust reinforcement or attention-based
discovery,establish graph confidence,or qualify dependent banking data.
A discovery optimizer is useful only when its search result preserves the declared causal target and assumptions.

~~~

~~~text
\section{Python identification: the question determines the reusable capability}
\label{exec18:pyid-question}

A lending analyst may ask whether changing an offer improves average repayment,
or whether a particular customer who failed to repay would have succeeded under
another offer. These questions share variables but require different information.
Let $A$ be a binary intervention and $Y(a)$ the repayment outcome under its
assignment to $a$. An average contrast $E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\}$ uses two marginal
intervention distributions. The retrospective question
$P\{Y(1)=1\mid A=0,Y=0\}$ also links the factual outcome to that person's
unobserved outcome under another assignment. A package capable of computing the
first quantity does not thereby identify the second. Nor does a representation
of a counterfactual variable establish an algorithm for identifying its law.
The distinction changes the proposed product boundary: a request must state its
query class and available information before an engine is selected.
\citep{exec13_y0_dsl,exec18_pyid_contract}

\subsection{Four complementary source boundaries}
\label{exec18:pyid-packages}

The inspected DoWhy revision separates model specification, identification and
estimation. Its identification method chooses between an ID identifier and an
automatic identifier. It can also construct a graph from supplied inputs, so
the proposed banking route requires an explicit reviewed graph instead of
treating that convenience as elicitation evidence. In the selected revision,
the function assigns the \texttt{proceed\_when\_unidentifiable} option but does
not forward it to either identifier; validation must inspect the returned
estimand and assumptions. This is a static source finding, not a demonstrated
runtime failure. Optional reuse of the pinned identification boundary remains
the preferred initial path. Section~\ref{sec:exec24-gcm-reuse} supplies the
separate GCM source review, including its structural assumptions and
factual-noise reconstruction. Its narrower reference-only decision does not
inherit qualification from this identification interface.
\citep{exec13_dowhy}

The selected pgmpy adjustment interface offers a narrower complementary role:
generation of candidate sets for a specified exposure and outcome. Candidate
generation must be followed by independent causal validation. The reviewed
implementation checks exposure parents in a way that can accept a supplied
mediator set when the exposure has no parents; its \texttt{minimal\_variance}
branch is advertised but raises \texttt{NotImplementedError}. An adapter must
exclude that branch and validate the chosen total-effect adjustment criterion.
Neither a minimal separator nor a successful role check guarantees a globally
minimum-variance adjustment set. These restrictions do not establish anything
about uninspected pgmpy modules.~\citep{exec13_pgmpy_reuse_primary}

The pinned y0 implementation gives a symbolic ADMG identification route.
Its conditional algorithm invokes a rule-2 exchange test and otherwise
normalizes an identified joint distribution. The inspected separation path has
the previously developed bidirected-collider counterexample: conditioning on
the collider can give probability $9/10$, whereas replacing the relevant
variable by intervention gives $1/2$. The proposed native conditional path
therefore remains disabled. Identifying the joint distribution and then
normalizing is a possible restricted alternative when that joint is identified
and its denominator is positive. This sufficient route is not a completeness
claim for conditional identification: failure to identify the entire joint
does not prove failure to identify a particular conditional target.
\citep{exec13_y0_id,exec13_y0_idc,exec13_y0_rule2,exec13_y0_separation,exec13_y0_oracles}

Ananke adds a differently organized source reference. The selected authentic
\texttt{ananke-causal} 0.5.0 distribution was uploaded on 5 December 2023; it is
not presented as the newest release. Its \texttt{OneLineID} object fixes
intervention vertices, finds relevant outcome ancestors and checks whether
each district's kernel can be obtained by fixing other vertices. The \texttt{id()}
method returns a Boolean. The \texttt{functional()} method returns a string
describing the fixing expression and prints fixing-order diagnostics. That
string is not yet a typed portable expression, a fitted estimator or an
uncertainty statement. Proposed reuse would preserve variable identities,
sums, products and fixing operations in a restricted expression representation;
it would never evaluate arbitrary returned text as program code.
\citep{exec18_pyid_one_line,exec18_pyid_contract}

Ananke's experimental identification variants also show why exception names
cannot be the scientific result contract. \texttt{OneLineAID} raises
\texttt{NotIdentifiedError} when the experimental graphs fail its ancestral
precondition; \texttt{OneLineGID} uses the same exception for nonconforming
experimental graphs. A precondition failure must be distinguished from a
valid query proved nonidentified in a declared model class. The source's
supplied-model witness routines compare observational marginals and
interventional distributions of two supplied models. They do not establish
automatic witness construction for every query or arbitrary cross-world
identification.~\citep{exec18_pyid_one_line}

Other Ananke components answer different questions. Its oracle intervenes in a
supplied true model and explicitly states that identification is not considered.
Conditional normalization inside that oracle cannot be cited as identification
from observed data. The missing-data routine addresses full-law identification
with explicit \texttt{R\_} and \texttt{X\_} naming and colluding-path checks.
The \texttt{CausalEffect} estimation interface targets the average contrast
$E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\}$ and selects among adjustment-, primal- and nested-fixability
strategies. A file named \texttt{counterfactual\_mean.py} is therefore evidence
about that average-effect interface, not a guarantee for a customer's joint
potential outcomes.~\citep{exec18_pyid_oracle,exec18_pyid_missing,exec18_pyid_mean}

\subsection{What even a randomized study leaves undetermined}
\label{exec18:pyid-coupling}

Consider an exact illustrative population, rather than a fitted bank dataset.
Let $A$ and a latent response type $U$ be independent fair binary variables,
and impose consistency $Y=Y(A)$ and no interference. In the stable model
$Y(0)=U$ and $Y(1)=U$. In the switching model $Y(0)=U$ and $Y(1)=1-U$.
Both are compatible with an allowed $A\to Y$ causal model when faithfulness
is not imposed. The first has no individual response to assignment; in the
second, improvements and harms cancel in the mean. Direct enumeration gives
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 P(A=a,Y=y)&=\tfrac14 &&(a,y\in\{0,1\}),\\
 P\{Y(0)=1\}&=P\{Y(1)=1\}=\tfrac12,\\
 E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\}&=0.
\end{aligned}
\label{exec18:pyid-equal-laws}
\end{equation}
Thus an arbitrarily large randomized study can recover the marginal laws in
this example without identifying their within-person coupling. Among factual
untreated failures, $A=0,Y=0$ implies $U=0$. The stable model then has
$Y(1)=0$, whereas the switching model has $Y(1)=1$. Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 P\{Y(1)=1\mid A=0,Y=0\}=
 \begin{cases}0,&\text{stable model},\\1,&\text{switching model}.\end{cases}
\label{exec18:pyid-conditional}
\end{equation}
Both conditioning events have probability $1/4$, so this disagreement is not
created by conditioning on an impossible event. Exact rational enumeration
retains the complete observed and response-type tables for both models.
\citep{exec18_pyid_coupling}

The ambiguity can be described sharply. Write $p_{ij}=P\{Y(0)=i,Y(1)=j\}$
and let $t=p_{01}$ be the proportion helped by the intervention. The two
marginal constraints and normalization force
\begin{equation}
 (p_{00},p_{01},p_{10},p_{11})
   =\left(\tfrac12-t,t,t,\tfrac12-t\right),
 \qquad 0\leq t\leq\tfrac12.
\label{exec18:pyid-sharp}
\end{equation}
Nonnegativity gives the necessary interval. Conversely, for every $t$ in that
interval, take a latent variable with these four response-type probabilities
and randomize $A$ independently. The resulting structural model attains the
same observed law and intervention marginals. This construction proves
attainability of every interior point as well as both endpoints. Therefore
$P\{Y(1)=1,Y(0)=0\}$ has sharp bounds $[0,1/2]$, and randomization yields
\begin{equation}
 P\{Y(1)=1\mid A=0,Y=0\}
 =\frac{p_{01}}{P\{Y(0)=0\}}=2t\in[0,1].
\label{exec18:pyid-bounds}
\end{equation}
This is an identified set under a stated information model, not a confidence
interval. Sampling uncertainty would require a further procedure that accounts
for estimation of the marginal restrictions.~\citep{exec18_pyid_coupling}

Suppose, solely to interpret the target, a successful recovery is worth
USD400 and changing the original intervention costs USD50. The retrospective
conditional net amount is $400(2t)-50$, with sharp range from minus USD50 to
USD350. The two models reverse the sign of this accounting despite identical
average causal effects. This quantity does not establish an implementable
prospective policy: the factual failure used to select the group was not
known before the original assignment. A future servicing decision would need
its own time-indexed action, available history and outcome horizon. The
example motivates a refusal or an explicit identified set, not hindsight-based
deployment.~\citep{exec18_pyid_coupling}

Additional scientific restrictions can change the answer. Monotonicity
$Y(1)\geq Y(0)$ rules out the harmed response type, so $p_{10}=t=0$ under
these equal marginals. It then forces the stable coupling. Randomization alone
does not supply that restriction. Repeated observations, mechanistic evidence
or a richer structural model would have to justify their own connection across
worlds and time; simply collecting more independent assignments does not reveal
both incompatible assignments for the same occasion. The proposed service
must record the added assumption and its scientific owner before narrowing
the set.~\citep{exec18_pyid_coupling,exec18_pyid_contract}

\label{exec18:pyid-integration}

The reuse proposal is deliberately component-specific. DoWhy supplies a

symbolic ID route, with its native conditional path excluded pending a
separation repair. Ananke supplies a district-fixing reference and a possible
isolated comparator. Directly adopting all four packages would not create one
uniform counterfactual service. Porting their source would transfer symbolic,
graph and maintenance obligations to this project without a demonstrated
deployment advantage; it is not selected initially.
\citep{exec13_dowhy,exec13_pgmpy_reuse_primary,exec13_y0_id,exec18_pyid_one_line,exec18_pyid_contract}

There is also a concrete environment conflict. The selected Ananke release
declares NumPy at least1.23 and below2, statsmodels at least0.13.2 and below0.14,
and pgmpy at least0.1.21 and below0.2. The selected DoWhy revision requires
NumPy above2 and statsmodels at least0.14; the selected pgmpy revision declares
NumPy at least2 and statsmodels at least0.14.5. These declared intervals cannot
all be satisfied in one unchanged environment. Separate pinned processes
communicating through a named-variable result contract are a design option,
not a tested environment resolution. Ananke also imports Sympy in the
identification source without explicitly declaring it in the inspected wheel
metadata; whether a resolved transitive dependency supplies it remains to be
checked. No import failure has been observed here.
\citep{exec18_pyid_metadata,exec18_pyid_one_line,exec13_dowhy_project,exec13_pgmpy_reuse_primary}

The proposed boundary validates cycles, node identity, edge type, latent status

Rights are similarly tied to the actual component and distribution. The

resolved by a package badge. Notice retention, modified-file marking where

distribution design. Process separation does not settle those questions.
\citep{exec13_dowhy_license,exec13_y0_license,exec18_pyid_license,exec18_pyid_metadata}

This comparison leaves explicit survey work. The selected DoWhy GCM paths
receive their own source review in Section~\ref{sec:exec24-gcm-reuse}; that
review does not complete native qualification or the wider census.
Implementations of general counterfactual identification and Python
partial-identification optimizers still need authenticated technical
sources, model classes and output checks. A solver would need to distinguish
a feasible witness from a certified sharp endpoint; a counterfactual engine
would need to state what structural information permits abduction and coupling.
The four inspected families support the bounded reuse choices described here.
They do not establish exhaustive Python coverage, installed adapters or
qualified banking decisions.~\citep{exec18_pyid_contract}
~~~

~~~text
search and a failed numerical calculation have different remedies. The
~~~

## Edit 150

docs/writing-repair/2026-10-29/src/9e8008ded4eb9569.tex

Before:
~~~text
\section[R mediation and sensitivity contracts]{R mediation and sensitivity: preserving the intervention, the mixture and the unit of uncertainty}
\label{sec:exec25-rmed}

A bank considering a servicing intervention needs to distinguish an improvement
caused by the intervention from an improvement transmitted through a particular
mechanism. Let $A$ denote an offer of restructuring, $M$ subsequent payment
engagement, and $Y$ loss over a fixed horizon. Baseline information $W$ precedes
the offer. A later liquidity assessment $Z$ may be changed by the offer and
affect both engagement and loss. The question therefore requires a declared
intervention on engagement, a target population, an information clock and
assumptions linking the intervention to observed data. R packages supply useful
approaches, but their targets and uncertainty calculations are not interchangeable.
This comparison extends the preceding mediation, medflex, sensemakr and EValue
discussions with CMAverse, medoutcon, regmedint, causalsens, tipr and BayesGmed.
Inspected sources and authored examples support conditional reuse decisions;
they do not establish native qualification. \citep{exec25_rmed_choice}

\subsection{A causal target before a software method}

Write $Y_{a,m}$ for the outcome after setting offer and mediator to $(a,m)$,
and $M_a$ for the mediator under offer $a$. Two complementary natural
decompositions on an additive scale are
\[
 \operatorname{TE}=E(Y_{1,M_1}-Y_{0,M_0})
 =\operatorname{PNDE}+\operatorname{TNIE}
 =\operatorname{TNDE}+\operatorname{PNIE}.
\]
Here $\operatorname{PNDE}=E(Y_{1,M_0}-Y_{0,M_0})$ and
$\operatorname{TNIE}=E(Y_{1,M_1}-Y_{1,M_0})$; the other pair interchanges the
reference treatment. The controlled direct effect $E(Y_{1,m}-Y_{0,m})$ instead
holds engagement at the same specified level. It need not equal a natural
effect, and subtracting it from TE need not yield a natural indirect effect.
The selected BayesGmed primary text develops these distinctions under consistency,
positivity, no unmeasured confounding and a cross-world condition. Randomizing
the offer alone does not supply every mediation assumption; a posterior interval
does not establish them either. \citep{exec25_rmed_yimer_paper}

When offer-induced liquidity confounds engagement and loss, an alternative
draws a new mediator $G_b$ from the distribution of $M_b$ conditional on $W$,
independently of the realized intermediate confounder under the declared
intervention law. Let $\mu(a,z,m,w)=E(Y\mid A=a,Z=z,M=m,W=w)$. The selected
D\'iaz and colleagues paper identifies the corresponding mean as
\[
 \theta(a,b)=\int \mu(a,z,m,w)\,p(z\mid a,w)\,
                  p(m\mid b,w)\,p(w)\,d(z,m,w).
\]
The identifying requirements include the relevant treatment and mediator
exchangeabilities, consistency and conditional support. This intervention
differs from drawing a mediator conditional on the intermediate confounder as
well as baseline information. Changing the conditioning set changes the
pathways assigned to direct and indirect components.
\citep{exec25_rmed_diaz_paper}

Define $\operatorname{IDE}=\theta(1,0)-\theta(0,0)$ and
$\operatorname{IIE}=\theta(1,1)-\theta(1,0)$. Their sum is the total contrast
under the randomized mediator intervention, which need not equal the ordinary
treatment effect. An authored example takes
$P(Z=1\mid A=0)=1/4$, $P(Z=1\mid A=1)=1/2$,
$P(M=1\mid Z)=1/4+Z/2$, and $Y=ZM$. The ordinary treatment effect is $3/16$,
whereas IDE is $3/32$ and IIE is $1/16$, summing to $5/32$. All mediator
probabilities are positive. The difference arises from changing dependence in
the intervention, not estimation error. The product must label the two totals
explicitly. \citep{exec25_rmed_choice}

\subsection{CMAverse: a broad interface with a consequential draw contract}

CMAverse version 0.1.0 documents regression, weighting, inverse odds weighting,
natural-effect, marginal structural and g-formula approaches. Its interface
restricts methods when post-treatment confounders are supplied and changes
natural-effect labels to randomized analogues. Parameter-function and imputation
estimators have different applicability; the documented logistic and Cox
parameter-function cases require a rare outcome. Its sensitivity interface
distinguishes unmeasured confounding from measurement error and documents a
single-variable measurement-error scope. These are useful capabilities to
compare, provided the proposed product exposes method, scale and restrictions.
\citep{exec25_rmed_cmaverse}

The selected g-formula delegate simulates intermediate confounders from
exposure and baseline covariates, then mediators using those variables and the
simulated intermediate values. In its post-treatment-confounder branch, it
subsequently permutes each mediator column across eligible rows. Outcome
prediction retains the row's baseline and intermediate variables. Global
permutation requires a different justification from a draw conditional on that
row's baseline information; separate column permutations also require
justification when a joint mediator law is intended. \citep{exec25_rmed_cmaverse}

For $W\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)$, mediator probabilities $1/4$ and
$3/4$ in the two baseline groups, and outcome regression $WM$, the
baseline-conditioned stochastic mean is $3/8$. A global shuffle pairs each
row with the marginal mediator probability $1/2$, yielding $1/4$ in expectation.
For two identical balanced binary mediators, $E(M_1M_2)=1/2$; independently
permuting columns yields $1/4$ in expectation. These exact witnesses specify
invariants for an adapter. They are neither native failure frequencies nor a
rejection of g-computation. The route is to declare the conditional joint draw,
reconcile the delegate, and retain an explicitly different target or a separately
reviewed repair. \citep{exec25_rmed_choice}

Conditional R invocation is preferable to porting a large method collection
before resolving its target. Requests should carry mediator order, conditioning
set, treatment contrast, scale, simulation budget and random state. Resampling
units must match the data law: a row bootstrap is not automatically branch-cluster
or shared-calendar inference. Imputation, simulation integration and bootstrap
variation require separate accounting. The GPL declaration and full dependency
inventory also accompany contemplated redistribution; this source review does
not clear every artifact. \citep{exec25_rmed_cmaverse,exec25_rmed_choice}

\subsection{medoutcon: efficient scores and the sampling contract}

medoutcon targets natural and interventional effects using one-step and targeted
minimum loss estimators. The primary paper assumes independent, identically
distributed observations, derives an efficient influence function, and requires
positivity and products of nuisance-estimation errors vanishing faster than
$n^{-1/2}$. Cross-fitting relaxes empirical-process restrictions; it does not
prove those rates for arbitrary learners or remove hidden confounding and
dependence. A low-dimensional intermediate-confounder representation avoids
directly estimating a high-dimensional mediator density, a useful advantage
for multivariate engagement measurements within the stated conditions.
\citep{exec25_rmed_diaz_paper}

The selected source switches to natural effects when $Z$ is explicitly absent,
constructs binary contrasts, and rescales outcomes by their observed range.
A constant outcome makes that scaling denominator zero. Contrasts subtract
influence scores before variance calculation; propensity clipping must be
recorded as a numerical choice rather than proof of population support. For
two-phase mediator measurement, the source uses
\[
 D_{\mathrm{obs}}=\frac{R}{\pi}D
                 -\left(\frac{R}{\pi}-1\right)m_D,
\]
where $R$ indicates observation, $\pi$ is inclusion probability and $m_D$
predicts the complete-data influence quantity. With $D=3$, $m_D=1$ and
$\pi=1/2$, the observed and missing cases give 5 and 1, averaging to 3 under
that law. False inclusion probabilities do not become valid through calculation.
\citep{exec25_rmed_medoutcon,exec25_rmed_choice}

In the inspected one-step survey-weight branch the estimate is a weighted
mean, but the variance expression multiplies the influence quantity by supplied
weights without corresponding normalization. For scores $(1,3)$, changing
weights from $(1,1)$ to $(2,2)$ retains estimate 2 while changing the displayed
variance-of-the-mean expression from 1 to 4. Requiring normalized weights may
reconcile that convention; an adapter accepting arbitrary relative weights
cannot silently assume it. The proportion-mediated option is a log-ratio
functional, distinct from an additive proportion. These observations motivate
qualification tests rather than establish installed-estimator coverage.
\citep{exec25_rmed_medoutcon,exec25_rmed_choice}

The conditional adoption route retains the R learner stack until independent
fixtures establish target, score, contrast, rescaling and uncertainty parity.
Public trials should include weak support, constants, weight rescaling,
incomplete mediator measurement and deliberately invalid dependent sampling.
A port needs a deployment benefit sufficient to maintain these scientific
invariants. \citep{exec25_rmed_choice}

\subsection{regmedint: interactions and conditional effects}

regmedint supplies a more explicit parametric alternative, carrying baseline
evaluation values, mediator and outcome model families, treatment--mediator
interaction and effect modification. Its case-control branch fits the mediator
in controls and states a rare-outcome requirement. The selected delta
calculation constructs separate regression covariance blocks. Evaluation at
mean covariates is not automatically population standardization, and a block
covariance is not automatically appropriate for clustered servicing data.
\citep{exec25_rmed_regmedint}

Consider $M=1+2A+\varepsilon_M$ and
$E(Y\mid A,M)=3A+4M+5AM$, with mean-zero disturbance and the necessary causal
assumptions. PNDE and TNIE are 8 and 18; TNDE and PNIE are 18 and 8; TE is
26. The controlled direct effect at zero is 3, and the coefficient product
$2\times4=8$ gives only one indirect component. Output must retain interaction,
reference treatment and mediator setting. Proportion mediated also needs a
nonzero interpretable total and need not lie between zero and one.
\citep{exec25_rmed_regmedint,exec25_rmed_choice}

Use this package conditionally as a parametric comparator and fixture source.

general risk decomposition. \citep{exec25_rmed_choice}

and numerical contracts visible. \citep{exec25_rmed_tipr,exec25_rmed_choice}

covariance matrix. These are different analyses requiring explicit justification.

dispatch. Unsupported link requests should be rejected rather than reported
as model changes. \citep{exec25_rmed_yimer_paper,exec25_rmed_bayesgmed}

\]

likelihood loses dependence on $p$, but the source expression retains it.

interval behavior and end-to-end costs are needed. For hypothetical USD30,000

alone cannot select a denominator or establish bank value. \citep{exec25_rmed_choice}
~~~

~~~text
\label{sec:exec25-rmed}

A bank considering a servicing intervention needs to distinguish an improvement
caused by the intervention from an improvement transmitted through a particular
mechanism. Let $A$ denote an offer of restructuring, $M$ subsequent payment
engagement, and $Y$ loss over a fixed horizon. Baseline information $W$ precedes
the offer. A later liquidity assessment $Z$ may be changed by the offer and
affect both engagement and loss. The question therefore requires a declared
intervention on engagement, a target population, an information clock and
assumptions linking the intervention to observed data. R packages supply useful
approaches, but their targets and uncertainty calculations are not interchangeable.
This comparison extends the preceding mediation, medflex, sensemakr and EValue
discussions with CMAverse, medoutcon, regmedint, causalsens, tipr and BayesGmed.
Inspected sources and authored examples support conditional reuse decisions;
they do not establish native qualification. \citep{exec25_rmed_choice}

\subsection{A causal target before a software method}

Write $Y_{a,m}$ for the outcome after setting offer and mediator to $(a,m)$,
and $M_a$ for the mediator under offer $a$. Two complementary natural
decompositions on an additive scale are
\[
 \operatorname{TE}=E(Y_{1,M_1}-Y_{0,M_0})
 =\operatorname{PNDE}+\operatorname{TNIE}
 =\operatorname{TNDE}+\operatorname{PNIE}.
\]
Here $\operatorname{PNDE}=E(Y_{1,M_0}-Y_{0,M_0})$ and
$\operatorname{TNIE}=E(Y_{1,M_1}-Y_{1,M_0})$; the other pair interchanges the
reference treatment. The controlled direct effect $E(Y_{1,m}-Y_{0,m})$ instead
holds engagement at the same specified level. It need not equal a natural
effect, and subtracting it from TE need not yield a natural indirect effect.
The selected BayesGmed primary text develops these distinctions under consistency,
positivity, no unmeasured confounding and a cross-world condition. Randomizing
the offer alone does not supply every mediation assumption; a posterior interval
does not establish them either. \citep{exec25_rmed_yimer_paper}

When offer-induced liquidity confounds engagement and loss, an alternative
draws a new mediator $G_b$ from the distribution of $M_b$ conditional on $W$,
independently of the realized intermediate confounder under the declared
intervention law. Let $\mu(a,z,m,w)=E(Y\mid A=a,Z=z,M=m,W=w)$. The selected
D\'iaz and colleagues paper identifies the corresponding mean as
\[
 \theta(a,b)=\int \mu(a,z,m,w)\,p(z\mid a,w)\,
                  p(m\mid b,w)\,p(w)\,d(z,m,w).
\]
The identifying requirements include the relevant treatment and mediator
exchangeabilities, consistency and conditional support. This intervention
differs from drawing a mediator conditional on the intermediate confounder as
well as baseline information. Changing the conditioning set changes the
pathways assigned to direct and indirect components.
\citep{exec25_rmed_diaz_paper}

Define $\operatorname{IDE}=\theta(1,0)-\theta(0,0)$ and
$\operatorname{IIE}=\theta(1,1)-\theta(1,0)$. Their sum is the total contrast
under the randomized mediator intervention, which need not equal the ordinary
treatment effect. An authored example takes
$P(Z=1\mid A=0)=1/4$, $P(Z=1\mid A=1)=1/2$,
$P(M=1\mid Z)=1/4+Z/2$, and $Y=ZM$. The ordinary treatment effect is $3/16$,
whereas IDE is $3/32$ and IIE is $1/16$, summing to $5/32$. All mediator
probabilities are positive. The difference arises from changing dependence in
the intervention, not estimation error. The product must label the two totals
explicitly. \citep{exec25_rmed_choice}

natural-effect, marginal structural and g-formula approaches. Its interface
restricts methods when post-treatment confounders are supplied and changes
natural-effect labels to randomized analogues. Parameter-function and imputation
estimators have different applicability; the documented logistic and Cox
parameter-function cases require a rare outcome. Its sensitivity interface

single-variable measurement-error scope. These are useful capabilities to

The selected g-formula delegate simulates intermediate confounders from
exposure and baseline covariates, then mediators using those variables and the
simulated intermediate values. In its post-treatment-confounder branch, it
subsequently permutes each mediator column across eligible rows. Outcome
prediction retains the row's baseline and intermediate variables. Global
permutation requires a different justification from a draw conditional on that
row's baseline information; separate column permutations also require
justification when a joint mediator law is intended. \citep{exec25_rmed_cmaverse}

row with the marginal mediator probability $1/2$, yielding $1/4$ in expectation.
~~~

~~~text
\section[Python mediation and sensitivity contracts]{Python mediation and sensitivity: effects, resampling, and the limits of computed bounds}
\label{sec:exec25-pymed}

A bank evaluating a digital servicing channel needs more than a coefficient labelled indirect effect. Let $A$ denote the assigned channel, $M$ a subsequent customer response, $X$ information fixed before assignment, and $Y$ the net outcome over a specified horizon. A response measured after a collection decision cannot silently become a baseline adjustment variable. The proposal therefore treats the observation clock, intervention, population and outcome scale as part of the request. A package comparison is useful only after these quantities have been fixed. The Python ecosystem supplies several different services: regression path summaries, model-based potential-outcome integration, graph-guided orchestration, and partial-identification calculations. They should be compared at the level of their estimands and failure conditions rather than placed behind one interchangeable mediation command.\cite{exec25_pymed_statsmodels,exec25_pymed_pingouin,exec25_pymed_dowhy,exec25_pymed_process,exec25_pymed_choice}

\subsection{An estimand contract before a package choice}
Write $M(a)$ for the mediator under assignment $a$, and $Y(a,m)$ for the outcome under joint interventions. A useful nested mean is
\[
 \theta(a,a')=E\{Y(a,M(a'))\}.
\]
For a binary contrast, $\theta(1,1)-\theta(1,0)$ is one natural indirect effect and $\theta(1,0)-\theta(0,0)$ its complementary direct effect. Their sum is the total effect, provided these nested quantities are justified. The corresponding definitions with the outcome exposure fixed at zero need not give the same indirect effect when there is interaction. Identification additionally requires a defensible causal model, consistency, overlap, and the relevant treatment--mediator and mediator--outcome exchangeability or stronger cross-world restrictions. Neither a fitted path nor a sensitivity plot certifies those assumptions. The preceding R comparison develops alternative interventional targets; the Python interface must retain that distinction.\cite{exec25_pymed_choice,exec25_pymed_sharp_paper}

For a concrete scale check, suppose $P\{M(0)=1\}=1/4$, $P\{M(1)=1\}=3/4$, and $E\{Y(a,m)\}=3a+4m$. Under an otherwise identified law, either natural indirect effect is $4(3/4-1/4)=2$. A logistic regression of the binary mediator on $A$ instead has slope $\log 9$; multiplying this slope by the outcome coefficient gives $4\log9\simeq8.789$. This is a coefficient product on mixed scales, not the same outcome contrast. Reporting the latter number as the former would change the business quantity before any uncertainty calculation begins. This is an authored population example, not an observed error rate from a fitted package.\cite{exec25_pymed_choice}

\subsection{Potential-outcome simulation versus regression paths}
The inspected statsmodels mediation implementation is a useful reference for explicit counterfactual construction. Its formula route rebuilds the design matrix after exposure and mediator interventions; this matters for interaction terms. Its matrix route directly replaces columns and cannot be assumed to rebuild derived interaction columns. It simulates mediator draws, uses the same mediator realization for both outcome-exposure levels within a given mediator assignment, and computes direct and indirect differences. The selected loops fix assignments to zero and one, so another treatment contrast requires an explicit transformation or an extended implementation.\cite{exec25_pymed_statsmodels}

Uncertainty requires a separate review. The parametric route draws mediator and outcome parameters in separate calls. The bootstrap route calls a fitting helper twice; each call generates its own row indices. These operations do not preserve arbitrary cross-equation dependence merely because both equations originated in one customer table. An exact toy calculation makes the distinction visible. Draw two values with replacement from $\{-1,1\}$, and let $Z^*$ be their mean. Its distribution is $(-1,0,1)$ with probabilities $(1/4,1/2,1/4)$. If two fitted components share this perturbation, $E[(Z^*)^2]=1/2$ and $\operatorname{Var}(2Z^*)=2$. Independently drawing the components gives product expectation zero and sum variance one. This does not prove that every statsmodels mediation interval is invalid: joint covariance can vanish under additional model conditions. It proves that a shared-resample contract and a separate-resample contract need a stated justification. Customer, household and calendar dependence introduce further choices that an ordinary row bootstrap does not settle.\cite{exec25_pymed_statsmodels,exec25_pymed_choice}

Two smaller boundaries also deserve tests before exposure through a product interface. Initial method validation accepts a prefix beginning with \texttt{para}, whereas the iteration dispatch selects parameter simulation only for the exact string \texttt{parametric}; accepting a prefix can consequently change the computational route. The sign-tail expression for reported significance counts strict positive and strict negative draws. With four exact zeros its arithmetic returns zero, which is not evidence against the null. The proportion-mediated calculation also divides by the total effect without defining an economic interpretation when that total is zero or changes sign. We would wrap a narrowly qualified version with exact enumerations, typed zero-total results and an explicit sampling contract, rather than infer qualification from the API name.\cite{exec25_pymed_statsmodels,exec25_pymed_choice}

Pingouin exposes a compact parallel-mediation workflow. The inspected implementation drops incomplete rows, detects binary mediators and uses logistic mediator regressions for them, fits a linear outcome model, and returns products of the mediator and outcome coefficients. The source therefore directly motivates the mixed-scale example above. Its bootstrap applies one row-index array to the mediator and outcome inputs, preserving the sampled row pairing. Its bias-corrected interval is explicitly not an accelerated BCa interval, and its documentation warns that bootstrap sign tails are not a null-conditioned permutation test. The zero-point-estimate branch returns a significance value of one, unlike the strict-sign expression just discussed. Moreover, the displayed $Y\sim M+X$ path omits treatment while the coefficient used for the indirect product comes from the full treatment-and-mediator outcome model; the product should not be reconstructed by multiplying arbitrary displayed rows.\cite{exec25_pymed_pingouin}

For continuous linear models with appropriately justified assumptions, Pingouin can be a conditional comparator. For binary mediators it should be presented as a regression-path summary unless a separate target derivation is supplied. Complete-case selection changes the analyzed population and requires its own missingness argument. Multiple mediator coefficients do not establish a causal ordering, joint intervention or absence of mediator--outcome confounding. These distinctions justify retaining the package as a candidate while rejecting a universal causal-effect interpretation.\cite{exec25_pymed_pingouin,exec25_pymed_choice}

The selected PyProcessMacro revision extends this regression-path family with moderated and serial constructions, categorical coding and outcome-family choices. Its serial path calculation multiplies coefficients along each ordered path. The bootstrap code fits the equations on the same resampled rows and retains a count of failed fits. It continues until the requested number of successful resamples is obtained, with an explicit failure cap. This is useful instrumentation, but the retained draws are conditional on successful fitting. A later public evaluation must report attempted, failed and accepted draws, separation and rank failures, and the effect of those failures on the reported interval. A request that produces enough successful draws has not thereby shown that discarded draws are ignorable. We would adopt the failure-accounting and shared-resample interface ideas, compare serial linear paths under an exact graph, and require a separate causal derivation for nonlinear coefficient products.\cite{exec25_pymed_process,exec25_pymed_choice}

\subsection{Graph orchestration does not make all two-stage estimates equivalent}
~~~
