~~~text
\section[C++ mediation and numerical contracts]{C++ mediation: preserve the intervention through numerical and data interfaces}
\label{sec:exec25-cmed}

A bank evaluating a channel-to-engagement-to-repayment mechanism needs more
than a fast matrix library. Let $A$ denote a channel assignment, $M$ subsequent
engagement and $Y$ repayment value. Under an explicitly justified linear
structural model $M=aA+U_M$ and $Y=cA+bM+U_Y$, with the required assignment
and mediator--outcome restrictions, a unit treatment contrast has indirect
effect $ab$, direct effect $c$ and total effect $c+ab$. The illustrative values
$(a,b,c)=(2,4,3)$ give $8$, $3$ and $11$. These are project derivations in a
declared model. A fitted structural-equation model, a differentiable solver or
a posterior sample does not establish the restrictions. The useful C++ question
is which computation can be adopted while preserving this meaning and its
uncertainty, and which apparent reuse would silently change the problem.

Four bounded repository searches and selected primary-source inspection identify
four different component roles: OpenMx's R-facing C++ structural-equation engine,
Stan Math's C++ primitives, bsem's R-to-Stan generated implementation, and gwsem's
genetic-data interface to OpenMx. Forty-seven authentic originals are tied to
complete selected repository trees, revisions no later than 7 October 2026,
retrieval receipts and byte hashes. The search returns additional uninspected
candidates and is not a saturation or absence result. In particular, an R
interface with a C++ backend must not be counted as an independent, fully
qualified C++ mediation system. No downloaded implementation was executed for
this comparison.~\citep{exec25_cmed_choice}

\subsection{OpenMx: joint algebra, row resampling and numerical failure}

OpenMx's RAM representation provides a natural computational home for a linear
mediation model. Writing $x=Bx+\epsilon$, disturbance covariance $S$ and an
observation-selection matrix $F$, its mathematical covariance target is
\[
 \Sigma=F(I-B)^{-1}S(I-B)^{-T}F^T.
\]
This covariance representation can include correlated disturbances; it does not
make a coefficient product causally identified. A proposed adapter should retain
the graph, variable order, error correlations, measurement model, fixed and
shared parameters, and the intervention contrast separately from the numerical
RAM matrices. Natural-effect restrictions and the banking information clock
remain explicit inputs.~\citep{exec25_cmed_openmx}

The inspected path delegate uses a finite polynomial when its nilpotence logic
permits it and an inverse computation otherwise. In the dense inverse branch it
forms a full-pivot LU decomposition and solves against the identity. The nearby
sparse branch checks the factorization status, records an iteration error and
sets its inverse buffer to missing values on failure. This is a difference in
the inspected local guards, not evidence that every dense singular model is
accepted by the whole package. Complete fit-function propagation and native
solver behavior remain to be qualified. A scalar feedback coefficient
$b=1-\varepsilon$ illustrates the underlying numerical problem: the response
$(1-b)^{-1}=\varepsilon^{-1}$ has derivative $\varepsilon^{-2}$ with respect
to $b$. At $\varepsilon=10^{-3}$ these are $1000$ and $1{,}000{,}000$.
Small residuals alone do not bound economically useful effect error near
singularity. At $b=1$ the inverse does not exist; an adapter must return an
explicit failure, not a finite treatment effect.~\citep{exec25_cmed_openmx,exec25_cmed_choice}

The bootstrap implementation offers useful audit structure. Its C++ output
retains each replication's seed, fit, parameter vector and status. The R accessor
selects statuses declared acceptable and warns when fewer than 95 percent pass.
Consequently, uncertainty computed from that accessor is conditional on retained
fits unless the effects of failed fits are separately justified. Report requested,
attempted, failed and retained denominators. The expression evaluator substitutes
the entire retained parameter vector before evaluating an algebra, which is the
appropriate mechanism for preserving within-draw dependence of a product.
For paired illustrative draws $(a,b)=(1,2),(3,6)$, the average product is $10$;
independent recombination of the two marginal sets gives $8$. The difference is
not Monte Carlo noise: it is a changed joint distribution. The displayed
bias-corrected interval uses a normal-quantile bias correction and empirical
type-1 quantiles; its inspected formula has no acceleration term, so it should
not be advertised as BCa.~\citep{exec25_cmed_openmx,exec25_cmed_choice}

Resampling semantics are equally important. The C++ loop draws frequency counts
for each dataset context; it does not by itself synchronize customer identities
across separate data objects. A same-row multivariate record can preserve its
cross-equation measurements, whereas independently resampling linked tables
requires an explicit justification or a different joint sampler. The public R
entry point states its independent-row assumption and rejects detected multilevel
and state-space models unless the user chooses an unsafe override. Such an
override changes execution permission, not the sampling theorem. The selected
C++ loop also contains an unimplemented-parallel marker despite carrying a
parallel flag; this local observation must not become a claim that all OpenMx
parallelism is absent. Reuse should test the exact entry point and report measured
resources.~\citep{exec25_cmed_openmx}

The wrapper checks that a model has been freshly run, while the backend's shown
prior-output compatibility test compares parameter and column counts. These
guards motivate an additional artifact identity over data, graph, parameter
names/order, fit settings, sampling law and seeds before bootstrap continuation.
Equal dimensions do not establish equal scientific requests. Seed replay,
exception restoration of row weights and starts, an empty acceptable-fit set,
ties in interval correction, and dense/sparse singular cases are public
qualification tasks. The source declaration is Apache 2.0; complete distributed
dependencies and any chosen optimizer require their own rights and artifact
review.~\citep{exec25_cmed_openmx}

\subsection{Stan Math: an auditable numerical layer with a narrow contract}

Stan Math is a candidate numerical dependency rather than a mediation estimator.
The inspected arithmetic matrix solve checks square and compatible dimensions
and delegates to LU. The reverse-mode overload uses a Householder QR solve and
a reverse callback. For $AX=B$, a perturbation obeys
$dX=A^{-1}(dB-dA\,X)$; with output adjoint $G$, the corresponding inputs are
$\bar B=A^{-T}G$ and $\bar A=-\bar B X^T$. These derivative identities explain
the callback and also show why an ill-conditioned $A$ affects both the result
and the gradient. Mathematical agreement does not imply bitwise parity between
the arithmetic and differentiated branches.~\citep{exec25_cmed_stanmath}

The positive-definite solve additionally checks symmetry, non-NaN values and
positive definiteness of the factorization. The inspected positive-definite
inverse checks its LDLT status, positivity and positive diagonal factors. Its
opening comment mentions positive/negative definiteness, but the operative
checks require positivity. Select the routine by its executable mathematical
contract. A covariance factor may be positive definite; the nonsymmetric RAM
matrix $I-B$ generally is not. Passing it to an SPD routine for convenience would
change the supported domain.~\citep{exec25_cmed_stanmath}

Conditional adoption should prefer these maintained primitives over an
unnecessary hand port, subject to a pinned compiler, Eigen and Stan versions,
float type, threading and license inventory. Public qualification should cover
zero-sized and incompatible matrices, singular and near-singular systems,
finite values, forward/reverse agreement, residual-based error bounds and
independent directional derivatives. A successful gradient is neither a hidden
confounding sensitivity interval nor a guarantee of global optimization.
The selected BSD-3-Clause text is an initial rights input, not clearance of
every compiled dependency.~\citep{exec25_cmed_stanmath,exec25_cmed_choice}

\subsection{bsem: inspect the translation from named paths to compiled density}

The selected bsem 1.0.0 package exposes factor and structural models through
rstan. Its retained generated C++ identifies Stan 2.21.0; the separately pinned
2026 Stan Math tree is not asserted to be bsem's installed dependency. The
model uses observed measurement entries, Gaussian latent regressions with unit
residual scale, loading priors and separate missing-value variants. These are
substantive modeling choices. Loading signs supplied to the R interface set
initial values; they do not by themselves constrain every posterior draw or
identify a bank's manipulable treatment.~\citep{exec25_cmed_bsem}

A named-path translation deserves an exact test before integration. The inspected
handler constructs dependent-variable indices in the order of the block names,
but constructs parent groups in the order of the path list. For block order
$(A,M,Y)$ and path list $Y\leftarrow M$ followed by $M\leftarrow A$, these
sequences pair as $M\leftarrow M$ and $Y\leftarrow A$. The intended chain with
coefficients $1/2$ and $3/4$ has product $3/8$; the mispaired equations are a
different model. This is an authored trace of the selected indexing expressions,
not a measured native frequency. An adapter must canonicalize both targets and
parents together, reject duplicate or self edges as appropriate, and test every
permutation of equivalent named input.~\citep{exec25_cmed_bsem,exec25_cmed_choice}

Cycles require more than reordering. Consider two simultaneous equations
$z_1=r z_2+e_1$ and $z_2=s z_1+e_2$, with independent standard-normal errors.
The product of the two residual normal densities integrates over $z$ to
$1/|1-rs|$ when $1-rs\ne0$. A normalized simultaneous-equation density therefore
needs the Jacobian multiplier $|1-rs|$ per observation. At $r=s=1/2$ the
residual product integrates to $4/3$ and the missing multiplier is $3/4$.
An acyclic triangular system has determinant one. The selected Stan text writes
the regression density product, so a translator must establish the intended
acyclic model or derive and implement the correct cyclic density; merely
obtaining posterior draws cannot resolve this distinction. No claim is made
that this static case was run through the package.~\citep{exec25_cmed_bsem,exec25_cmed_choice}

Two smaller interface details can materially alter sensitivity analysis. The R
handler forwards the second parsed coefficient-prior parameter, while Stan uses
its square root as the normal or Cauchy scale. An input second value of $4$
therefore gives normal standard deviation $2$, rather than $4$ under a
conventional standard-deviation reading. Also, the selected Stan data declare
coefficient-prior locations nonnegative, even though the coefficient itself is
unrestricted. A proposed negative prior location must be rejected or translated
with an explicit schema change, never silently reinterpreted. These observations
concern this selected model, not Stan's general prior capabilities.~\citep{exec25_cmed_bsem}

For missing data, the R interface records observed and missing positions and
fills a working matrix with row means. The missing-value Stan variant introduces
separate unknown entries and gives them the measurement density; the observed
likelihood iterates the observed index set. The temporary means should not be
described as the final inferential imputation. A later R handler applies conditional chain-sign transformations to extracted
loadings, scores and selected coefficients. Its index mapping must preserve the
structural equations before any joint mediation draw is admitted. No missingness
indicator model in the selected density establishes an arbitrary nonignorable
mechanism. Preserve
the target population and missingness assumptions, and retain chains,
diagnostics and joint draws for any mediation functional. Conditional
equation-level reuse is plausible after fixing translation contracts; direct
admission as a banking mediation engine is deferred. GPL-3, rstan and the
complete compiled dependency chain must be reviewed for the intended
distribution.~\citep{exec25_cmed_bsem,exec25_cmed_choice}

\subsection{gwsem: useful workflow ideas do not justify a domain-mismatched loader}

gwsem combines genetic-file loading with OpenMx models. The selected compute plan
loads a variant, resets starts, runs optimization inside a try/catch plan and
writes checkpoints including covariance and sample-size information. This is a
concrete example of preserving per-request computation rather than reporting
only a final coefficient. Its user documentation also places statistical
identification responsibility on the model author. These ideas can inform a
bank adapter, but genetic marker formats and allele semantics do not become
customer-event semantics by renaming fields.~\citep{exec25_cmed_gwsem}

The inspected BGEN callback gives a particularly useful public fixture. Its
numeric probability branch computes $d=p_1+2p_0$ and replaces an exact zero
with a missing value. The valid probability vector $(0,0,1)$ has dosage zero
under that very formula. For the three deterministic vectors $(0,0,1)$,
$(0,1,0)$ and $(1,0,0)$, mathematical dosages are $0,1,2$ with mean $1$;
retaining only the positive values changes the mean to $1.5$. The explicit
missing-value callback instead throws an unimplemented exception. These are
static branch witnesses. The upstream parser and actual file-format path must
be tested before asserting a native defect or failure rate. A bank port must
keep legitimate zero activity distinct from missing telemetry regardless.
The selected package declares GPL version 3 or later and includes multiple
third-party C/C++ components. Reject direct banking adoption of the domain
loader; consider only a separately justified workflow abstraction with a
complete rights and semantic review.~\citep{exec25_cmed_gwsem,exec25_cmed_choice}

\subsection{A public qualification route with explicit economic meaning}

The practical proposal is a typed adapter over selected components. It receives
the intervention, units, graph and disturbance restrictions, named parameter
mapping, sampling unit and missingness contract. It returns the effect target,
joint draws or covariance, numerical diagnostics, complete attempt counts and
typed refusal. CLI and MCP entry points should serialize the same request and
artifact hashes; neither may infer a causal estimand from a successful fit.
Large draws can remain in a versioned local artifact referenced by hash, while
the response carries bounded diagnostics. Replaying a seed without replaying
the graph, row mapping, solver and sampling law is insufficient.

The first public fixtures should use known linear laws, permuted path names,
correlated disturbances, tied and failed bootstrap fits, independent and
clustered sampling, near-singular matrices, prior-scale changes and zero-versus-
missing records. Then test target-language interfaces, interrupts and recovery,
resource use, and the full cost of all attempted requests. No expensive bank
experiment is needed to expose these translation errors. For a hypothetical
10,000 customers valued at USD10 per outcome unit, the illustrative joint-product
difference of two units changes the proposal value by USD200,000. This
reproducible arithmetic is a motivation for qualification, not observed ROI.
The decision is conditional adoption of appropriate numerical primitives,
conditional OpenMx algebra reuse, deferred bsem admission pending translation
qualification, and rejection of a direct domain-loader port, while preserving
the public numerical and semantic qualification.~\citep{exec25_cmed_choice}
~~~

~~~text
\section[Remaining-language mediation contracts]{MATLAB, Julia and Stata mediation: compare estimands and execution contracts}
\label{sec:exec25-omed}

A bank comparing mediation packages across languages needs the same scientific
request in every environment: an intervention, its contrast, a mediator law,
an outcome scale, a target population and a sampling design. A mediation
package can otherwise conceal a coefficient product, a nested counterfactual
mean, a modified treatment policy or a descriptive path model. This comparison
develops six concrete component choices: CANlab's MATLAB Mediation Toolbox;
the Julia packages Paramed.jl, Mediation.jl and CausalMediation.jl;
CausalTargeted.jl's compatibility interface; and the Stata cmed collection.
Four bounded repository searches and 55 authenticated original files establish
selected source contracts, not ecosystem saturation. The queries return
irrelevant uses of the word mediation, uninspected candidates and unreturned
results. Revisions are pinned before the 7 October 2026 cutoff; source
descriptions are not native performance evidence.~\citep{exec25_omed_choice}

Consider a bank's reminder assignment $A$, account engagement $M$, and repayment
$Y$. In the declared linear system $M=2A+U_M$ and $Y=3A+4M+U_Y$, the additional
assumptions needed for causal mediation yield direct and indirect unit effects
of $3$ and $8$. The contrast $0\rightarrow2$ gives $6$, $16$ and total $22$.
These values make a useful portable oracle: language and numerical routine may
change, but the contrast must be applied exactly once. With nonlinear outcomes,
several mediators or intermediate confounding, the oracle must change to the
specific identified functional. A fitted path diagram cannot provide that
functional by itself.~\citep{exec25_omed_choice}

\subsection{CANlab: distinguish levels, accepted resamples and interval probability}

CANlab's inspected MATLAB path engine includes single-level and multilevel
branches, ordinary and robust regressions, and bootstrap options. Its dispatch
explicitly rejects some combinations, including robust multilevel computation.
The fast ordinary bootstrap path constructs normal-equation inverses for the
mediator and outcome regressions and returns the product of the two relevant
slopes. This is a concrete reusable path calculation, subject to matrix
conditioning and the scientific assumptions attached to a coefficient product.
The main entry point removes missing observations jointly from the current
variables. In a bank panel, that complete-case set can be a different population
from all eligible customers. Selection and information timing must therefore
be represented outside the regression call.~\citep{exec25_omed_canlab}

The resampling helper draws rows, deletes resamples with no predictor variation,
and replaces them until its iteration cap is reached. It also reseeds the random
generator from the clock. These are substantive reproducibility and sampling
choices. With two predictor values $(0,1)$, four equally likely size-two bootstrap
samples contain two constant samples. Removing them leaves only $(0,1)$ and
$(1,0)$. The sample-mean variance is $1/8$ under ordinary resampling but zero
conditional on acceptance. This exact example is not a claim about a measured
mediation coverage rate; it demonstrates why the replacement rule and every
rejected attempt belong in the reported experiment. A wrapper should capture
the actual index matrix or change seed handling through a reviewed port.
\citep{exec25_omed_canlab,exec25_omed_choice}

The confidence-interval call also needs branch-specific qualification. The

variation, extreme bias correction, tied resamples and the diagonal selection

Paramed.jl describes itself as a port of a Stata parametric-mediation program.

constructs delta-method uncertainty using a block-diagonal combination of
model covariance matrices. Even after software repairs, that combination needs
a justification for the relevant joint estimation law. Evaluating covariates
at a mean is also not automatically the same as averaging a nonlinear effect
over the bank's customer population.~\citep{exec25_omed_paramed}

An exact covariance permutation illustrates an immediate translation concern.
The helper assigns its output array to the input array and then overwrites
entries while moving the intercept to the last position. For the positive
definite matrix
\[
 V=\begin{pmatrix}4&1&2\\1&9&3\\2&3&16\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 PVP^T=\begin{pmatrix}9&3&1\\3&16&2\\1&2&4\end{pmatrix},
\]
the intended permutation is nonsingular, with determinant $500$. Tracing the
selected in-place assignments instead gives
\[
 \widetilde V=\begin{pmatrix}9&3&9\\3&16&3\\9&3&9\end{pmatrix},
\]
which is singular. This is an authored finite-array witness, not a native Julia
test. A correct port should use an explicit index permutation or a separate
copy and check symmetry, positive definiteness and the variance of the same
linear combination before and after reordering.~\citep{exec25_omed_paramed,exec25_omed_choice}

The selected two-sided normal-tail calculation also uses the signed statistic
without its absolute value. At $z=-1$, $2\{1-\Phi(z)\}$ is approximately

the typed logfile default, older Julia/DataFrames syntax and transitive imports
still require an installed-environment review. The MIT source license supports
consideration of a repair or equation-level port; it does not establish modern
runtime compatibility or validity of every analytic approximation. Direct
admission is deferred.~\citep{exec25_omed_paramed,exec25_omed_choice}

perturbing their parameters before simulating potential outcomes. Its selected
bootstrap perturber creates a sampled index vector but refits with the original
index vector. For a deterministic fit, that branch therefore does not create
parameter resampling variation. With observations $(0,2)$, ordinary bootstrap
means are $0,1,1,2$, whose variance is $1/2$; refitting the unchanged observations
always gives mean one. The subsequent outcome simulator can still generate
variation, so it would be wrong to claim that every returned interval has zero
width. The issue is that one source of uncertainty is absent while another
remains.~\citep{exec25_omed_mediationjl,exec25_omed_choice}

The same implementation has distinct asymptotic parameter draws, predictive
simulation for normal, binomial and Poisson families, and substitutions of
observed outcomes for some simulated entries. A proposed adapter must state
whether its interval concerns a sample average, a population effect or a
predictive quantity, preserve the treatment contrast and justify cross-model
dependence. Repairing the unused index is necessary but insufficient. No
license-named file was found in the selected complete tree; distribution rights
remain unresolved.~\citep{exec25_omed_mediationjl,exec25_omed_choice}

\subsection{CausalMediation and CausalTargeted: typed effects need matching laws}

CausalMediation.jl provides useful architectural ideas: explicit effect families,
mediator--outcome confounder fields, refusal of natural effects with declared
intermediate confounders, and optional relation-kind checks for diagram edges.
Its identification bridge requires relation kinds when a supplied certificate
has a semantic fingerprint, while a call without relation kinds is otherwise
allowed by the inspected helper. These are declaration checks, not evidence
that an imported graph or certificate is scientifically true. The CausalTargeted
mediation interface delegates through an extension to CausalMediation and errors
when it is unavailable. Counting the facade as a second independently verified
estimator would exaggerate coverage.~\citep{exec25_omed_causalmediation,exec25_omed_targeted}

The nested outcome helper exposes the mediator law more clearly than a package
description. It fits separate mediator regressions and simulates independent
Gaussian residuals for the selected continuous-mediator path. With no
intermediate confounder and at most one requested Monte Carlo draw, it instead
substitutes mediator means. Consider the exact structural example
$Y=A M^2$, where $M$ is standard normal and unaffected by $A$. The direct unit
contrast is $E[M^2]=1$, but substitution of $E[M]=0$ gives zero. Similarly, with
$Y=A M_1M_2$, zero mediator means, unit variances and covariance $1/2$, the
contrast is $1/2$; independent Gaussian draws remove it. These examples identify
the restrictions needed for the inspected computation, rather than estimating
its average error across unspecified applications.~\citep{exec25_omed_causalmediation,exec25_omed_choice}

The source computes a mediator density ratio as a product of coordinate-wise
Gaussian ratios, each clamped between $1/5$ and $5$. The product is therefore
bounded by $5^p$ for $p$ mediators, not by five. For three mediators its upper
bound is $125$; multiplication by the selected exposure-weight cap of ten
permits a factor of $1250$. Diagnostics must report the joint weight
distribution and effective sample size, not merely a per-coordinate threshold.
The unweighted summary uses sample standard deviations divided by $\sqrt n$;
this formula does not automatically justify customer clustering or shared
calendar dependence.~\citep{exec25_omed_causalmediation,exec25_omed_choice}

The implementation also distinguishes binary-treatment and continuous
modified-treatment-policy calculations. In the continuous branch it omits
the mediator-residual term from the displayed influence-function helper and
uses the plugin plus outcome-residual contributions. That source choice requires
a separate derivation for the exact policy and nuisance law. References in code
comments are discovery leads; they cannot establish the omitted term is
unnecessary without inspected primary technical text. The selected natural
effect helper delegates to the interventional helper with an empty confounder
list, so equality requires the stated compatibility assumptions. Preserve the
separate categorical-treatment implementation rather than attributing every
continuous-path restriction to the whole package.~\citep{exec25_omed_causalmediation}

The conditional reuse route is to retain the typed request and refusal design,
then qualify each effect-family and treatment-support combination independently.
Public fixtures should test mean substitution, mediator correlation, intermediate
confounding, weight truncation, influence-function centering and numerical
integration error. Selected MIT declarations are useful rights inputs; the
complete CausalDynamics, learner, solver and artifact chain remains to be
examined. Porting an interface without its identification and uncertainty
contract is not a scientific integration.~\citep{exec25_omed_causalmediation,exec25_omed_targeted,exec25_omed_choice}

\subsection{Stata cmed: inspect the chosen estimator beneath the common command}

The Stata cmed collection exposes linear-model, weighting, imputation,
multiply-robust and debiased-learning routes. Its linear wrapper delegates to
Stata bootstrap or an optional parallel bootstrap, with a survey branch. The
inspected linear calculation multiplies the treatment difference once when
forming direct, indirect and total effects, and supports treatment--mediator
interaction terms. It reproduces the symbolic $0\rightarrow2$ oracle of
direct six, indirect sixteen and total twenty-two under the specified linear
model; no Stata run is claimed.~\citep{exec25_omed_cmedstata,exec25_omed_choice}

The weighting delegate fits treatment probabilities with and without mediators,
forms three stabilized weighting schemes, optionally clips them at specified
sample percentiles, multiplies normalized sampling weights, and estimates three
weighted outcome means. The resulting decomposition is explicit, but propensity
positivity, estimated-weight uncertainty and the consequences of clipping must
be evaluated for the same target population. The displayed percentile censoring
is a weight operation; it is not by itself a model for censored outcomes or
proof of mediator identification.~\citep{exec25_omed_cmedstata}

The debiased-learning wrapper selects among named robust types and forest or
lasso delegates, checks some required external commands and restricts selected
branches to binary treatment and mediator coding. Inspecting this wrapper does
not qualify the uninspected learners, cross-fitting details or every advertised
family. A comparison should retain the exact Stata version, extension versions,
survey/cluster settings, estimation sample and all failed bootstrap replications.
The selected complete tree has no license-named file; source availability is not
automatic permission to redistribute it, and Stata runtime entitlement remains
separate. Conditional equation-level comparison is useful now; direct product
integration awaits those explicit scientific and rights gates.~\citep{exec25_omed_cmedstata,exec25_omed_choice}

\subsection{A common public contract across languages}

For the proposed CLI and MCP interface, effect family, contrast, mediator joint
law, missingness, units and sampling clusters should be typed request fields.
The output should bind the exact package revision and environment, return all
failure and resampling counts, expose numerical and scientific refusal, and
reference large draw artifacts by identity. An agent translating a business
question may propose this request and the diagram; it must not fill in
unobserved assignment truth or hide an incompatible effect family. The same
public known-law request should be replayed through each admitted adapter.

The public test plan is specific: index-use and covariance-permutation tests;
positive and negative normal-tail statistics; conditional resampling and
confidence-level branches; nonlinear mediator integration and correlated
mediators; treatment contrasts, weights, missingness and clustered inference;
and artifact, license and failure-reporting checks. A hypothetical 10,000-customer
decision worth USD10 per unit loses USD50,000 of stated benefit when a
half-unit mediator-correlation contribution is omitted. This arithmetic explains
the value of cheap public tests before expensive bank trials. It is not measured
ROI. The selected comparisons remain conditional and incomplete, while
~~~

~~~text
\section{d3rlpy: learning a policy without losing its evaluation target}
~~~
After:
~~~text
A repeated servicing decision changes both cash flows and the information
available for later decisions. Choosing software therefore begins with the
policy question: evaluate a fixed rule from logged experience, learn a rule
and evaluate it separately, or plan within a supplied model. A numerical
answer can be accurate for one of these questions and misleading for another.

The chapter first examines learned policies and their evaluation populations,
then R methods for learning and evaluating dynamic rules. The detailed Python
comparisons distinguish sequential scores, one-time offers and hidden-state
planning before bringing those choices together. Java and C++ provide
contrasting learning, inference and planning implementations. The final Julia
studies connect interface semantics to concrete model evaluation and
partial-history weighting. Their worked examples keep policy selection,
information loss, monetary scaling and uncertainty visible throughout.

\section{d3rlpy: learning a policy without losing its evaluation target}
~~~

~~~text
\subsection{A common temporal report preserves different scientific questions}

The comparisons support a sequence of decisions. First define the calendar,
intervention and target response. Then justify the moments, structural
restrictions or state law that supply information about it. Only then can a
numerical path and uncertainty procedure be compared. Dynamic-panel GMM,
structural shock analysis, local projections and conditional forecasting remain
serious alternatives, with different identifying information and failure modes.
A shared report should make those differences visible instead of inferring a
common causal meaning from similar coefficient or forecast arrays.

The funding question can also depend on uncertain customer relationships and
on whether a pilot population represents the intended rollout. The next chapter
extends the information question to relationship graphs, transported policies
and audit design: what additional observations would actually distinguish the
bank's competing decisions?

~~~

~~~text
\subsection{What must be preserved from the audit to the decision}

The chapter's alternatives answer different information problems. Joint audits
can distinguish relationship laws that separate-edge labels cannot. Coordinated
actions can sometimes avoid an unresolved graph moment. Population adjustment
uses justified invariance and support; imputation uses an observation and
analysis model; historical retrieval uses identity and availability rules.
Neither a completed table nor a precise conditional calculation establishes
all of those premises.

A defensible recommendation therefore retains the missing information and its
monetary consequence. It may call for an additional joint audit, a different
allocation, a restricted target population, sensitivity analysis or refusal.
The software choices matter because their score, covariance, mask, clock and
failure behavior can preserve or change that recommendation. The next chapter
examines hidden-state and Bayesian computations as further conditional tools,
with their assumptions carried into the comparison.

~~~

docs/writing-repair/2026-10-29/src/ae88652272512440.tex

Before:
~~~text
\section[R transport and missingness contracts]{R transport and missingness: preserve the population, the missingness law, and the analysis target}
\label{sec:exec25-rtm}

A bank moving a successful servicing experiment to a different customer population faces two related but distinct questions. Which customers should the experimental effect describe, and what can be learned when outcomes or adjustment variables are unavailable? A transport estimator changes the population over which an identified response is averaged. An imputation model supplies a distribution for unobserved values under declared restrictions. Neither operation automatically supplies the assumptions needed by the other. This distinction governs the proposed R interface and its comparison with generalize, transportr, causaltransportr, mice, smcfcs, and causalOT. The inspected releases are pinned before the client cutoff, with precise identities and primary implementation anchors. The comparisons concern those selected implementations, not every release. No downloaded package was executed.~\citep{exec25_rtm_generalize,exec25_rtm_transportr,exec25_rtm_causaltransportr,exec25_rtm_mice,exec25_rtm_smcfcs,exec25_rtm_causalOT}

\subsection{The population contract precedes the estimator}

Let $S=1$ identify the source trial and $S=0$ the target sample, $A$ be a binary treatment, $X$ the pre-treatment covariates, and $Y$ the outcome in declared units. Write $\rho(x)=P(S=1\mid X=x)$ and $e(x)=P(A=1\mid X=x,S=1)$. Under consistency, source treatment exchangeability, overlap, and equality of the relevant conditional potential-outcome means across populations, the target contrast is
\[
 \tau_0=E\{m_1(X)-m_0(X)\mid S=0\},\qquad
 m_a(x)=E(Y\mid A=a,X=x,S=1).
\]
These are restrictions on the causal and sampling problem, not consequences of fitting a selection classifier. A corresponding augmented population functional is
\begin{align*}
 \tau_0=\frac{1}{P(S=0)}E\bigg[&(1-S)\{m_1(X)-m_0(X)\}\\
 &+S\frac{1-\rho(X)}{\rho(X)}
 \left\{\frac{A}{e(X)}(Y-m_1(X))
       -\frac{1-A}{1-e(X)}(Y-m_0(X))\right\}\bigg].
\end{align*}
With the true selection and treatment probabilities, conditioning on $X,S=1$ reduces the residual term to the difference between the true and working response contrasts, multiplied by the target covariate density. It therefore repairs a misspecified response model in this population calculation. With the correct response model, that residual has conditional expectation zero. These algebraic statements do not establish finite-sample coverage after nuisance fitting, cluster sampling, or clipping. The authored finite-law reference checks the identity separately from those extensions.~\citep{exec25_rtm_choice}

The generalize weighting delegate distinguishes disjoint source and target samples, using $(1-\rho)/\rho$, from a nested-population mode using $1/\rho$. It removes rows missing selection covariates, normalizes target survey weights by their target mean, and optionally caps source weights at an empirical percentile. Its random-forest path expands survey rows using rounded-up counts and fixes a sampling-size argument at 454. An adapter must record the retained population, sampling interpretation, and delegate arguments rather than treat all settings as equivalent weighting.~\citep{exec25_rtm_generalize}

The package also illustrates why an output named TATE is insufficient to identify its scale. The inspected weighting routine uses a Gaussian model when the outcome has more than two observed values, but uses a quasibinomial fit and exponentiates its treatment coefficient when there are exactly two. The latter quantity is an odds ratio in the applicable binary-logit model, not a risk difference. For risks $0.1$ and $0.2$, the difference is $0.1$, while the odds ratio is $9/4$. Multiplying the latter by customer counts and a per-event value would be dimensionally wrong. The result envelope must carry the estimand, coding, link, contrast, and scale separately, and reject ambiguous two-valued numeric outcomes.~\citep{exec25_rtm_generalize,exec25_rtm_choice}

Population trimming is equally consequential. generalize forces its trimming option in the selected TMLE dispatch. Its helper retains factor levels and numerical coordinate ranges represented in the trial. This does not establish joint support: source points $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$ admit target point $(0,1)$ under both marginal ranges even though the joint point has no source support. Conversely, excluding customers changes the target to its retained subset. Both populations and the excluded mass must be reported; a smaller interval after restriction is not improved evidence for every original customer.~\citep{exec25_rtm_generalize,exec25_rtm_choice}

\subsection{Read the score and its complete delegate chain}

transportr separates a task, nuisance fits, cross-fitting, and an influence-function object. Its standard score uses source inverse odds and an average response difference over target observations. The task exposes population roles, observation indicators, and cluster identifiers. Nevertheless, its default one-fold setting uses the same observations for training and validation. More folds activate separate fold construction, with a cluster-aware branch when identifiers are supplied. Cluster-aware splitting alone does not derive cluster-aware uncertainty. The selected influence routine hands row contributions to the external ife package without a cluster identifier in that call; the complete uncertainty delegate remains a qualification requirement. The documented sampling-weight argument is currently unused.~\citep{exec25_rtm_transportr}

The standard score also needs a bounded missing-outcome contract. Its outcome regression is trained on observed source rows, whereas its residual helper replaces every missing product with zero. The displayed standard influence function contains no explicit inverse observation-probability factor. This requires a separately justified missingness argument; an observation-indicator argument does not establish general censoring robustness. Zero times an unavailable target outcome is a structural omission, while a missing source outcome or failed nuisance prediction is a different event. The adapter must distinguish them instead of translating all missing products into successful zeros.~\citep{exec25_rtm_transportr}

A separate iterated-outcome delegate gives another reason to qualify an exact branch. Both its treatment-one and treatment-zero fits select the variable named \texttt{.outcome\_eps1}, although the task also carries \texttt{.outcome\_eps0}. This source-level routing concern requires a public fixture with distinct arm-specific pseudo-outcomes. It is not a measured failure rate and does not invalidate an unrelated standard-ATE branch. Reuse must be specified by task, estimator and delegate.~\citep{exec25_rtm_transportr}

causaltransportr supplies explicit generalize, transport and in-sample targets with augmented weighting, unaugmented weighting, outcome modeling and calibration alternatives. Its nuisance code fits $S$ and constructs source-membership probabilities. In the inspected no-surrogate transport branch, the augmented score uses $S\rho/(1-\rho)$, while the unaugmented branch uses $S(1-\rho)/\rho$. These are different weights under that definition of $\rho$. To expose the consequence without a fitted package, take $P(S=1)=4/5$, independent randomized treatment with probability $1/2$, $Y=A$, and a working outcome regression identically zero. The target effect is one. The expected augmented residual with the displayed reversed odds, divided by $P(S=0)$, is 16; correct inverse odds give one. This is an exact population witness for the selected formula under supplied nuisance values, not a claim that every estimator or native run produces 16.~\citep{exec25_rtm_causaltransportr,exec25_rtm_choice}

The optional normalization needs its own contract. Selected branches divide the residual matrix by the column sums of treatment probabilities, which are not sums of the displayed inverse probability weights. With ten rows and probability $1/2$ throughout, the divisor is five. The native parity fixture must check matrix recycling, dimensions and the intended normalized score. The summary delegate divides sums by a possibly substituted target denominator while calculating standard deviations over the supplied contribution rows. Its uncertainty formula must be derived for the same normalization and target-sample design. Source inspection identifies the questions; it does not supply the variance theorem.~\citep{exec25_rtm_causaltransportr,exec25_rtm_choice}

\subsection{Imputation preserves a model, not missing causal information}

mice offers chained equations, blocks, predictor matrices, passive transformations and multiple-imputation analysis. Its selected sampler forms fitting rows from complete cases, observed outcomes, and the complement of the ignore indicator. Its documentation states that some multivariate delegates do not honor ignore and can require a complete predictor space incompatible with arbitrary where masks. A training/test boundary must therefore be verified for the chosen imputer. A global flag cannot certify that validation outcomes have been withheld from every delegate. Its monotone one-iteration shortcut also edits the predictor matrix without checking that the data actually have the assumed pattern.~\citep{exec25_rtm_mice}

Predictive mean matching returns observed donor values. That can preserve support and avoid implausible draws, but it cannot generate an unobserved value outside donor support: with donors zero and one, a missing value of two cannot be produced by that rule. This is a limitation of the mechanism, not a claim that extrapolation is always desirable. The product should expose donor count, exclusions, matching rule and missingness sensitivity, rather than describe every filled table as recovered truth.~\citep{exec25_rtm_mice,exec25_rtm_choice}

The selected MNAR normal imputer makes this boundary explicit by adding a user-specified unidentifiable-model term to a normal draw. Those sensitivity coefficients are supplied restrictions, not quantities learned from unobserved outcomes. In a simple mean calculation with missing fraction $0.3$, changing the missing-group mean by an elicited $\delta=2$ changes the overall mean by $0.6$. The output should be a sensitivity curve indexed by declared coefficients and their interpretation. Its spread is not automatically a confidence interval for an identified effect. A chosen coefficient cannot certify the bank's reporting or assignment mechanism.~\citep{exec25_rtm_mice,exec25_rtm_choice}

This distinction survives pooling. mice explicitly warns against pooling completed datasets before fitting the scientific model. It combines parameter estimates and variances, preferring a robust standard-error field when supplied by the model's tidy method. For estimates $(0,2,4)$ with within-imputation variances all one, the between-imputation variance is four. Its missing-data rule gives total variance $1+(1+1/3)4=19/3$, whereas its partially synthetic-data rule gives $1+4/3=7/3$. Neither validates an incompatible imputation model, a misspecified causal target, or an unsupported complete-data variance. The interface must preserve pooling rule, degrees of freedom, parameter identity, and covariance requirements. Scholarly references in package comments are not newly cited here without genuine local originals.~\citep{exec25_rtm_mice,exec25_rtm_choice}

smcfcs addresses compatibility with a declared substantive model. Its discrete covariate update multiplies covariate-model probabilities by the substantive outcome likelihood and normalizes the products. With prior $P(X=1)=1/2$, $P(Y=1\mid X=1)=0.8$, and $P(Y=1\mid X=0)=0.2$, an observed $Y=1$ changes the compatible imputation probability to $0.8$. Drawing from the marginal probability $1/2$ would discard that information. Passive transformations are updated within the procedure, so interactions and nonlinear terms must remain consistent through the calculations. Compatibility with a chosen model still does not establish its scientific truth.~\citep{exec25_rtm_smcfcs,exec25_rtm_choice}

For continuous proposals the inspected implementation first makes up to 24 vectorized rejection attempts, then uses a finite per-subject batch. If every candidate is rejected, it increments a failure counter; the previously stored value remains, and the routine later warns while returning imputed datasets. Under an illustrative constant acceptance probability $0.1$ and batch limit two, rejecting all 26 proposals has probability $0.9^{26}$. This is not an observed package rate or a universal rejection law. It shows why suppressing warnings erases a scientific failure condition. The wrapper must retain warnings, affected records, variables, iterations and limits, and refuse clean completion until a qualified policy handles unresolved draws. Increasing the limit is a possible computational remedy, not a proof of compatibility or convergence.~\citep{exec25_rtm_smcfcs,exec25_rtm_choice}

\subsection{Optimal transport and adoption decisions}

causalOT uses optimal-transport methods to construct causal weights; this mathematical transport does not automatically transport experimental effects to a new population. The selected API distinguishes ATT, ATC and ATE, carries initial sample weights, and forms weighted contrasts with optional outcome-model augmentation. Its numeric effective-sample-size method evaluates $1/\sum_i w_i^2$ under a documented sum-to-one convention. Raw weights $(1,3)$ therefore give $0.1$, while normalized weights $(1/4,3/4)$ give $1.6$. Effective sample size must carry its normalization convention and cannot certify joint support or valid effect uncertainty.~\citep{exec25_rtm_causalOT,exec25_rtm_choice}

Reuse decisions are conditional and specific. generalize is a candidate for population weighting and diagnostics after target, scale and trimming qualification. transportr offers task and nuisance boundaries but needs branch-specific observation, routing and uncertainty qualification. Direct admission of the selected causaltransportr score is deferred pending correction or a justified interpretation of its odds and normalization, followed by public parity tests. mice is a candidate imputation and pooling engine under a per-method contract; smcfcs is a candidate where its substantive-model and rejection-failure conditions match the request. causalOT is a candidate weighting component, not a substitute for a transportability argument. A port must reproduce scientific decisions and failure states as well as successful arithmetic; direct adoption must retain versioned runtime behavior.~\citep{exec25_rtm_choice}

Source declarations distinguish MIT for generalize and causaltransportr, GPL version three or later for transportr, GPL version two or later for mice, and the selected GPL version-three declarations for smcfcs and causalOT. These do not settle complete dependency, native-library, service or redistribution rights. Pinned bundles retain identity, hashes, repository blob checks and inspected anchors. Four bounded discovery queries preserve returned candidates and omissions; no exhaustive ecosystem or saturation claim follows. Papers mentioned by packages remain discovery leads until genuine originals and technical anchors are available.~\citep{exec25_rtm_generalize,exec25_rtm_transportr,exec25_rtm_causaltransportr,exec25_rtm_mice,exec25_rtm_smcfcs,exec25_rtm_causalOT,exec25_rtm_choice}

Public qualification can precede expensive bank experiments. Fixtures should freeze selection law, intervention, population weights, outcome scale, nuisance values, joint support, imputation mask and sampling unit; compare exact scores before fitting learners; then test fitted nuisance functions, dependence, failure propagation and costs separately. CLI and MCP requests should serialize these fields and return typed refusals for unsupported combinations. In the hypothetical odds witness, a discrepancy of 15 outcome units across 10,000 customers valued at USD10 per unit changes the arithmetic by USD1.5 million. This motivates prototype tests, not a measured loss or ROI claim. The immediate route is concrete while authentic bank truth and adoption remain later gates: qualify the population and missingness contract before interpreting a completed dataset as a completed causal argument.~\citep{exec25_rtm_choice}
~~~

~~~text
Let $S=1$ identify the source trial and $S=0$ the target sample, $A$ be a binary treatment, $X$ the pre-treatment covariates, and $Y$ the outcome in declared units. Write $\rho(x)=P(S=1\mid X=x)$ and $e(x)=P(A=1\mid X=x,S=1)$. Under consistency, source treatment exchangeability, overlap, and equality of the relevant conditional potential-outcome means across populations, the target contrast is
\[
 \tau_0=E\{m_1(X)-m_0(X)\mid S=0\},\qquad
 m_a(x)=E(Y\mid A=a,X=x,S=1).
\]
These are restrictions on the causal and sampling problem, not consequences of fitting a selection classifier. A corresponding augmented population functional is
\begin{align*}
 \tau_0=\frac{1}{P(S=0)}E\bigg[&(1-S)\{m_1(X)-m_0(X)\}\\
 &+S\frac{1-\rho(X)}{\rho(X)}
 \left\{\frac{A}{e(X)}(Y-m_1(X))
       -\frac{1-A}{1-e(X)}(Y-m_0(X))\right\}\bigg].
\end{align*}
With the true selection and treatment probabilities, conditioning on $X,S=1$ reduces the residual term to the difference between the true and working response contrasts, multiplied by the target covariate density. It therefore repairs a misspecified response model in this population calculation. With the correct response model, that residual has conditional expectation zero. These algebraic statements do not establish finite-sample coverage after nuisance fitting, cluster sampling, or clipping. The authored finite-law reference checks the identity separately from those extensions.~\citep{exec25_rtm_choice}

The generalize weighting delegate distinguishes disjoint source and target samples, using $(1-\rho)/\rho$, from a nested-population mode using $1/\rho$. It removes rows missing selection covariates, normalizes target survey weights by their target mean, and optionally caps source weights at an empirical percentile. Its random-forest path expands survey rows using rounded-up counts and fixes a sampling-size argument at 454. An adapter must record the retained population, sampling interpretation, and delegate arguments rather than treat all settings as equivalent weighting.~\citep{exec25_rtm_generalize}

The package also illustrates why an output named TATE is insufficient to identify its scale. The inspected weighting routine uses a Gaussian model when the outcome has more than two observed values, but uses a quasibinomial fit and exponentiates its treatment coefficient when there are exactly two. The latter quantity is an odds ratio in the applicable binary-logit model, not a risk difference. For risks $0.1$ and $0.2$, the difference is $0.1$, while the odds ratio is $9/4$. \section[Python transport and missingness contracts]{Python transport and missingness: defaults, uncertainty, and the meaning of completion}
~~~
~~~text
\label{sec:exec25-ptm}

A bank selecting a Python workflow for a partially observed target population must choose more than an estimator name. It must preserve the population, treatment contrast, outcome scale, observation mechanism, and uncertainty target through selection weighting, prediction, imputation and discovery. The selected primary implementations are zEpid, causallib, miceforest, statsmodels and causal-learn, pinned at or before the client cutoff. They perform different scientific jobs. A shared Python runtime makes composition possible, but does not establish that their scientific contracts compose. The following comparison uses authenticated source and exact authored laws; no downloaded package was executed.~\citep{exec25_ptm_zepid,exec25_ptm_causallib,exec25_ptm_miceforest,exec25_ptm_statsmodels,exec25_ptm_causallearn}

\subsection{Transport requires the right score, not just the right odds}

zEpid explicitly separates generalizability, where the trial belongs to the target population, from transportability to a disjoint target. Its IPSW class fits selection models and uses inverse probabilities or inverse odds as appropriate. The selected fit computes separately normalized weighted means in the two treatment groups and reports a difference and ratio. A constant stabilization factor cancels in such an arm-specific weighted mean. Its documentation directs uncertainty estimation to a nonparametric bootstrap, and the selected source contains a placeholder for a missingness model. The adapter must therefore specify who is resampled, which models are refitted, and whether missing outcomes are supported by a separate qualified mechanism. The presence of sampling weights is not a proof of censoring adjustment.~\citep{exec25_ptm_zepid}

The same package's GTransportFormula fits a source response model and averages counterfactual predictions over either the combined population or only the target sample. This makes a target-population choice visible. Its optional weighting must still be interpreted consistently in source fitting and target averaging. The AIPSW class adds augmentation and explicitly refuses its optional weights argument at construction. That refusal is valuable product behavior: an adapter should preserve it rather than silently drop weights to obtain a numerical answer.~\citep{exec25_ptm_zepid}

Augmentation changes the role of stabilization. Let $S$ mark source membership, $A$ treatment, and write $p=P(S=1)$ and $e=P(A=1\mid S=1)$ in a simple randomized law. With $p=4/5$, $e=1/2$, $Y=A$, and a working response regression set to zero, the target effect is one. The selected AIPSW transport formula divides its residual sum by the target count. Its default sampling stabilization multiplies inverse odds by $p/(1-p)$, while the default treatment stabilization is one in this constant-probability example. Thus the supplied-nuisance population value of that selected residual is $pe/(1-p)=2$. In generalize mode, the corresponding default residual average is $pe=2/5$. With unstabilized sampling and treatment factors, the transport reference is
\[
 \frac{pe}{1-p}\frac{1-p}{p}\frac1e=1.
\]
These are authored population calculations for the displayed branches. They are not outputs from fitted package runs, and a correct outcome model can remove the residual discrepancy in this example. They show why cancellation in a normalized IPW mean cannot be assumed in an augmented residual added to a different averaging term. The proposed qualification compares all combinations of target mode, response misspecification, treatment weighting and stabilization before admitting a claimed robustness property.~\citep{exec25_ptm_zepid,exec25_ptm_choice}

The economic implication is conditional but concrete. In that two-versus-one witness, 10,000 hypothetical customers valued at USD10 per outcome unit produce a USD100,000 discrepancy. This is neither an observed loss nor an ROI estimate. It defines a public prototype test whose cost can be compared with the risk of misinterpreting the result before any expensive bank experiment.~\citep{exec25_ptm_choice}

\subsection{Treatment balancing is a component of a population argument}

causallib supplies reusable treatment weighting, response standardization and doubly robust components. Its selected IPW implementation predicts a probability matrix, clips entries to requested bounds, and takes reciprocals. These are useful implementation boundaries, but treatment assignment and source selection remain distinct variables with different identifying roles. Reusing a treatment-weight class for population transport requires an explicit transformation and target derivation; the API alone does not provide them.~\citep{exec25_ptm_causallib}

The exact shape of a weight matrix matters. In the selected stabilized branch, prevalence is looked up using each row's observed treatment and multiplied into every column of that row. This produces the usual numerator on the observed-treatment diagonal. It is different from a counterfactual matrix whose column $a$ always uses $P(A=a)$. With prevalences $(1/4,3/4)$ and probabilities $(1/2,1/2)$, the selected rows are $(1/2,1/2)$ for an observed control and $(3/2,3/2)$ for an observed treated subject; a column-stabilized reference would have $(1/2,3/2)$ in both rows. The observed diagonal agrees, so this is not a claim that ordinary observed IPW extraction is wrong. It is a warning to specify which entries a downstream consumer interprets.~\citep{exec25_ptm_causallib,exec25_ptm_choice}

Likewise, componentwise clipping need not preserve the probability simplex. Clipping $(0.98,0.01,0.01)$ to $[0.1,0.9]$ gives $(0.9,0.1,0.1)$ with sum $1.1$. Such values can be intentional bounded denominators, but should not automatically be passed as a normalized categorical distribution. The proposed result schema distinguishes original probabilities, bounded denominators, normalized sampling probabilities and final weights. Qualification must retain how many values were clipped, the changed estimand or approximation, and any downstream normalization.~\citep{exec25_ptm_causallib,exec25_ptm_choice}

\subsection{Completed datasets and valid uncertainty are separate deliverables}

miceforest provides model-based chained imputation with several mean-matching choices. The selected implementation can choose observed nearest-neighbor donors, sample categorical values according to model probabilities, or skip mean matching. With zero candidates it uses regression predictions or modal classes. These choices change the conditional imputation law. For a fixed binary prediction $P(Y=1)=1/4$, a stochastic draw has mean $1/4$ and variance $3/16$, whereas modal completion returns zero with zero conditional draw variance. Other randomness from fitted models or initialization can remain; the claim is only about the selected conditional completion step. Faster deterministic completion is not automatically a valid multiple-imputation uncertainty mechanism.~\citep{exec25_ptm_miceforest,exec25_ptm_choice}

The deployment contract is also concrete. Imputing new data requires stored models and candidate values; the selected method refuses when iteration data were not saved. Script-level random-state reproducibility is distinguished from record-level reproducibility, which has additional seed and data conditions. The binary fast path with record seeds calls the global NumPy seed function for each record. A CLI/MCP worker must therefore isolate and restore its random-state boundary if other tasks share the process. This is a source-level interference risk to test, not a measured concurrency failure. The neighbor query also requests all workers, making resource limits part of an execution wrapper's responsibilities.~\citep{exec25_ptm_miceforest}

statsmodels offers a different MICE implementation with parametric perturbation, donor matching and analysis-result pooling. It drops rows where all variables are missing and resets the index. A bank pipeline must preserve a separate identifier and the dropped-row ledger to avoid assigning completed values to the wrong customers. The imputer permits Gaussian parameter draws or bootstrap perturbation and supplies a model contract for predictions and covariance. The selected setter stores the donor-count setting on the common object rather than in a per-variable dictionary, so a later setter can change the donor count used for other variables. This must be made explicit in an adapter instead of promising an unsupported per-variable setting.~\citep{exec25_ptm_statsmodels}

The pooling implementation retains full covariance. With three two-parameter estimates $(0,0)$, $(2,2)$ and $(4,4)$, and an identity within-imputation covariance, the pooled covariance is
\[
 T=\begin{pmatrix}19/3&16/3\\16/3&19/3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The variance of the parameter difference is two. Discarding cross-covariance would instead give $38/3$. This exact example shows why returning only marginal standard errors loses information needed by a banking contrast. The selected code uses the empirical between-imputation covariance and the factor $1+1/m$; valid analysis still depends on the imputation and complete-data models. Small numbers of imputations, inadequate donor support, singular fits and unsupported degrees-of-freedom assumptions require explicit qualification.~\citep{exec25_ptm_statsmodels,exec25_ptm_choice}

\subsection{Missingness-aware discovery has its own assumptions}

causal-learn provides test-wise deletion and a missingness-correction path for conditional-independence testing. The selected missing-value Fisher test chooses complete rows for each tested variable set, inverts their correlation matrix, and uses the multiplier $\sqrt{n_{\rm test}-|Z|-3}$. It explicitly rejects zero overlap and singular inversion, but the displayed path has no preceding positive-degrees-of-freedom guard. At three rows and no conditioning variables the multiplier is zero, yielding a nominal value of one when the correlation calculation remains finite. This is an exact formula boundary requiring a minimum-information refusal policy, not evidence that a three-row dataset establishes independence.~\citep{exec25_ptm_causallearn,exec25_ptm_choice}

The correction routine depends on a previously inferred skeleton and missingness-parent information. It falls back to test-wise deletion when the correction condition or usable predictors are absent. Otherwise it fits linear regressions, shuffles complete predictor rows, and adds retained residual vectors to predicted values to form virtual data. The assumptions needed to transfer those residuals to a new predictor distribution remain substantive. Heteroskedasticity, nonlinear relationships, estimated missingness parents, and the randomness of the virtual sample must be part of the qualification design. A graph learned from such a procedure is not by itself a confidence set for the customer's intervention effect.~\citep{exec25_ptm_causallearn}

One dispatch detail is particularly important for typed interfaces: both accepted correction names, including the G-squared-named option, set the selected correction test to mc\_fisherz. The wrapper must not promise a categorical G-squared correction merely because the supplied name was accepted. It should resolve the actual implementation and refuse an unsupported semantic contract. A bank selecting a Python workflow for a partially observed target population must choose more than an estimator name. It must preserve the population, treatment contrast, outcome scale, observation mechanism, and uncertainty target through selection weighting, prediction, imputation and discovery. The selected primary implementations are zEpid, causallib, miceforest, statsmodels and causal-learn, pinned at or before the client cutoff. They perform different scientific jobs. A shared Python runtime makes composition possible, but does not establish that their scientific contracts compose. The following comparison uses authenticated source and exact authored laws; no downloaded package was executed.~\citep{exec25_ptm_zepid,exec25_ptm_causallib,exec25_ptm_miceforest,exec25_ptm_statsmodels,exec25_ptm_causallearn}
~~~

~~~text
\subsection{Transport requires the right score, not just the right odds}

zEpid explicitly separates generalizability, where the trial belongs to the target population, from transportability to a disjoint target. Its IPSW class fits selection models and uses inverse probabilities or inverse odds as appropriate. The selected fit computes separately normalized weighted means in the two treatment groups and reports a difference and ratio. A constant stabilization factor cancels in such an arm-specific weighted mean. Its documentation directs uncertainty estimation to a nonparametric bootstrap, and the selected source contains a placeholder for a missingness model. The adapter must therefore specify who is resampled, which models are refitted, and whether missing outcomes are supported by a separate qualified mechanism. The presence of sampling weights is not a proof of censoring adjustment.~\citep{exec25_ptm_zepid}

The same package's GTransportFormula fits a source response model and averages counterfactual predictions over either the combined population or only the target sample. This makes a target-population choice visible. Its optional weighting must still be interpreted consistently in source fitting and target averaging. The AIPSW class adds augmentation and explicitly refuses its optional weights argument at construction. That refusal is valuable product behavior: an adapter should preserve it rather than silently drop weights to obtain a numerical answer.~\citep{exec25_ptm_zepid}

Augmentation changes the role of stabilization. Let $S$ mark source membership, $A$ treatment, and write $p=P(S=1)$ and $e=P(A=1\mid S=1)$ in a simple randomized law. With $p=4/5$, $e=1/2$, $Y=A$, and a working response regression set to zero, the target effect is one. The selected AIPSW transport formula divides its residual sum by the target count. Its default sampling stabilization multiplies inverse odds by $p/(1-p)$, while the default treatment stabilization is one in this constant-probability example. Thus the supplied-nuisance population value of that selected residual is $pe/(1-p)=2$. In generalize mode, the corresponding default residual average is $pe=2/5$. With unstabilized sampling and treatment factors, the transport reference is
\[
 \frac{pe}{1-p}\frac{1-p}{p}\frac1e=1.
\]
These are authored population calculations for the displayed branches. They are not outputs from fitted package runs, and a correct outcome model can remove the residual discrepancy in this example. They show why cancellation in a normalized IPW mean cannot be assumed in an augmented residual added to a different averaging term. The proposed qualification compares all combinations of target mode, response misspecification, treatment weighting and stabilization before admitting a claimed robustness property.~\citep{exec25_ptm_zepid,exec25_ptm_choice}

The economic implication is conditional but concrete. In that two-versus-one witness, 10,000 hypothetical customers valued at USD 10 per outcome unit produce a USD 100,000 discrepancy. This is neither an observed loss nor an ROI estimate. It defines a public prototype test whose cost can be compared with the risk of misinterpreting the result before any expensive bank experiment.~\citep{exec25_ptm_choice}

\subsection{Treatment balancing is a component of a population argument}

causallib supplies reusable treatment weighting, response standardization and doubly robust components. Its selected IPW implementation predicts a probability matrix, clips entries to requested bounds, and takes reciprocals. These are useful implementation boundaries, but treatment assignment and source selection remain distinct variables with different identifying roles. Reusing a treatment-weight class for population transport requires an explicit transformation and target derivation; the API alone does not provide them.~\citep{exec25_ptm_causallib}

The exact shape of a weight matrix matters. In the selected stabilized branch, prevalence is looked up using each row's observed treatment and multiplied into every column of that row. This produces the usual numerator on the observed-treatment diagonal. It is different from a counterfactual matrix whose column $a$ always uses $P(A=a)$. With prevalences $(1/4,3/4)$ and probabilities $(1/2,1/2)$, the selected rows are $(1/2,1/2)$ for an observed control and $(3/2,3/2)$ for an observed treated subject; a column-stabilized reference would have $(1/2,3/2)$ in both rows. The observed diagonal agrees, so this is not a claim that ordinary observed IPW extraction is wrong. It is a warning to specify which entries a downstream consumer interprets.~\citep{exec25_ptm_causallib,exec25_ptm_choice}

Likewise, componentwise clipping need not preserve the probability simplex. Clipping $(0.98,0.01,0.01)$ to $[0.1,0.9]$ gives $(0.9,0.1,0.1)$ with sum $1.1$. Such values can be intentional bounded denominators, but should not automatically be passed as a normalized categorical distribution. The proposed result schema distinguishes original probabilities, bounded denominators, normalized sampling probabilities and final weights. Qualification must retain how many values were clipped, the changed estimand or approximation, and any downstream normalization.~\citep{exec25_ptm_causallib,exec25_ptm_choice}

miceforest provides model-based chained imputation with several mean-matching choices. The selected implementation can choose observed nearest-neighbor donors, sample categorical values according to model probabilities, or skip mean matching. With zero candidates it uses regression predictions or modal classes. These choices change the conditional imputation law. For a fixed binary prediction $P(Y=1)=1/4$, a stochastic draw has mean $1/4$ and variance $3/16$, whereas modal completion returns zero with zero conditional draw variance. Other randomness from fitted models or initialization can remain; the claim is only about the selected conditional completion step. Faster deterministic completion is not automatically a valid multiple-imputation uncertainty mechanism.~\citep{exec25_ptm_miceforest,exec25_ptm_choice}

The deployment contract is also concrete. Imputing new data requires stored models and candidate values; the selected method refuses when iteration data were not saved. Script-level random-state reproducibility is distinguished from record-level reproducibility, which has additional seed and data conditions. The binary fast path with record seeds calls the global NumPy seed function for each record. A CLI/MCP worker must therefore isolate and restore its random-state boundary if other tasks share the process. This is a source-level interference risk to test, not a measured concurrency failure. The neighbor query also requests all workers, making resource limits part of an execution wrapper's responsibilities.~\citep{exec25_ptm_miceforest}
~~~
