\section{Commercial missing-data workflows and transfer between bank populations}
\label{exec21:transport-scope}

A bank may obtain a credible intervention estimate in a pilot and still make a
poor decision when it extends the intervention to another branch. Customers may
differ, follow-up outcomes may be missing, and the software used to complete
the records may report uncertainty for a different quantity from the proposed
decision. A useful commercial comparison therefore follows the complete
question: which population receives which action, when is the outcome measured,
why is it unobserved, and which assumptions connect the observed records to the
decision? Imputation, uncertainty combination and population transfer are
separate steps. A feature called ``missing values'' establishes none of those
connections by its name alone.

The selected primary documentation provides concrete comparators. Stata's
\texttt{mi} family manages multiple completed datasets and their analysis;
SAS/STAT's MI and MIANALYZE procedures separate generation and combination;
IBM SPSS Missing Values exposes imputation and output-specific pooling.
The inspected IBM edition is 31.0.2. The SAS HTML identifies version 14.1,
whereas the Stata manuals contain release-19 example-data paths and July 2026
PDF metadata. These identities delimit the comparison; later retrieval does
not authenticate every byte as the edition available at the literature cutoff.
Exact licensed builds, current entitlements and broader commercial coverage
remain unresolved. EViews, Mplus and commercial graphical tools remain leads
requiring matched technical originals for this particular target.
\cite{exec21_transport_stata_mi,exec21_transport_sas_mi_intro,exec21_transport_spss_missing}

\subsection{Missingness assumptions precede record completion}
\label{exec21:transport-missingness}

Let $A$ be a binary action, $X$ covariates recorded before that action, $Y(a)$
the monetary outcome under action $a$, and $R$ an indicator that the outcome is
observed. The record contains $(X,A,R,RY)$, with a separate missingness mask so
that an absent outcome is never mistaken for a zero. Consistency connects an
observed outcome to $Y(A)$; treatment exchangeability and positive treatment
probability are additional causal assumptions. For the particular problem in
which only $Y$ is missing, a conditional mean restriction sufficient for response
adjustment is
\begin{equation}
 E[Y\mid X,A,R=1]=E[Y\mid X,A],\qquad
 P(R=1\mid X,A)>0.
 \label{exec21:transport-mar}
\end{equation}
The stronger familiar MAR restriction makes response independent of the missing
outcome conditional on the observed variables. When covariates are also missing,
the pattern-specific observed information and imputation model must be specified
again; equation~\eqref{exec21:transport-mar} is not a general multivariate recipe.
Administrative censoring, a variable undefined for a customer, and an outcome
lost through nonresponse need distinct observation models.

Stata's substantive manual and the SAS assumptions chapter distinguish MAR
from MCAR and describe ignorability using MAR together with distinct parameters
for the data and missingness models. They also explain why an assumption about
unobserved values cannot be verified by inspecting only the observed values.
The SAS profile adds distributional restrictions for particular regression and
MCMC procedures. These restrictions must accompany a procedure name. A good
fit to observed records, a plausible-looking imputed distribution or rejection
of an MCAR diagnostic does not establish MAR.
\cite{exec21_transport_stata_substantive,exec21_transport_sas_assumptions}

An exact example makes the investment consequence visible. Let a latent response
type $H$ be equally likely to be zero or one, randomize $A$ independently of
$H$, and set $R=H$. All customers have $Y(0)=0$. Responders have $Y(1)=10$.
In one complete-data law, nonresponders have $Y(1)=-10$; in a second they have
$Y(1)=10$. The observable joint distribution of $(A,R,RY)$ is identical in
both laws: each action-response cell has probability $1/4$, and observed treated
outcomes equal 10. Yet the complete-population effects are respectively 0 and
10. At an assumed action cost of USD 4, the margins are USD $-4$ and USD 6.
More imputation draws from one selected model cannot distinguish these worlds.
The project reference enumerates the complete laws and verifies equality of
their observed distributions. It does not assert that either law describes
actual bank records.\cite{exec21_transport_reference}

A transparent sensitivity parameter writes the unobserved treated mean as
$10+\delta$, keeping the control mean zero. The resulting target is
\begin{equation}
 \tau(\delta)=10+\tfrac12\delta,\qquad
 V(\delta)=6+\tfrac12\delta.
 \label{exec21:transport-sensitivity}
\end{equation}
For the illustrative restriction $\delta\in[-20,0]$, value ranges from $-4$
to 6 and changes sign at $\delta=-12$. The interval is supplied as a sensitivity
restriction, not learned from the missing outcomes. The SAS sensitivity chapter
documents a pattern-mixture approach in MI and explicitly says that the
selection-model approach is not supplied by that procedure profile. A result
that changes under a plausible MNAR scenario establishes dependence of the
decision on assumptions; it does not establish which scenario is true. Exact
syntax and later-release capabilities need their own evidence.
\cite{exec21_transport_sas_sensitivity,exec21_transport_reference}

\subsection{What the three documented workflows preserve}
\label{exec21:transport-workflows}

Stata offers four MI storage styles while retaining the original data as
$m=0$ and the completed datasets as $m=1,\ldots,M$. Variables can be regular,
imputed or passive, with passive variables representing algebraic functions
of other variables. The introduction also states that extended missing values
\texttt{.a} through \texttt{.z} persist as hard missing in the documented
profile. An interchange layer that maps every absent value to an ordinary
numeric null could therefore change what the engine is asked to impute.
Maintaining the missingness reason and role is part of the statistical contract.
\cite{exec21_transport_stata_mi}

For chained equations, Stata documents a default burn-in of ten iterations,
ordering from the most to the least observed variable, configurable conditional
models and saved trace summaries. Perfect prediction produces an error unless
an explicit augmentation option is requested. The manual discusses
incompatible conditionals and dependence of results on specification, order
and burn-in. These are useful controls, but a chosen default is not a proof of
convergence or of adequacy for a causal estimand. For example, an imputer that
omits a treatment interaction needed by the analyst can erase the heterogeneity
needed for the branch-transfer decision even if marginal summaries look
reasonable.\cite{exec21_transport_stata_chained,exec21_transport_stata_substantive}

There is a stronger reason to retain the conditional specifications themselves.
Consider binary $U,V$ with proposed conditionals
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 P(U=1\mid V=0)&=P(U=1\mid V=1)=\tfrac12,\\
 P(V=1\mid U=0)&=\tfrac14,\qquad P(V=1\mid U=1)=\tfrac34.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{exec21:transport-conditionals}
\end{equation}
For any positive binary joint distribution, the odds ratio calculated from
either pair of conditionals must agree. Here the first specification requires
odds ratio 1 and the second requires 9, so no such joint distribution exists.
Nevertheless, alternating draws can have stable distributions. In the cell
order $(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)$, a scan updating $U$ then $V$ has stationary
law $(3,1,1,3)/8$; reversing the scan has stationary law $(1,1,1,1)/4$.
Direct multiplication verifies each invariant distribution. Thus an apparently
stable trace does not demonstrate compatibility of the supplied conditionals.
This exact constructed example is a diagnostic design, not an observed failure
of a particular vendor's implementation.\cite{exec21_transport_reference}

SAS supplies a related but separately versioned workflow. Its MI overview
distinguishes sequential methods for monotone patterns from multivariate-normal
MCMC and fully conditional specification for arbitrary patterns. FCS uses
separate conditional models rather than beginning with an explicit common
multivariate model. The completed datasets are analyzed using the relevant
complete-data procedures, and MIANALYZE reads parameter estimates together with
standard errors or covariance matrices. It notes an additional assumption for
multivariate Wald inference and special treatment for quantities such as
correlations and ratios. The proposal therefore needs a typed collection of
estimates and covariance matrices, not just a filled table. The recovered HTML
contains equations as images that are outside this text inspection; the numerical
pooling formulas below are grounded in the readable Stata manual.
\cite{exec21_transport_sas_mi_intro,exec21_transport_sas_mianalyze_intro,exec21_transport_sas_combining}

IBM's manual makes another important distinction. Multiple Imputation accepts
analysis weights in summaries and imputation models, but it does not explicitly
handle strata, clusters or other complex sampling structures. The manual also
says that Complex Samples procedures do not automatically analyze MI datasets
in this profile. Frequency weights and analysis weights have different
semantics; noninteger frequency weights are rounded. Passing a final sampling
weight therefore does not establish a cluster-aware covariance calculation.
Stata documents a survey-prefix analysis route, but that alone also leaves
the imputation model's treatment of the sampling design to be justified.
\cite{exec21_transport_spss_missing,exec21_transport_stata_estimate}

SPSS chooses a monotone method when the pattern permits it and otherwise uses
FCS. Automatic FCS uses ten iterations; the manual provides history output
for convergence assessment. Main effects are the automatic specification,
with optional categorical two-way interactions under selected settings.
Scale variables can use linear regression or predictive mean matching, whose
documented default donor count is five; categorical models use logistic
regression. Constraints can cause redraws, and excluding highly incomplete
variables removes them from both imputation and prediction. Reproducing a run
requires the same seed, case order, variable order and settings. These details
affect the implied procedure and belong in an adapter request.
\cite{exec21_transport_spss_missing}

The output variable \texttt{Imputation\_} distinguishes original data from
the $M$ completed versions, and split-file settings control how those versions
are analyzed. IBM distinguishes naive combination, which supplies a pooled
parameter, from univariate combination, which can also supply standard errors,
effective degrees of freedom, intervals and missing-information diagnostics.
Support is specific to each output; an unsupported procedure returns no pooled
output. An integration must preserve that unavailability rather than attach a
generic confidence interval to every pooled number.
\cite{exec21_transport_spss_missing}

\subsection{Combine uncertainty on the declared estimand scale}
\label{exec21:transport-pooling}

For a fixed scalar estimand $Q$, let $\widehat Q_m$ and $U_m$ be the estimate
and its completed-data variance from imputation $m$. The documented combination
rule is
\begin{align}
 \overline Q&=M^{-1}\sum_{m=1}^M\widehat Q_m,&
 \overline U&=M^{-1}\sum_{m=1}^M U_m,\nonumber\\
 B&=(M-1)^{-1}\sum_{m=1}^M(\widehat Q_m-\overline Q)^2,&
 T&=\overline U+(1+M^{-1})B.
 \label{exec21:transport-poolformula}
\end{align}
The between-imputation term reflects missing-data uncertainty under the
specified imputation model, and $B/M$ reflects using finitely many imputations.
Neither accounts automatically for uncertainty about an unverified MAR or
population-invariance assumption. Valid completed-data inference and suitable
imputation remain premises. For vector parameters the covariance matrices,
including their off-diagonal terms and common coefficient identities, must be
preserved.\cite{exec21_transport_stata_estimate,exec21_transport_stata_substantive}

For the authored values $(\widehat Q_1,\widehat Q_2,\widehat Q_3)=(0,2,4)$
and $U_m=1$, equation~\eqref{exec21:transport-poolformula} gives
$\overline Q=2$, $B=4$ and $T=19/3$. Retaining only the within variance gives
1. Incorrectly treating the three completed-data estimates as independent
replicate measurements would give $\overline U/M=1/3$. Neither is the MI
variance. The documented large-complete-sample degrees-of-freedom approximation
uses $r=(1+M^{-1})B/\overline U$ and
$\nu=(M-1)(1+1/r)^2$, giving $361/128$ here. A small complete-data sample
requires the further adjustment documented by the manual; the arithmetic is
not a universal coverage result.\cite{exec21_transport_stata_estimate,exec21_transport_reference}

The estimand scale also matters. If two log-odds estimates correspond to odds
ratios 1 and 9, exponentiating their average coefficient gives 3, whereas
averaging the odds ratios gives 5. Stata documents coefficient-scale pooling
followed by an optional exponentiated display; it also has explicit requests
for transformed coefficients. A declared transformed estimand needs its own
completed-data uncertainty and suitable pooling justification. Neither 3 nor
5 is a bank's average profit or a marginal treatment effect merely because it
was returned after imputation.\cite{exec21_transport_stata_estimate,exec21_transport_reference}

Failure handling is part of the same argument. Stata normally stops when an
imputation's estimation fails or the estimation sample changes. Its
\texttt{errorok} and \texttt{esampvaryok} options permit different behavior.
An automatic wrapper must expose such choices and retain the failing
imputation and sample identities. Otherwise it can silently pool different
populations or select only successful fits. The appropriate number of
imputations should be chosen using stability and Monte Carlo error diagnostics
for the requested inference; high relative efficiency of a point estimator
does not guarantee stable intervals or decision thresholds.
\cite{exec21_transport_stata_estimate,exec21_transport_sas_mi_intro}

\subsection{Transport needs an explicit population bridge}
\label{exec21:transport-target}

Let $S=1$ denote the source pilot and $S=0$ the target branch, and define
$p_s(x)=P(X=x\mid S=s)$ and
$\tau(x)=E[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x,S=1]$. One sufficient route assumes consistency,
source treatment exchangeability, positive source treatment and response
probabilities, valid response adjustment within source covariates, and equality
of conditional potential-outcome means across $S$. It also requires source
support wherever $p_0(x)>0$. Under these restrictions, iterated expectation gives
\begin{equation}
 \tau_0=\sum_x p_0(x)\tau(x)
       =E\left[\left.\frac{p_0(X)}{p_1(X)}\tau(X)\right|S=1\right].
 \label{exec21:transport-standardize}
\end{equation}
This is a project derivation for a declared finite-covariate regime. Equality of
conditional means is extra scientific information; it is not established by
the existence of a weight column or by the imputation procedure.
\cite{exec21_transport_reference}

For clarity, write $e_a(x)=P(A=a\mid X=x,S=1)$ and
$r_a(x)=P(R=1\mid A=a,X=x,S=1)$. Under the same response restriction and
positivity, each source conditional mean can be written
\begin{equation}
 \mu_a(x)=E\left[\left.
       \frac{\mathbb{1}\{A=a\}RY}{e_a(x)r_a(x)}
       \right|X=x,S=1\right].
 \label{exec21:transport-response}
\end{equation}
Condition first on $A=a$ and $R=1$, cancel the treatment and response
probabilities, then apply the mean restriction and source causal assumptions.
Substitution into equation~\eqref{exec21:transport-standardize} gives a
combined population, treatment and response-weight expression. It is not a
variance estimator: estimated nuisance models, sampling the target covariates,
clustering and any use of MI require a jointly justified inference procedure.
Weights for these different purposes must remain separately named.

Suppose the source proportions of two customer strata are $(4/5,1/5)$ and the
target proportions are $(1/5,4/5)$. Conditional intervention effects are USD
10 and USD $-10$. The pilot's average effect is 6, the target's is $-6$, and
the population weights are $1/4$ and 4. At an assumed cost of USD 2, the pilot
margin is USD 4 and the target margin is USD $-8$. The exact reference also
enumerates randomized treatment and four positive response rates, verifying
that the combined weighting expression recovers the stipulated target.
No software error is needed for the naive deployment decision to reverse:
the wrong population suffices.\cite{exec21_transport_reference}

If the source instead contains only the first stratum, the second effect is
unobserved and no finite reweighting creates its information. With the explicit
restriction that the second effect lies in $[-10,10]$, the target effect is
$2+(4/5)\tau(1)\in[-6,10]$, giving margin $[-8,8]$ at cost 2. Without such
a justified bound, even that interval cannot be asserted. An adapter should
report the support defect and any defensible identified set. Silently trimming
the second stratum changes the target population; silently predicting into it
adds extrapolation assumptions.\cite{exec21_transport_reference}

\subsection{Competitive position and a public qualification route}
\label{exec21:transport-integration}

The documented commercial systems already provide substantive imputation,
analysis and diagnostic workflows. The proposal has not demonstrated a native
replacement or superior estimation performance. Its proposed contribution is
to preserve the causal question and its restrictions across those workflows:
source and target populations, observation clocks, missingness reasons,
imputation identity, covariance semantics and explicit refusal. Licensed
isolated execution is a candidate integration route; public manuals do not
grant redistribution rights for the engines. EViews, Mplus and graphical-tool
profiles cannot be ranked without the missing originals, and prices remain
unknown.\cite{exec21_transport_stata_estimate,exec21_transport_sas_mianalyze_intro,exec21_transport_spss_missing}

A useful first prototype would compare a selected licensed procedure and an
already reviewed open implementation on the same generated population,
missingness law and estimand. Complete-record analysis, complete-case analysis,
single imputation, proper multiple imputation and an explicitly specified
response-weight procedure supply substantive alternatives. Fix the causal
target, sample law, interaction structure, number of imputations, diagnostic
and refusal rules before evaluation. Include MAR and MNAR cases, complete and
missing source support, compatible and incompatible imputation models, cluster
sampling, changing coefficient sets and unsuccessful fits. Report bias,
coverage under the claimed regime, interval width, unavailable requests,
simulation error and full workflow cost. A sensitivity grid evaluates
robustness; it is not a device for choosing whichever assumption makes a
preferred intervention profitable.

The library, CLI and MCP interfaces should carry the same request and result
meaning. Original and imputed data need stable unit and imputation identifiers,
measurement types, category references, passive transformations and sampling
design. Results need per-imputation estimates and covariance, pooled scale and
degrees of freedom, convergence diagnostics, population support and retained
failures. An assistant can help locate technical passages, propose models and
explain sensitivity; it cannot infer the unobserved outcomes or authorize a
scientific assumption from fluent text. These public comparisons can establish
whether the proposed integration merits a more expensive bank experiment.


\subsection{What must be preserved from the audit to the decision}

The chapter's alternatives answer different information problems. Joint audits
can distinguish relationship laws that separate-edge labels cannot. Coordinated
actions can sometimes avoid an unresolved graph moment. Population adjustment
uses justified invariance and support; imputation uses an observation and
analysis model; historical retrieval uses identity and availability rules.
Neither a completed table nor a precise conditional calculation establishes
all of those premises.

A defensible recommendation therefore retains the missing information and its
monetary consequence. It may call for an additional joint audit, a different
allocation, a restricted target population, sensitivity analysis or refusal.
The software choices matter because their score, covariance, mask, clock and
failure behavior can preserve or change that recommendation. The next chapter
examines hidden-state and Bayesian computations as further conditional tools,
with their assumptions carried into the comparison.

\section{Commercial missing-data workflows and transfer between bank populations}
\label{exec21:transport-scope}

A bank may obtain a credible intervention estimate in a pilot and still make a
poor decision when it extends the intervention to another branch. Customers may
differ, follow-up outcomes may be missing, and the software used to complete
the records may report uncertainty for a different quantity from the proposed
decision. A useful commercial comparison therefore follows the complete
question: which population receives which action, when is the outcome measured,
why is it unobserved, and which assumptions connect the observed records to the
decision? Imputation, uncertainty combination and population transfer are
separate steps. A feature called ``missing values'' establishes none of those
connections by its name alone.

The selected primary documentation provides concrete comparators. Stata's
\texttt{mi} family manages multiple completed datasets and their analysis;
SAS/STAT's MI and MIANALYZE procedures separate generation and combination;
IBM SPSS Missing Values exposes imputation and output-specific pooling.
The inspected IBM edition is 31.0.2. The SAS HTML identifies version 14.1,
whereas the Stata manuals contain release-19 example-data paths and July 2026
PDF metadata. These identities delimit the comparison; later retrieval does
not authenticate every byte as the edition available at the literature cutoff.
Exact licensed builds, current entitlements and broader commercial coverage
remain unresolved. EViews, Mplus and commercial graphical tools remain leads
requiring matched technical originals for this particular target.
\cite{exec21_transport_stata_mi,exec21_transport_sas_mi_intro,exec21_transport_spss_missing}

\subsection{Missingness assumptions precede record completion}
\label{exec21:transport-missingness}

Let $A$ be a binary action, $X$ covariates recorded before that action, $Y(a)$
the monetary outcome under action $a$, and $R$ an indicator that the outcome is
observed. The record contains $(X,A,R,RY)$, with a separate missingness mask so
that an absent outcome is never mistaken for a zero. Consistency connects an
observed outcome to $Y(A)$; treatment exchangeability and positive treatment
probability are additional causal assumptions. For the particular problem in
which only $Y$ is missing, a conditional mean restriction sufficient for response
adjustment is
\begin{equation}
 E[Y\mid X,A,R=1]=E[Y\mid X,A],\qquad
 P(R=1\mid X,A)>0.
 \label{exec21:transport-mar}
\end{equation}
The stronger familiar MAR restriction makes response independent of the missing
outcome conditional on the observed variables. When covariates are also missing,
the pattern-specific observed information and imputation model must be specified
again; equation~\eqref{exec21:transport-mar} is not a general multivariate recipe.
Administrative censoring, a variable undefined for a customer, and an outcome
lost through nonresponse need distinct observation models.

Stata's substantive manual and the SAS assumptions chapter distinguish MAR
from MCAR and describe ignorability using MAR together with distinct parameters
for the data and missingness models. They also explain why an assumption about
unobserved values cannot be verified by inspecting only the observed values.
The SAS profile adds distributional restrictions for particular regression and
MCMC procedures. These restrictions must accompany a procedure name. A good
fit to observed records, a plausible-looking imputed distribution or rejection
of an MCAR diagnostic does not establish MAR.
\cite{exec21_transport_stata_substantive,exec21_transport_sas_assumptions}

An exact example makes the investment consequence visible. Let a latent response
type $H$ be equally likely to be zero or one, randomize $A$ independently of
$H$, and set $R=H$. All customers have $Y(0)=0$. Responders have $Y(1)=10$.
In one complete-data law, nonresponders have $Y(1)=-10$; in a second they have
$Y(1)=10$. The observable joint distribution of $(A,R,RY)$ is identical in
both laws: each action-response cell has probability $1/4$, and observed treated
outcomes equal 10. Yet the complete-population effects are respectively 0 and
10. At an assumed action cost of USD 4, the margins are USD $-4$ and USD 6.
More imputation draws from one selected model cannot distinguish these worlds.
The project reference enumerates the complete laws and verifies equality of
their observed distributions. It does not assert that either law describes
actual bank records. \cite{exec21_transport_reference}

A transparent sensitivity parameter writes the unobserved treated mean as
$10+\delta$, keeping the control mean zero. The resulting target is
\begin{equation}
 \tau(\delta)=10+\tfrac12\delta,\qquad
 V(\delta)=6+\tfrac12\delta.
 \label{exec21:transport-sensitivity}
\end{equation}
For the illustrative restriction $\delta\in[-20,0]$, value ranges from $-4$
to 6 and changes sign at $\delta=-12$. The interval is supplied as a sensitivity
restriction, not learned from the missing outcomes. The SAS sensitivity chapter
documents a pattern-mixture approach in MI and explicitly says that the
selection-model approach is not supplied by that procedure profile. A result
that changes under a plausible MNAR scenario establishes dependence of the
decision on assumptions; it does not establish which scenario is true. Exact
syntax and later-release capabilities need their own evidence.
\cite{exec21_transport_sas_sensitivity,exec21_transport_reference}

that the combined weighting expression recovers the stipulated target.
No software error is needed for the naive deployment decision to reverse:
the wrong population suffices. \cite{exec21_transport_reference}

If the source instead contains only the first stratum, the second effect is
unobserved and no finite reweighting creates its information. With the explicit
restriction that the second effect lies in $[-10,10]$, the target effect is
$2+(4/5)\tau(1)\in[-6,10]$, giving margin $[-8,8]$ at cost 2. Without such
a justified bound, even that interval cannot be asserted. An adapter should
report the support defect and any defensible identified set. Silently trimming
the second stratum changes the target population; silently predicting into it
adds extrapolation assumptions. \cite{exec21_transport_reference}

\subsection{Competitive position and a public qualification route}
\label{exec21:transport-integration}

The documented commercial systems already provide substantive imputation,
analysis and diagnostic workflows. The proposal has not demonstrated a native
replacement or superior estimation performance. Its proposed contribution is
to preserve the causal question and its restrictions across those workflows:
source and target populations, observation clocks, missingness reasons,
imputation identity, covariance semantics and explicit refusal. Licensed
isolated execution is a candidate integration route; public manuals do not
grant redistribution rights for the engines. EViews, Mplus and graphical-tool
profiles cannot be ranked without the missing originals, and prices remain
unknown. \cite{exec21_transport_stata_estimate,exec21_transport_sas_mianalyze_intro,exec21_transport_spss_missing}

A useful first prototype would compare a selected licensed procedure and an
already reviewed open implementation on the same generated population,
missingness law and estimand. Complete-record analysis, complete-case analysis,
single imputation, proper multiple imputation and an explicitly specified
response-weight procedure supply substantive alternatives. Fix the causal
target, sample law, interaction structure, number of imputations, diagnostic
and refusal rules before evaluation. Include MAR and MNAR cases, complete and
missing source support, compatible and incompatible imputation models, cluster
sampling, changing coefficient sets and unsuccessful fits. Report bias,
coverage under the claimed regime, interval width, unavailable requests,
simulation error and full workflow cost. A sensitivity grid evaluates
robustness; it is not a device for choosing whichever assumption makes a
preferred intervention profitable.

The library, CLI and MCP interfaces should carry the same request and result
meaning. Original and imputed data need stable unit and imputation identifiers,
measurement types, category references, passive transformations and sampling
design. Results need per-imputation estimates and covariance, pooled scale and
degrees of freedom, convergence diagnostics, population support and retained
failures. An assistant can help locate technical passages, propose models and
explain sensitivity; it cannot infer the unobserved outcomes or authorize a
scientific assumption from fluent text. These public comparisons can establish
whether the proposed integration merits a more expensive bank experiment.


\subsection{What must be preserved from the audit to the decision}

The chapter's alternatives answer different information problems. Joint audits
can distinguish relationship laws that separate-edge labels cannot. Coordinated
actions can sometimes avoid an unresolved graph moment. Population adjustment
uses justified invariance and support; imputation uses an observation and
analysis model; historical retrieval uses identity and availability rules.
Neither a completed table nor a precise conditional calculation establishes
all of those premises.

A defensible recommendation therefore retains the missing information and its
monetary consequence. It may call for an additional joint audit, a different
allocation, a restricted target population, sensitivity analysis or refusal.
The software choices matter because their score, covariance, mask, clock and
failure behavior can preserve or change that recommendation. The next chapter
examines hidden-state and Bayesian computations as further conditional tools,
with their assumptions carried into the comparison.

\section{NumPyro: preserving the experiment through handlers and compiled inference}
\label{sec:exec23-numpyro-worker}

NumPyro is a plausible Python worker when a bank can state a probabilistic model and wants to explore a JAX-based computational route. Its role begins with that supplied model. It does not determine whether a servicing action is manipulable, whether an unrecorded customer state confounds treatment, or whether a financial reporting field was available when the decision was made. These scientific choices must enter the model contract before a sampler can answer the intended question. The pinned source examined here declares version 0.22.0 at revision \texttt{033f7e2e57bd0396fba8493ae246debe52f2c973}, committed on 5 October 2026. This is a source declaration at a revision within the literature cutoff, rather than an assertion that an independently acquired release artifact has identical contents. The root license is Apache-2.0, the Python requirement is at least 3.11, and the direct numerical requirements include JAX and jaxlib at least 0.7.0. Device-specific extras and the additional Funsor inference route require their own artifact and rights review.\cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

The comparison with PyMC is therefore a comparison of proposed worker contracts. PyMC's inspected route transforms a graph and controls predictive freezing and regeneration; NumPyro's inspected route applies handlers to executions of a stochastic function and passes arrays through compiled inference. Neither representation supplies missing assignment information. Both need the same banking estimand, information clock, outcome units and refusal semantics. Their different defaults make a transparent adapter more useful than a wrapper that merely gives identically named commands.\cite{exec23_pymc_sources,exec23_numpyro_sources}

\subsection{Conditioning, intervention and the meaning of an execution trace}

In the inspected handler implementation, \texttt{condition} sets a matched sample value and marks the site observed. \texttt{substitute} can replace several kinds of primitive, including deterministic values, without making the same observation declaration. \texttt{replay} takes matched sampled values from an execution trace, checks the sampled-versus-observed role and leaves already observed target sites alone. Thus matching a site name is a mechanism for moving values; it is not evidence that two models describe the same financial experiment. An adapter must bind the model, data and site roles as well as their array shapes.\cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

The \texttt{do} handler makes an especially consequential distinction. It creates a fresh sample site with the original name whose value does not propagate to descendants, then sends the supplied intervention value down the original computation. A returned treatment value and a recorded sample under the original treatment name can consequently differ by design. The upstream counterfactual tests explicitly distinguish the model's returned values from the trace values, including when observation and intervention are composed. Those tests describe intended behavior; they have not been executed in this proposal. A converter that extracts the original-name trace entry and calls it the administered action could misreport the experiment even when the handler follows its own contract. Multiple intervention handlers at the same site also require attention to the inspected warning and handler order.\cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

The causal distinction can be checked without a numerical backend. Let an unobserved binary type $U$ have probability $1/2$, let a binary action $A$ agree with $U$ with probability $3/4$, and set the response to $Y=2A+4U$. Enumeration gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathrm{E}(Y\mid A=0)=1,\qquad
 \mathrm{E}(Y\mid A=1)=5,\qquad
 \mathrm{E}\{Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a)\}=2a+2.
\end{equation}
The association is four response units and the intervention contrast is two. This is the same deliberately confounded law used in the PyMC comparison, recalculated by an independently authored finite enumeration here. It supplies a common semantic oracle: conditioning an action and cutting its assignment mechanism have different answers. Neither backend acquires identification simply by returning one of these numbers.\cite{exec23_pymc_reference,exec23_numpyro_reference}

Composing handlers also does not make every customer-specific counterfactual identified. To see the extra requirement, let $Y^0$ and $Y^1$ denote binary responses under two actions. One structural model has $(Y^0,Y^1)=(U,U)$ for $U\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(1/2)$; another has $(Y^0,Y^1)=(U,1-U)$. Both have
\begin{equation}
 \Pr(Y^0=1)=\Pr(Y^1=1)=\tfrac12,
\end{equation}
but $\Pr(Y^1=1\mid Y^0=1)$ is one in the first model and zero in the second. Equal single-world intervention marginals leave this cross-world quantity undetermined. A shared-noise construction or another justified restriction can define a model-specific answer, and sensitivity across these constructions can expose the ambiguity. A model proposed by an LLM must state that construction explicitly; handler composition cannot verify it. This example is an authored identification witness, not an upstream software failure.\cite{exec23_numpyro_reference}

\subsection{Prediction must preserve which latent variables are regenerated}

The inspected \texttt{Predictive} implementation substitutes supplied posterior values, then executes the model. By default it ignores stored deterministic values during substitution and recomputes them from their parents. Setting \texttt{condition\_deterministic=True} instead permits those stored values to be substituted. Output selection through \texttt{return\_sites} has a separate role. As a simple arithmetic check, equal-weight parent values $(1,2)$ give a stored-square mean of $5/2$ and a recomputed-cube mean of $9/2$. Keeping the old deterministic values after changing the expression answers a different question from recomputation. NumPyro's default and PyMC's inspected predictive controls should therefore be represented by explicit regeneration choices in a common interface. One cannot infer equivalence from matching output names.\cite{exec23_numpyro_sources,exec23_pymc_sources,exec23_numpyro_reference}

Posterior substitution also fixes supplied stochastic sites. Including such a site among requested outputs does not ask the model to redraw it. Conversely, an absent latent site is not automatically inferred from an observed response during ordinary forward execution. The inspected \texttt{infer\_discrete} path invokes additional enumeration and posterior-sampling machinery; ordinary prediction uses a different masking and execution path. The documentation further requires clearing an observed response to generate a new realization of that response. Leaving an old observation attached can preserve that value rather than create a new future outcome. A bank worker must distinguish parameter draws learned from historical data, historical customer states, states to infer from new evidence and genuinely new outcomes.\cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

A servicing example shows why this is an economic distinction. Suppose a hidden type $U=1$ has prior probability $1/3$, and an alert $S=1$ has probabilities $3/4$ under type one and $1/4$ under type zero. The alert probability and posterior type probability are
\begin{equation}
 \Pr(S=1)=\tfrac{5}{12},\qquad
 \Pr(U=1\mid S=1)=
 \frac{(1/3)(3/4)}{(1/3)(3/4)+(2/3)(1/4)}=\tfrac35.
\end{equation}
Let an additional action have stipulated net payoffs USD 100 for type one and USD $-200$ for type zero; taking no additional action pays zero. Averaging over the posterior gives
\begin{equation}
 V(1\mid S=1)=\tfrac35(100)+\tfrac25(-200)=-20.
\end{equation}
Replacing the type distribution by its most probable state instead reports USD 100 and selects the action, with an actual expected loss of USD 20 under the specified posterior law. Ignoring the alert and drawing the type from its prior gives yet another action value, USD $-100$. Posterior averaging, MAP substitution and unconditioned regeneration are three different procedures. These exact, stipulated amounts motivate the adapter's uncertainty contract; they are not measured returns from a bank or observed package behavior.\cite{exec23_numpyro_reference}

\subsection{Discrete inference and continuous sampling have separate contracts}

For enumerable latent sites, the inspected model utilities prepare parallel enumeration, with plate dimensions controlling the tensor arrangement. The Funsor contribution is an additional dependency and is labelled experimental by its import path. The inspected discrete handler accepts temperature one for posterior sampling and temperature zero for MAP-style decoding; other temperatures are rejected. Its source also warns that inferred-trace log probabilities are not meaningful. A downstream likelihood audit must not reuse those trace log probabilities as an ordinary fitted likelihood. Likewise, a MAP path is not a collection of posterior paths and cannot propagate hidden-state uncertainty in the servicing example. The scan boundary needs more careful qualification: the handler documentation says the scan primitive is unsupported, whereas the selected tests include scan hidden-Markov examples of lengths one and two and mark length ten as expected to fail because of a Markov sum-product adjoint limitation. This documentation/test tension justifies a registered length- and construction-specific trial, not a blanket assertion of support or a reproduced failure. None of those upstream tests has been run here.\cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

NumPyro also exposes composable Gibbs and HMC-within-Gibbs routes. The inspected discrete selector distinguishes enumerable sites being updated from sites already marked for marginalization. The proposal must record that choice, support sizes, block structure and proposal settings. The inspected composition rejects some configurations, including subsample plates and value-dependent supports across blocks; the HMC-within-Gibbs entry rejects a bare potential-function model. These restrictions do not establish that a different kernel can repair the case. Native qualification should compare a small hidden-state model against complete enumeration and retain separate acceptance for marginal likelihood, posterior state probabilities and policy value. A state decoder agreeing with one selected path cannot satisfy all three.\cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

A continuous reference can be equally transparent. With a $\mathrm{Beta}(2,3)$ prior and four successes plus one failure, the likelihood gives a $\mathrm{Beta}(6,4)$ posterior. Ratios of its normalizing integrals yield mean $3/5$ and variance $6/275$. This provides a check of both location and spread without treating an optimizer's answer as a posterior. A later registered trial can assess chains against those moments, finite-sample Monte Carlo tolerances and diagnostic behavior. Passing that trial would qualify this numerical construction under its declared law; it would not identify a confounded action or validate an unknown causal model.\cite{exec23_numpyro_reference}

\subsection{Devices, random keys, diagnostics and restart identity}

The inspected MCMC interface requests parallel chains by default but falls back to sequential chains with a warning if too few devices are available. Vectorized chains are another declared route. Device count, execution method and actual array precision must therefore enter a run identity; a requested GPU or parallel configuration is insufficient evidence that it was used. The source utilities expose platform and 64-bit configuration, and the host-device-count helper carries its own configuration caveat. These are controls to test, not measured throughput or a general speed advantage over PyMC.\cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

Randomness needs equally explicit treatment. The seed handler carries a mutable random key and documents a closure pattern to avoid leaking this state through JAX transformations. MCMC splits a single key for multiple chains; it also accepts a supplied batch of keys. An adapter should preserve how chains and prediction tasks receive keys and check the intended independence or deliberate coupling. Four exact copies of a Bernoulli$(1/2)$ draw have average variance $1/4$; four independent draws have average variance $1/16$. Labelling copies as independent would understate variance by a factor of four. This is an authored dependence counterexample, not a finding that NumPyro's scalar-key splitting duplicates chains. Deliberately coupled random numbers for a paired comparison can be legitimate, but their covariance must be represented.\cite{exec23_numpyro_sources,exec23_numpyro_reference}

The inspected HMC state includes trajectory and divergence information, while the default collected fields retain samples and divergences. Further quantities need explicit collection. Summary functions use split R-hat and effective sample size with declared chain/draw axes and minimum draw requirements. Their names do not establish identity with another package's diagnostic implementation. The proposed worker must distinguish an unavailable diagnostic, a nonfinite value, an adverse diagnostic and a satisfactory result under predeclared criteria. None of these outcomes certifies assignment truth, graph identification or repeated-sampling calibration of a causal policy interval.\cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

For continuation, \texttt{last\_state} and \texttt{post\_warmup\_state} expose more information than saved posterior draws. The documented continuation route reuses the final state and its random key; warmup behavior changes when a post-warmup state is supplied. This is a useful interface for a future recovery design, but not evidence of durable serialization, crash consistency or compatibility across changed models. A restart contract must bind the complete sampler state, model/data identities, transformations, adaptation, random-key lineage, numerical environment and publication boundary. Local fault injection must then show whether uninterrupted and interrupted executions meet the registered comparison rule. Timing must also account for JAX's asynchronous dispatch, which the MCMC documentation expressly notes; elapsed Python submission time alone is not complete computational cost.\cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

\subsection{A concrete reuse decision and a bounded qualification route}

The appropriate disposition is to retain NumPyro as a source-qualified reference for a future native Python worker. Direct use would preserve its handler, enumeration and numerical semantics within a pinned environment. A general R, Java or C++ port would duplicate those semantics and the compiler boundary without demonstrated benefit; a process interface is the more defensible candidate until conversion costs are measured. PyMC remains a substantive alternative for graph transformation and posterior prediction, while exact finite and conjugate calculations remain independent semantic references. Selection between workers should use matched supported models, accepted uncertainty output, full compilation and warmup costs, effective sample production, prediction, memory, serialization and recovery. No hardware performance ranking follows from the source review.\cite{exec23_numpyro_sources,exec23_pymc_sources,exec23_numpyro_reference}

Library, CLI and MCP entrypoints should preserve one model and experiment identity: observation versus intervention, factual versus cross-world target, fixed versus regenerated sites, posterior averaging versus MAP decoding, units and clock, chain layout, precision and diagnostic availability. An LLM can propose these declarations, retrieve the supporting assumptions and explain refused requests; the model owner must justify their scientific meaning. A maintainer must bind the selected NumPyro, JAX, jaxlib, Funsor and device artifacts and their rights. An operator must set budgets, verify actual device execution and test durable recovery. The pinned metadata names a license-file path that differs from the inspected root filename, so a release trial must inspect the actual distributed notices rather than infer their custody from a classifier. None of these owner roles is filled by an API response.\cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

Before integration approval, a registered native trial should exercise the finite confounding and cross-world witnesses, compare posterior averaging with discrete decoding, check deterministic substitution under changed inputs, validate the conjugate moments, inspect invalid supports and dimensions, verify diagnostic availability and test interrupted continuation. Whole-environment rights, numerical reliability and the causal assumptions remain separate acceptance questions. The exact examples demonstrate why those experiments have merit before costly bank validation; general causal identification and bank adoption remain open.\cite{exec23_numpyro_sources,exec23_numpyro_reference}

No hardware performance ranking follows from the source review. \cite{exec23_numpyro_sources,exec23_pymc_sources,exec23_numpyro_reference}

Library, CLI and MCP entrypoints should preserve one model and experiment identity: observation versus intervention, factual versus cross-world target, fixed versus regenerated sites, posterior averaging versus MAP decoding, units and clock, chain layout, precision and diagnostic availability. An LLM can propose these declarations, retrieve the supporting assumptions and explain refused requests; the model owner must justify their scientific meaning. A maintainer must bind the selected NumPyro, JAX, jaxlib, Funsor and device artifacts and their rights. An operator must set budgets, verify actual device execution and test durable recovery. The pinned metadata names a license-file path that differs from the inspected root filename, so a release trial must inspect the actual distributed notices rather than infer their custody from a classifier. None of these owner roles is filled by an API response. \cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

Before integration approval, a registered native trial should exercise the finite confounding and cross-world witnesses, compare posterior averaging with discrete decoding, check deterministic substitution under changed inputs, validate the conjugate moments, inspect invalid supports and dimensions, verify diagnostic availability and test interrupted continuation. Whole-environment rights, numerical reliability and the causal assumptions remain separate acceptance questions. The exact examples demonstrate why those experiments have merit before costly bank validation; general causal identification and bank adoption remain open. \cite{exec23_numpyro_sources,exec23_numpyro_reference}

\chapter{Interference, allocation policies and software adoption}
\label{v13:sw-networks}

The preceding relationship analysis showed why a policy may require joint
graph and action information. This chapter examines the allocation problem
itself. It distinguishes network and grouped targets, develops the two initial
software references, and compares spatial, experimental, learned-policy and
simulation alternatives. The recurring small graphs and cost denominators are
matched comparison devices; each implementation's different assumptions and
failure conditions remain part of the argument.

\section{The unit receiving treatment need not be the independent unit}

A household member's offer can influence another member's borrowing, and an
outreach campaign can affect connected firms. In such settings a potential
outcome depends on more than the individual's own action. Writing only
$Y_i(a_i)$ hides the policy being evaluated. A more explicit representation is
$Y_i(a_i,\mathbf a_{-i})$, often restricted through an exposure mapping of
other units' actions. The mapping and the network are scientific inputs;
neither is established merely by finding matching customer identifiers.

Two broad software constructions appear in the inspected sources. MossSpider
uses a network and exposure summaries in a network-targeted estimation
workflow. Inferference uses grouped formulas, allocation probabilities and
inverse-probability weighting. These constructions have different observation
laws and potentially different targets. Their package names do not establish
interchangeability.\cite{v13_sw_mossspider,v13_sw_inferference}

An allocation policy illustrates the target. Suppose two linked borrowers have
binary outreach actions $A_1,A_2$, independently assigned with probability $p$
under the proposed policy. Stipulate the synthetic financial outcome
\[
 Y_i(a_i,a_j)=100a_i+40a_j-30a_i a_j
\]
in CNY. The first term represents the own-action contribution, the second a
spillover and the last diminishing combined benefit. These are hypothetical
structural values, not bank estimates. Averaging under the allocation gives
\[
 V(p)=140p-30p^2.
\]
For $p=0.2$ the mean is 26.8 CNY; for $p=0.8$ it is 92.8 CNY. The allocation
contrast is 66 CNY per borrower. Exact enumeration of the four assignments
checks the formula.\cite{v13_project_exact}

The direct effect of changing only the individual's own action is instead
$100-30a_j$, or $100-30p$ when the neighbor is independently treated with
probability $p$. This differs from the total allocation contrast. Reporting
one as the other can misprice the campaign even when every arithmetic
calculation is correct. The bank must specify whether it changes one action,
the neighborhood's allocation or an entire branch policy, and which costs
are included in the outcome.

\section{MossSpider: network semantics are part of the estimand}

The inspected \texttt{NetworkTMLE} documentation describes expected incidence
under a treatment plan, with Monte Carlo integration over allocations for
stochastic plans. It states a direct-contact interference assumption. The
constructor rejects self-loops, noninteger node identities and nonbinary
exposure, creates a relabeled network while retaining original identities,
and constructs an unweighted adjacency matrix.\cite{v13_sw_mossspider}

These details matter for bank graphs. A weighted guarantee network is not the
same as an unweighted adjacency graph. Removing weights can turn a small
guarantee into the same exposure contribution as a large one. Relabeling nodes
is harmless only when results can be mapped back to the correct identities.
A linkage error can attach the correct numerical estimate to the wrong firm.
Semantic conformance therefore needs an identity roundtrip and an explicit
policy for unsupported weighted relationships.

Direction requires particular review. The documentation initially describes an
undirected graph but also explains a directed influence convention opposite
the graph arrow, and the selected constructor includes directed handling. This
combination requires a concrete test with an asymmetric small graph. One should
not infer direction from a diagram's appearance or assume that every library
uses source-to-target influence. A two-node one-way example with distinguishable
covariates can determine which neighbor contributes to each exposure summary.
Section~\ref{sec:exec24-interference-reuse} develops the selected mapping,
policy and variance paths. Their inspected direction convention still needs
matched native tests; directed bank-network adoption remains a proposed use.\cite{v13_sw_mossspider}

Degree restrictions also change the target. The documentation treats nodes
outside a requested degree range as background, with their exposures unchanged
by the intervention. This can be scientifically useful, but it is not the
same as deleting those nodes from the graph or intervening on all customers.
The response must state which nodes are in the target population, which remain
background and how their factual exposure affects the intervention outcome.

The source disclaims a missing-data procedure. Missing node attributes,
uncertain links and omitted customers are common in banking, but the existence
of an exposure-mapping function does not solve those observation problems.
One must either supply defensible complete data in the declared regime or
develop a separate missingness/linkage construction. Network-targeted estimation
does not automatically qualify ownership or inclusion truth.

The observed MIT text makes a restricted adapter worth considering. Full adoption
requires qualification of the exposure-model and mapping code, targeting step,
Monte Carlo integration and variance calculation, together with actual
dependency/runtime checks. The developed study retains deterministic-policy
refusals, background-node treatment and a potentially negative variance
quadratic; these restrictions belong in any proposed adapter. A claim of general contagion, dynamic financial-network equilibrium or
arbitrary spillovers would go beyond the selected implementation evidence.

\section{Inferference: grouped allocation and numerical integration}

The inspected \texttt{interference} function uses a formula that identifies
outcome, exposure, optional participation, propensity covariates and a grouping
variable. It accepts allocation probabilities and propensity-model choices
including \texttt{glm}, \texttt{glmer}, \texttt{HLfit} and an oracle route.
Its documented causal-estimation path is IPW with naive or robust variance
options. The selected code sorts records by group and checks group count,
allocation range and the variance option.\cite{v13_sw_inferference}

A group-based model can be appropriate when the scientific design justifies
within-group interference and the required between-group sampling assumptions.
It does not become a model of arbitrary connected borrowers by assigning
everyone a group label. Cross-group guarantees or shared market shocks can
violate the intended observation law. The grouping decision needs domain
evidence and should be subjected to sensitivity analysis where boundaries
are uncertain.

The default logit integrand is restricted to a single random effect in the
documented implementation. The code rejects more than one when that integrand
is selected. Thus a proposal with household and branch random effects needs a
different justified integration path; silently dropping one random effect is
a model change. An oracle propensity option is useful for synthetic reference
calculations, but supplied true parameters cannot be counted as evidence that
an estimated-propensity workflow is calibrated.

There is also a reproducibility issue visible directly in the source. The prose
describes \texttt{integrate\_allocation} as defaulting to false, while the
inspected function signature sets it to true. The proper response is to specify
and record the argument explicitly. Section~\ref{sec:exec24-interference-reuse}
traces the downstream ratio and derivative paths; their flag propagation,
allocation-mass and missing-group restrictions still require matched native
qualification. It is not appropriate to select whichever default gives a more
favorable result after comparing outputs.\cite{v13_sw_inferference}

For large groups, multiplying many probabilities can create numerical problems.
The documentation discusses an allocation-integration option in this context.
Qualification should include large and uneven groups, boundary allocation
probabilities, integration tolerances and variance derivatives. A successful
floating-point result does not prove adequate support; an underflow error does
not prove nonidentification. These are different failure modes and need
different diagnostics.

The observed DESCRIPTION declares GPL version 2 or later and a dated version.
That informs a dependency review but does not establish the license status of
every linked component or distribution arrangement. A candidate grouped-policy
reference should remain distinct from a decision to embed or port it.

\section{A common comparison must distinguish network and group assumptions}

The two packages can be compared on a common small allocation problem only
after their target, exposure mapping and sampling assumptions are aligned.
For the two-borrower example, the exact four-assignment enumeration supplies a
transparent functional reference. A larger benchmark should vary degree,
group size, allocation probability, support, observation errors and dependence.
It should include examples where a direct-contact or group restriction is false.

Metrics should separate the target mean, direct and spillover contrasts,
coverage, finite availability, Monte Carlo integration error and total cost.
Increasing simulated allocations reduces integration error conditional on a
fitted model. It does not create independent groups or validate the graph.
Uncertainty must follow the actual sampling unit; counting nodes as independent
merely because the graph is stored in a table can produce misleading precision.

The implementation contract should retain the original graph, its direction
and weights, the identity map, intervention population, allocation rule,
background nodes and exposure mapping. A result should be rejected as
semantically incompatible if a proposed bridge silently changes any of these.
This requirement is shared by library calls, command-line jobs and agent tools.
An interface can make a scientific restriction visible; it cannot make it true.

\section{Provisional reuse choices and the evidence needed to change them}

The inspected software supports a portfolio of candidate components rather
than a single universal engine. The following choices describe potential uses and qualification conditions,
not accepted integrations or benchmarks. The earlier functional and
longitudinal chapters develop the corresponding source findings
(Chapters~\ref{v13:sw-functional} and~\ref{v13:sw-regimes}); the table retains
the conditions that must survive implementation rather than treating those
studies as still absent.

\begin{longtable}{p{0.18\textwidth}p{0.34\textwidth}p{0.39\textwidth}}
\toprule
Component & Candidate role & Conditions to preserve and qualify\\
\midrule
\endhead
DirectLiNGAM & Functional discovery adapter & Reviewed base-class behavior, prior orientation,
functional assumptions and adverse latent/Gaussian cases\\
y0 & Symbolic ID/IDC adapter & Reviewed recursive paths, conditional-path restriction,
graph validation, expression roundtrip and nonidentification references\\
delicatessen & Equation and numerical reference & Solver, Jacobian, covariance,
sampling unit and complete dependency contract\\
statsmodels & Point-treatment GMM baseline & Matched population, propensity bounds,
actual covariance behavior and dependent-data limits\\
pygformula & Longitudinal-regime adapter & History/event meaning, simulation,
bootstrap unit, diagnostics and policy scope\\
grf & R/native heterogeneous-effect component & Native algorithms, variance,
aggregation measure, ABI and license/distribution review\\
CausalGPS & Continuous-density component & Density/transformation helpers,
counterfactual doses, support and downstream estimation\\
causaldrf & Dose-response reference & Full function, interval procedures,
support, recovered holder notice and dependency terms\\
MossSpider & Restricted network-policy component & Direction, mapping, identity,
targeting, variance and observation restrictions\\
inferference & Grouped-allocation reference & Integrands, numerical defaults,
variance, group law and dependency terms\\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

An integration decision is stronger than identifying a promising function.
Direct adoption needs a stable, compatible dependency and scientific contract.
An adapter needs semantic parity and error preservation. A port needs the right
to reuse the implementation, an upstream behavioral oracle, independent
references, numerical/statistical equivalence criteria and a maintenance owner.
A research reference can be valuable without becoming a product dependency.
Deferral is justified when these prerequisites are missing; rejection should
state a concrete incompatibility and a revisit condition.

Commercial comparison must apply the same discipline. Vendor documentation can
establish a dated documented feature, but not measured agreement or operating
cost without an executed comparison. An inaccessible manual cannot support a
claim that the vendor lacks an operation. Our proposed graph-to-effect or
banking workflow is likewise not a delivered competitive advantage. A sound
build/buy/partner decision compares the vendor's documented and measured state
with our implemented, conditional, proposed or absent state, and makes the
missing evidence explicit.

Licensing is one part of this decision. The selected MIT and BSD texts,
repository GPL text and package license declarations provide traceable starting
points. Dependencies, bundled data, separate notices, native libraries and the
intended distribution arrangement still need review. A subprocess boundary
does not automatically settle licensing obligations, just as a Python wrapper
does not establish that a native operation has been qualified.

The software survey can therefore guide implementation immediately without
claiming premature adoption. It identifies precise operations, preserves their
mathematical meaning and specifies the evidence needed for the next decision.
Runtime, bank validation and independent scientific acceptance remain separate
from these source-grounded provisional choices.
