\chapter{Customer histories, heterogeneous effects and economic units}
\label{v131:histories-forests}

This chapter returns to the customer-level request after the network comparisons.
The earlier longitudinal, forest and dose studies supply the detailed methods;
the question here is what must remain unchanged when their outputs are reused.
Whole histories, within-period event order, the population being averaged and
the units of a treatment density can each change the economic answer. The
examples retain those distinctions without treating a common interface as a
common estimand.

\section{Resampling a sequence requires a sampling model}

Consider a bank evaluating a sequence of servicing decisions over twelve
months. The data contain repeated observations of each borrower, interventions
that depend on previous balances and competing events such as account closure.
The statistical unit might be a borrower history, a household, a branch or an
independent economic calendar. These choices imply different resampling laws.
A routine with ``bootstrap'' in its name does not determine the appropriate law.

LiNGAM's generic bootstrap resamples rows and refits the model. VARLiNGAM has
a distinct path: it fits a lag model, applies a contemporaneous LiNGAM model to
the residuals, resamples residual vectors and reconstructs a sequence using the
fitted autoregressive coefficients. The inspected loop temporarily sets the
lag-selection criterion to \texttt{None}. Consequently, one must inspect the
initial lag/coefficient settings and the loop's refit behavior before claiming
that it propagates model-selection uncertainty.\cite{v131_sw_lingam}

Residual resampling can be a sensible candidate under an appropriate innovation
law. It does not automatically preserve persistent residual dependence,
unmodeled common shocks or a different sampling calendar. Row resampling is a
different candidate suitable for a different observational unit. A banking
comparison should include a correctly specified innovation model and an adverse
case with persistent residuals, preserving the uncertainty target and failures
in both. Bootstrap edge frequencies should not be reported as a calibrated
effect confidence region without an additional argument.

pygformula's inspected bootstrap draws observed subject identifiers with
replacement, copies each subject's complete history and assigns a fresh replicate
identifier to each draw. It updates histories and refits covariate and outcome
models. Expanding to the requested simulation population occurs in a separate
step. These operations distinguish the observed sampling unit from the Monte
Carlo population used to evaluate a fitted regime.\cite{v131_sw_pygformula}

The fresh identifiers matter. Drawing borrower 17 twice should produce two
bootstrap histories, not concatenate them into one impossible person with two
records at every date. An integration test needs duplicate draws, unequal
history lengths and multiple interventions. It must also preserve the original
calendar when that calendar is part of the estimand. Subject resampling alone
does not account for a market shock shared by every subject on the same date.

Failed fits require equally explicit handling. The inspected bootstrap helper
catches an exception, warns and returns a dictionary whose
\texttt{boot\_results} is \texttt{None}. The caller filters such entries when
assembling one result list, but subsequently constructs \texttt{bootests} by
indexing every original entry. A failed entry therefore exposes a static
inconsistency in that caller path. This observation requires reproduction in
the pinned runtime before attributing an observed frequency or impact to it.
The integration must count attempted, successful and failed replications and
preserve the failure reason, irrespective of whether the eventual repair
aborts, returns an explicit unavailable interval or uses a preregistered rule.
\cite{v13_sw_pygformula,v131_sw_pygformula}

\section{The intervention clock and competing-event target}

The inspected simulation path applies an intervention to the current simulated
frame and then refreshes history variables before outcome prediction. Static
schedules index their values by the absolute time index \texttt{int\_values[t]}.
Threshold interventions bound the current action between the supplied limits.
Custom interventions receive the current frame, available pool and time index.
The API permits useful regimes, but does not itself certify that a custom
function uses only information available at the decision time.
\cite{v131_sw_pygformula}

For example, ``contact once delinquency has persisted for two months'' refers
to the observed history before the action, whereas ``contact borrowers who
will be delinquent next month'' uses future information. Both can be expressed
as executable code if future fields have been made available. A valid interface
must enforce the declared information clock and treat prohibited reads as a
contract violation. Thresholds should also retain their monetary units and
whether they change an action, a measurement or an eligibility condition.

Competing events alter the target even when the same outcome model is used.
In a stipulated discrete-time model, let $d_t$ be the probability of a competing
event in period $t$ among those still at risk, and let $y_t$ be the outcome
hazard conditional on avoiding that competing event. If competing events occur
before outcomes within a period, the cumulative incidence through $T$ is
\[
 F_Y(T)=\sum_{t=1}^T
 \left\{\prod_{s<t}(1-d_s)(1-y_s)\right\}(1-d_t)y_t.
\]
This formula follows by partitioning on the period of the first outcome event.
It differs from a hypothetical law that eliminates the competing event.

For two periods with $y=(0.1,0.2)$ and $d=(0.05,0.1)$, the first contribution
is $0.095$ and the second is $0.9(0.95)(0.9)(0.2)=0.1539$. Total incidence is
$0.2489$. Removing competing events while holding these outcome hazards fixed
gives $1-(0.9)(0.8)=0.28$. At a stipulated 10,000 accounts and CNY 100 per event,
the corresponding expected-loss difference is CNY 31,100. This is exact
illustrative arithmetic. It does not identify the effect of eliminating a
real bank's competing event or establish that the outcome hazard would remain
fixed under that intervention.\cite{v131_project_semantics}

The inspected pygformula source separately computes survival risks with and
without a competing-event path, using subject-level cumulative products and
then population means. That code provides a concrete place to check the
within-period ordering, history alignment and target definition. It does not
settle whether observed censoring or competing-event assumptions are valid in
the proposed banking application.\cite{v131_sw_pygformula}

\section{Following an R forest operation into its C++ implementation}

For grf, the causal-forest binding assigns the same variable index to treatment
and instrument, then calls an instrumental predictor. The predictor factory
constructs \texttt{InstrumentalPredictionStrategy}. The native prediction uses
a ratio of centered outcome--instrument and treatment--instrument moments.
When instrument and treatment coincide, this corresponds to a weighted local
covariance divided by a weighted local treatment variance. This traced route
supports the interpretation of continuous-treatment output as a local slope
under its functional assumptions.\cite{v131_sw_grf}

It does not identify an arbitrary finite change in a nonlinear dose-response
curve. A change from an offer rate of one unit to two units needs the appropriate
counterfactual contrast and exposure support. A slope, an average slope and a
finite contrast can coincide in a linear model and diverge otherwise. The bank
must choose the target before comparing software outputs.

The native variance routine forms influence-like quantities across tree
groups, separates between-group variation from group noise and calls a Bayes
debiaser. These groups concern the forest's computation. They are distinct
from the observed borrower clusters used by the R average-effect calculation.
Inspecting both paths avoids the false inference that a tree-group variance
option automatically accounts for a persistent banking calendar. The debiaser,
forest sampling, serialization and numerical safeguards require qualification
before a direct native interface is admitted. Section~\ref{exec13:grf-adapter}
develops the selected native representation, variance-field and persistence
contracts; source inspection does not replace their runtime tests.\cite{v131_sw_grf}

The maintained R interface is therefore a reasonable first integration
candidate, subject to a complete license/dependency and behavioral review.
A direct C++ port would have to preserve the forest representation, prediction
strategy, variance method, randomization and exceptional outcomes across version
changes. Avoiding one language boundary does not by itself justify that
maintenance commitment. The open-source decision should compare the operational
cost of an R process or library bridge with the full scientific and technical
cost of a maintained port.

\section{Population averaging, support and unavailable combinations}

In grf's inspected all-population AIPW path, the mean is a weighted average of
\texttt{get\_scores} output. The variance calculation sums centered weighted
scores within the declared clusters, squares these group contributions and
applies a group-count correction. For binary treatment, the score uses the
usual propensity residual divided by $\widehat e(1-\widehat e)$. For continuous
treatment, an auxiliary regression forest estimates the conditional variance
of the treatment; the debiasing weight divides the treatment residual by that
estimate.\cite{v131_sw_grf}

Small conditional variance is an information problem. Borrowers with essentially
one available offer rate do not support precise estimation of a local rate
response simply because a forest can fit the outcome. Qualification should
retain weak-support cases and identify whether the operation returns a
warning, an extreme weight, an unavailable result or a misleading finite value.
The inspected formula alone supplies no finite-sample guarantee for such cases.

The all, treated, control and overlap populations must remain distinct. In the
overlap path the code fits a residualized outcome on a residualized treatment
and uses cluster or heteroskedastic covariance as applicable. Moving to an
overlap target may improve stability while changing which banking population
the result describes. A wrapper must not silently make that choice on the
analyst's behalf.\cite{v131_sw_grf}

Option support must be determined from reachable control flow. The inspected
average-effect routine rejects TMLE when clusters or sample weights are supplied
before reaching later formulas that contain cluster-related expressions. Seeing
those later formulas would not justify advertising clustered TMLE at this entry
point. Likewise, only specified combinations support continuous treatment.
The adapter's capability matrix needs explicit accepted combinations and
typed refusal for the others.\cite{v131_sw_grf}

\section{A generalized propensity score has physical units}

Let a continuous exposure follow a location-scale law
$A=\mu(X)+s(X)R$, with $s(X)>0$. Conditional change of variables gives
\[
 f_{A\mid X}(a\mid x)
 =\frac{1}{s(x)}f_{R\mid X}
       \left(\frac{a-\mu(x)}{s(x)}\middle|x\right).
\]
The Jacobian $1/s(x)$ is necessary for a density with respect to the original
exposure measure. If a common residual density is used instead of
$f_{R\mid X}$, an additional residual-distribution assumption is being made.

CausalGPS's inspected \texttt{compute\_resid} returns the standardized residual
$(a-b)/c$. Its \texttt{compute\_density} helper calls R's density estimate and
interpolates it with \texttt{rule=2}. In the inspected kernel branch of
\texttt{estimate\_gps}, the standardized-residual density is assigned to the
GPS field without division by the predicted scale in that branch. The normal
branch instead evaluates a normal density using its fitted mean and scale.
These observations establish a concrete scale question for downstream matching,
weighting and dose-response construction. Section~\ref{sec:exec24-dose-response-reuse}
traces the selected weighting ratio and outcome frontend. Its scale witness
narrows the outstanding question without qualifying every downstream operation.\cite{v13_sw_causalgps,v131_sw_causalgps}

At a standardized residual of zero, a standard normal density is about
$0.3989423$. Two strata with scales one and two have original-exposure densities
$0.3989423$ and $0.1994711$ at their respective means. Retaining only the common
standardized-residual value loses that difference. If the exposure is measured
in units one hundred times smaller, its numerical value is multiplied by one
hundred and the corresponding density must be divided by one hundred. The
probability of any physical exposure interval remains unchanged. These exact
transformations provide a reference for a future unit-consistency test.
\cite{v131_project_semantics}

Some downstream procedures might deliberately use a transformed balancing
quantity, while others require a density in the original units. The integration decision therefore remains conditional on a declared use of
the returned field and a justified interpretation of its scale. The selected
weighting path has been traced; its remaining scale and native-conformance
questions must be resolved before admission. Silently changing the helper
could alter package behavior without resolving the scientific contract. A
matched comparison should examine heterogeneous scales, near-zero scales,
counterfactual dose evaluation and an explicit unit conversion, retaining any
unsupported cases.

The causaldrf comparison has a separate source obligation. Its accompanying
license notice identifies the year and copyright holder, supplementing the
package's license declaration. That resolves the availability of that notice;
it does not settle transitive licensing or qualify its interval routines.
Section~\ref{sec:exec24-dose-response-reuse} develops the selected interval-index
and pointwise-versus-simultaneous restrictions, which remain part of the
proposed comparison. Source availability, permission to distribute and justified
uncertainty remain separate questions.\cite{v131_sw_causaldrf}

\section{Implications for reusable causal operations}

These examples support a common semantic contract with explicit graph
orientation, query/failure type, independent observational unit, decision clock,
target population, dose units and uncertainty construction. A business-facing
assistant can elicit these fields and explain unresolved choices, while a
deterministic validator checks the declared operation against its supported
combinations. An LLM's plausible description is not evidence that a package
uses the intended covariance or intervention target.

The relevant next qualification compares complete causal requests. It retains
the same estimand and information across packages, separates sampling from
Monte Carlo error, includes failed fits and preserves unbounded sets. Numerical
agreement in a benign case is useful evidence about implementation, but cannot
establish assignment truth, identification or useful precision in adverse
banking regimes. Those remain scientific and institutional requirements.


The commercial comparison that follows applies the same criteria to documented
vendor capabilities and to this proposal's actual evidence. A product feature
is useful only for a specified request; a proposed preserving interface is not
yet demonstrated superiority over an existing engine.

\chapter{Customer histories, heterogeneous effects and economic units}
\label{v131:histories-forests}

This chapter returns to the customer-level request after the network comparisons.
The earlier longitudinal, forest and dose studies supply the detailed methods;
the question here is what must remain unchanged when their outputs are reused.

examples retain those distinctions without treating a common interface as a
common estimand.

\section{Resampling a sequence requires a sampling model}

Consider a bank evaluating a sequence of servicing decisions over twelve
months. The data contain repeated observations of each borrower, interventions
that depend on previous balances and competing events such as account closure.
The statistical unit might be a borrower history, a household, a branch or an
independent economic calendar. These choices imply different resampling laws.
A routine with ``bootstrap'' in its name does not determine the appropriate law.

LiNGAM's generic bootstrap resamples rows and refits the model. VARLiNGAM has
a distinct path: it fits a lag model, applies a contemporaneous LiNGAM model to
the residuals, resamples residual vectors and reconstructs a sequence using the
fitted autoregressive coefficients. The inspected loop temporarily sets the
lag-selection criterion to \texttt{None}. Consequently, one must inspect the
initial lag/coefficient settings and the loop's refit behavior before claiming
that it propagates model-selection uncertainty. \cite{v131_sw_lingam}

Residual resampling can be a sensible candidate under an appropriate innovation
law. It does not automatically preserve persistent residual dependence,
unmodeled common shocks or a different sampling calendar. Row resampling is a
different candidate suitable for a different observational unit. A banking
comparison should include a correctly specified innovation model and an adverse
case with persistent residuals, preserving the uncertainty target and failures
in both. Bootstrap edge frequencies should not be reported as a calibrated
effect confidence region without an additional argument.

pygformula's inspected bootstrap draws observed subject identifiers with
replacement, copies each subject's complete history and assigns a fresh replicate
identifier to each draw. It updates histories and refits covariate and outcome
models. Expanding to the requested simulation population occurs in a separate
step. These operations distinguish the observed sampling unit from the Monte
Carlo population used to evaluate a fitted regime. \cite{v131_sw_pygformula}

The fresh identifiers matter. Drawing borrower 17 twice should produce two
bootstrap histories, not concatenate them into one impossible person with two
records at every date. An integration test needs duplicate draws, unequal
history lengths and multiple interventions. It must also preserve the original
calendar when that calendar is part of the estimand. Subject resampling alone
does not account for a market shock shared by every subject on the same date.

catches an exception, warns and returns a dictionary whose

inconsistency in that caller path. This observation requires reproduction in

\chapter{What language models contribute to causal knowledge}
\label{la:frontier}

Section~\ref{scisyn:assistance} gives the principal recommendation for language
assistance. This chapter develops its evidential basis. It first distinguishes
knowledge, formal reasoning, mechanism proposals and workflow support, then
asks how published evaluations transfer to a banking decision. Exact examples
show how task mixtures, shared errors and unresolved causal models can change
that decision. The final comparisons examine consistency judges, orchestration,
literature extraction and the design of a versioned assistance experiment.

\section{Four different questions about cause and effect}

A banker asking why deposit balances fell can be asking for an explanation of
a recorded event, an estimate of a feasible rate intervention, a prediction of
next month's balance, or a diagnosis of an observation error. A fluent answer
can move between these objects without announcing the change. Evaluating assistance therefore starts by distinguishing the task: a proposed scientific question, evidence about a causal model,
a formal calculation conditional on that model, or a recommendation under a
specified loss. Success on one task does not establish success on the others.

The early frontier argument proposes using language models to organize domain
knowledge, draft graphs, critique assumptions and suggest robustness analyses.
It also records the ability to reproduce recognizable public data and
distinguishes transforming known information from discovering a new causal
structure.\cite{v12_la_2305_00050} This distinction is particularly consequential
in banking. A familiar statement about interest rates can be useful prior
knowledge, but the effect of a particular bank's deposit offer depends on its
population, competitors, eligibility rules and information clock. A remembered
relationship does not determine that intervention effect.

Formal benchmarks introduce a second object. CLadder constructs questions from
known causal structures with different verbalizations. Its results concern
answers to those generated questions, including historically specified models
and prompting methods.\cite{v12_la_2312_04350} Such a benchmark can reveal failures
to distinguish observation from intervention. It cannot establish that a model
elicits the right variables from an unfamiliar bank process, measures them
correctly, or returns calibrated uncertainty after fitting to dependent data.
These are additional stages of the proposed product.

Third, a language model can propose a causal mechanism for numerical analysis.
Model Discovery Agent illustrates a separation between executable mechanism
proposals and numerical fitting, evidence approximation and experiment design.
Its finite predictive evaluations explicitly do not establish causal
identification.\cite{v12_la_2608_09696} A mechanism may predict well because
several observationally equivalent models predict equally well. The bank must
still justify which intervention the model represents and which new experiment
would distinguish economically different mechanisms.

Finally, workflow assistance concerns selection and coordination of established
operations. Causal-learn+ describes assistance with diagnosis, assumptions,
method selection and interpretation while retaining algorithm outputs and
graph ambiguity.\cite{v12_la_2606_23608} This is a useful architectural direction.
It changes the analyst's interaction with numerical tools; it does not make a
method's premises true. The comparisons that follow keep these four contributions
separate while studying how they can work together.

\section{Text supplies a different information channel}

Write $D$ for the observed numerical records, $K$ for inspected documentary or
expert evidence, and $\mathcal M(D,K)$ for the models consistent with the
declared interpretation of both. For target $\psi$, a set-valued answer is
\[
 \Psi(D,K)=\{\psi(M):M\in\mathcal M(D,K)\}.
\]
This notation does not assert that finite data identify the population law or
that a statistical confidence procedure has been supplied. It describes which
models the analysis intends to consider. Statistical uncertainty about the law
must subsequently be propagated through the model set.

Additional reliable knowledge may exclude a model that the observed distribution
alone cannot exclude. A contract establishing that an invitation was randomized,
for example, has a different evidential role from a predictive correlation.
But a model-generated sentence repeating that randomization is common practice
does not establish what happened in the bank's historical process. The analysis
must identify the original source, the relevant population and dates, the
interpretation of its claim, and the person or measurement that supports it.

This also explains why retrieving more documents need not improve discovery.
LACR combines background knowledge, retrieved documents and optional numerical
information, and includes an UNKNOWN response. Its reported retrieval effects
differ across benchmarks, with adverse as well as favorable outcomes.
\cite{v12_la_2402_15301} Retrieval changes $K$; it does not certify $K$. Documents
may concern a different treatment definition, contain an association stated as
a cause, or duplicate the same original assertion. Ten repeated documents are
not ten independent confirmations of an edge.

An appropriate evidence object therefore retains the claim, source passage,
date, domain, units and proposed role. A passage may justify a variable
definition without justifying an arrow. A process document may establish that
one action occurs before another without excluding a common cause. A source
about another bank may suggest a hypothesis while leaving transport assumptions
unresolved. These roles determine the strength with which $K$ can restrict the
model class.

\section{Discovery methods use language judgments in different ways}

Three broad routes recur in the inspected literature: direct graph or relation
prediction, refinement of numerical discoveries, and priors or constraints used
within a search.\cite{v12_la_2402_11068} The distinction matters because it locates
where a wrong assertion enters the calculation.

In direct conditional-independence elicitation, chatPC obtains language-model
judgments from descriptions and context. Its statistical calculation concerns
the proportion of YES/NO model responses.\cite{v12_la_2406_07378} Repeated answers
can measure response variability under a prompt. Without a separate argument,
they are not repeated draws of the bank variables and do not yield a sampling
test of independence in the bank population. A highly stable wrong answer can
therefore be more dangerous than a visibly variable one.

Soft guidance provides a different failure boundary. The inspected CD-UCT
method combines language and mutual-information scores to guide graph search
without excluding otherwise valid DAGs. Language-only priors are not uniformly
beneficial in its reported comparisons.\cite{v12_la_2405_13551} Ancestral-path
constraints can likewise enter through a soft log-prior penalty, with reported
degradation under inaccurate prior information.\cite{v12_la_2306_16902} Softness
leaves room for the numerical criterion to resist the suggestion, but it does
not establish that the final graph probabilities are calibrated.

Hard restrictions can be scientifically appropriate when backed by a genuine
design fact. They are more consequential when inferred from prose: deleting a
candidate model deletes every effect value that only that model permits.
Statistical Causal Prompting converts model outputs into forced, forbidden or
unknown prior knowledge using method-specific mappings. The inspected examples
include failures as well as improvements.\cite{v12_la_2402_01454} The interface
must expose both the original assertion and the conversion rule, so a reviewer
can determine whether a numerical threshold has quietly become a scientific
exclusion.

Noisy language priors can also guide a sequential allocation of questions over
edges while retaining PAG representations.\cite{v12_la_2506_16234} This is closer
to a budgeted information problem than to asking for a finished graph in one
prompt. Its relevance to a bank still depends on whether the supplied knowledge
applies to the observed regime, whether latent structure is represented
correctly, and whether the retained ambiguity survives into the effect query.

\section{Temporal discovery is not a change of vocabulary}

A statement that collections activity affects arrears omits the action time,
available history, response horizon and possible feedback. Expanding a variable
name into a paragraph does not supply these missing indices. A temporal graph
needs explicit time labels and a rule governing contemporaneous edges, lag
limits, hidden histories, stationarity and interventions.

RealTCD combines a language-derived initial adjacency with numerical score
optimization over temporal graphs and intervention targets. Its setup includes
causal sufficiency, a known observational regime, finite lag and a DAG on
unrolled variables; its identification statement has further stated premises.
The inspected real-system assessment lacks a ground-truth DAG and evaluates

\chapter{What language models contribute to causal knowledge}
\label{la:frontier}

Section~\ref{scisyn:assistance} gives the principal recommendation for language
assistance. This chapter develops its evidential basis. It first distinguishes
knowledge, formal reasoning, mechanism proposals and workflow support, then
asks how published evaluations transfer to a banking decision. Exact examples
show how task mixtures, shared errors and unresolved causal models can change
that decision. The final comparisons examine consistency judges, orchestration,
literature extraction and the design of a versioned assistance experiment.

\section{Four different questions about cause and effect}

A banker asking why deposit balances fell can be asking for an explanation of
a recorded event, an estimate of a feasible rate intervention, a prediction of
next month's balance, or a diagnosis of an observation error. A fluent answer
can move between these objects without announcing the change. Evaluating assistance therefore starts by distinguishing the task: a proposed scientific question, evidence about a causal model,
a formal calculation conditional on that model, or a recommendation under a
specified loss. Success on one task does not establish success on the others.

The early frontier argument proposes using language models to organize domain
knowledge, draft graphs, critique assumptions and suggest robustness analyses.
It also records the ability to reproduce recognizable public data and
distinguishes transforming known information from discovering a new causal
structure. \cite{v12_la_2305_00050} This distinction is particularly consequential
in banking. A familiar statement about interest rates can be useful prior
knowledge, but the effect of a particular bank's deposit offer depends on its
population, competitors, eligibility rules and information clock. A remembered
relationship does not determine that intervention effect.

Formal benchmarks introduce a second object. CLadder constructs questions from
known causal structures with different verbalizations. Its results concern
answers to those generated questions, including historically specified models
and prompting methods. \cite{v12_la_2312_04350} Such a benchmark can reveal failures
to distinguish observation from intervention. It cannot establish that a model
elicits the right variables from an unfamiliar bank process, measures them
correctly, or returns calibrated uncertainty after fitting to dependent data.
These are additional stages of the proposed product.

Third, a language model can propose a causal mechanism for numerical analysis.
Model Discovery Agent illustrates a separation between executable mechanism
proposals and numerical fitting, evidence approximation and experiment design.
Its finite predictive evaluations explicitly do not establish causal
identification. \cite{v12_la_2608_09696} A mechanism may predict well because
several observationally equivalent models predict equally well. The bank must
still justify which intervention the model represents and which new experiment
would distinguish economically different mechanisms.

Finally, workflow assistance concerns selection and coordination of established
operations. Causal-learn+ describes assistance with diagnosis, assumptions,
method selection and interpretation while retaining algorithm outputs and
graph ambiguity. \cite{v12_la_2606_23608} This is a useful architectural direction.
It changes the analyst's interaction with numerical tools; it does not make a
method's premises true. The comparisons that follow keep these four contributions
separate while studying how they can work together.

\section{Text supplies a different information channel}

Write $D$ for the observed numerical records, $K$ for inspected documentary or
expert evidence, and $\mathcal M(D,K)$ for the models consistent with the
declared interpretation of both. For target $\psi$, a set-valued answer is
\[
 \Psi(D,K)=\{\psi(M):M\in\mathcal M(D,K)\}.
\]
This notation does not assert that finite data identify the population law or
that a statistical confidence procedure has been supplied. It describes which
models the analysis intends to consider. Statistical uncertainty about the law
must subsequently be propagated through the model set.

Additional reliable knowledge may exclude a model that the observed distribution
alone cannot exclude. A contract establishing that an invitation was randomized,
for example, has a different evidential role from a predictive correlation.
But a model-generated sentence repeating that randomization is common practice
does not establish what happened in the bank's historical process. The analysis
must identify the original source, the relevant population and dates, the
interpretation of its claim, and the person or measurement that supports it.

This also explains why retrieving more documents need not improve discovery.
LACR combines background knowledge, retrieved documents and optional numerical
information, and includes an UNKNOWN response. Its reported retrieval effects
differ across benchmarks, with adverse as well as favorable outcomes.
\cite{v12_la_2402_15301} Retrieval changes $K$; it does not certify $K$. Documents
may concern a different treatment definition, contain an association stated as
a cause, or duplicate the same original assertion. Ten repeated documents are
not ten independent confirmations of an edge.

An appropriate evidence object therefore retains the claim, source passage,
date, domain, units and proposed role. A passage may justify a variable
definition without justifying an arrow. A process document may establish that
one action occurs before another without excluding a common cause. A source
about another bank may suggest a hypothesis while leaving transport assumptions
unresolved. These roles determine the strength with which $K$ can restrict the
model class.

\section{Discovery methods use language judgments in different ways}

Three broad routes recur in the inspected literature: direct graph or relation
prediction, refinement of numerical discoveries, and priors or constraints used

where a wrong assertion enters the calculation.

In direct conditional-independence elicitation, chatPC obtains language-model
judgments from descriptions and context. Its statistical calculation concerns

can measure response variability under a prompt. Without a separate argument,
they are not repeated draws of the bank variables and do not yield a sampling
test of independence in the bank population. A highly stable wrong answer can
therefore be more dangerous than a visibly variable one.

method combines language and mutual-information scores to guide graph search

beneficial in its reported comparisons. \cite{v12_la_2405_13551} Ancestral-path
constraints can likewise enter through a soft log-prior penalty, with reported
degradation under inaccurate prior information. \cite{v12_la_2306_16902} Softness

not establish that the final graph probabilities are calibrated.

applies to the observed regime, whether latent structure is represented
correctly, and whether the retained ambiguity survives into the effect query.

\chapter{Translating a banking decision into a causal question}
\label{la:translation}

The preceding evidence review leaves a practical starting point: assistance
must preserve the question before it can improve an answer. This chapter
builds that question from population, action, outcome, loss and information
time. Incentive and servicing examples expose common substitutions; a
literature-graph study separates extracted claims from hypotheses; the
formulation workflow then leads to robust population comparisons and goal
clarification. Together these treatments explain which commitments an analyst
must resolve and which alternatives an assistant must retain.

\section{A business sentence can contain several questions}

``Should we increase the deposit offer?'' sounds like a single question, but
it leaves several choices unresolved. The intended action could be a change
in the quoted rate, the eligibility rule, the message shown to a customer or
the allocation of a fixed promotional budget. The outcome could be a new
deposit, retained balances, funding cost or total relationship value. The
population could be existing customers, applicants who received an offer or
everyone eligible under a proposed rule. Each choice defines a different
causal problem.

A language assistant can expose these alternatives and organize the evidence
needed to resolve them. It should not choose the easiest target to estimate
and silently treat that target as the owner's decision. In the project funding
case, the response of balances to a 25-basis-point increase and the change in
net funding cost over thirty days are retained as separate candidates. Their
business motivation is shared; their outcomes and decision consequences are
not identical. The unresolved choice is useful information, not a failure
that must be hidden by returning a number.

The co-pilot roadmap discussed by Alaa and colleagues motivates this progression
from a scientific question through assumptions, statistical targets and
interpretation. Their illustrative medical examples attend to eligibility,
baseline time, treatment and follow-up. The inspected paper also reports that
generic uncued answers can omit relevant design concerns. Applying those
principles to banking is a project proposal; the medical examples do not
validate banking clocks or interventions.\cite{v12_la_2407_19118}

\section{A question as a collection of commitments}

The project represents a question as
\begin{equation}
 Q=(\mathcal U,P,\mathcal A,\pi,\pi_0,Y,H,\nu,\ell,\mathcal I).
 \label{la:question}
\end{equation}
Here \(\mathcal U\) is the unit of analysis; \(P\) is the target population;
\(\mathcal A\) is the feasible action set; \(\pi\) and \(\pi_0\) are the
policy and comparator; \(Y\) is the outcome; \(H\) is the horizon; \(\nu\)
is the measure used to average over the population; \(\ell\) is the loss,
including its units; and \(\mathcal I\) specifies information available at
each action. This notation defines the project's declaration contract. It is
not an identification theorem.

The unit needs particular care. An account can be an observation while a
customer is the decision unit and a household is the unit within which actions
interact. An assistant can ask which role each identifier plays, but a column
called customer ID does not certify ownership or stable linkage. If several
accounts share a budget or pricing rule, an account-level action may also be
an infeasible description of the intervention. The feasible action set should
reflect what the responsible institution can actually change.

The comparator must be as explicit as the intervention. ``No treatment'' might
mean no new contact, continuation of the current contact policy, no rate
increase, or a different offer under a fixed budget. A dynamic policy can
include future actions conditional on history, so its comparator is also a
history-dependent rule. An effect relative to one comparator cannot be
reused for another solely because the same treatment variable appears in the
dataset.

The outcome and loss should also remain separate. A change in balances has
units of currency held over a horizon; funding expense combines balances,
rates and time. A larger deposit balance can have a positive acquisition
interpretation and an unfavorable net-cost implication. If \(g(a)\) is a
specified gross benefit and \(c(a)\) is a specified cost, the decision may
depend on \(E[g(a)-c(a)]\), not on \(E[g(a)]\) alone. The definitions and
valuation assumptions must be supplied before that subtraction is meaningful.
The assistant should make missing costs visible rather than invent prices.

\section{Changing a population measure changes the answer}

Let \(X\) denote baseline features and let
\(\tau(x)=E[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x]\). A weighted target can be written
\begin{equation}
 \theta_w=\frac{E[w(X)\tau(X)]}{E[w(X)]},\qquad E[w(X)]>0.
 \label{la:weighted-target}
\end{equation}
Uniform, treated-population, overlap and trimmed targets use different
weights. Under the conditions that make a propensity \(e(x)=\Pr(A=1\mid X=x)\)
appropriate for the intended population, familiar choices are \(1\),
\(e(x)\), \(e(x)(1-e(x))\) and
\(1\{a\leq e(x)\leq b\}\), respectively. The formula records which average
is wanted. It does not establish exchangeability, support, estimation rates
or coverage.

An exact project example makes the distinction visible. Let two strata have
equal population probability, with propensities \(0.2\) and \(0.5\), and
effects \(0\) and \(10\). Trimming to \([0.1,0.9]\) keeps both strata, so
the trimmed-population effect is \(5\). Overlap weights are \(0.16\) and
\(0.25\), giving
\[
 \theta_{\mathrm{overlap}}=
 \frac{0.16(0)+0.25(10)}{0.16+0.25}=\frac{250}{41}
 =6.09756\ldots.
\]
Both calculations can be exact and still answer different questions. A label
such as ``overlap population'' is insufficient if its underlying weighting
rule is not retained.

This issue is directly relevant to the inspected OCI agent paper. Chou and
colleagues describe a principal/actor/critic workflow, reproducible notebooks,
point-in-time estimation and overlap diagnostics. The inspected trimming
passage uses a target label that must be reconciled with the actual weighting
rule before mapping it to conventional overlap weighting. The proposed
architecture is informative, but an assistant should not inherit a target
label without checking its definition.\cite{v12_la_2607_22443}

Changing the target to remove unsupported accounts can be scientifically
reasonable, but it is a new decision question. A bank owner may care about
precisely those accounts for which treatment support is weak. An honest report
can say that a narrower target is estimable under the supplied assumptions
while the original target remains unresolved. It should show the excluded
population, the new averaging rule and the implications for the decision.

\section{Information is governed by an availability clock}

The date on which an event occurred differs from the date on which an analyst
or policy could observe it. For a recorded variable \(V\), write \(e_V\) for
event time and \(a_V\) for availability time. The finite project fixtures
require \(e_V\leq a_V\), and a policy acting at time \(t\) can use the value
only if \(a_V\leq t\). A derived feature becomes available no earlier than
its required inputs. These rules prevent an apparently historical feature
from leaking future information into a decision.

In the servicing fixture, an account condition occurs at day ten but becomes
available at day eleven. A rule acting on day eleven may use it; a rule acting
on day ten may not. The distinction matters even when both values later appear
in the same warehouse table. A language assistant should request the recording
and availability convention, rather than infer it from a field name or a
sorted timestamp.

Advance announcements and forecasts require different variable definitions.
A forecast observed today of next month's condition is a current forecast
variable, not a measurement of a future realized condition with an impossible
availability time. Revised historical data similarly require a vintage or
revision convention. The project's finite validator does not implement every
revision protocol. It checks the stated recorded-value contract and leaves
more complex clocks as explicit extensions.

Equal timestamps do not determine direction. Two columns aggregated to the
same day may hide a finer action sequence or a common cause. The assistant
can propose a finer clock and identify the evidence needed to support it.
It cannot establish temporal precedence by placing one variable first in a
diagram. When the granularity is insufficient, the ambiguity should survive
into the model class.

\section{An available covariate is not automatically an adjustment variable}

In a sequential servicing model, \(A_0\) changes an intermediate condition
\(L_1\), which affects both a later action \(A_1\) and the outcome \(Y\).
The same \(L_1\) is a mediator for the first action and a common cause of the
second action--outcome relation. Its appropriate use depends on the target.
Including every available column in one regression does not preserve all
possible total, direct and policy effects.

The project declaration therefore distinguishes a policy-history purpose
from an ordinary adjustment purpose. A simple directed-path diagnostic flags
a post-treatment descendant proposed as an ordinary total-effect control.
It does not declare all post-treatment conditioning invalid. Controlled
direct effects and longitudinal procedures need their own question and
formal analysis. A warning from a declaration validator is not a replacement
for an adjustment criterion or an identification algorithm.

Observation processes can alter the target in a similar way. Suppose only
successfully linked records enter an analysis and both action and repayment
affect successful linkage. The selection indicator is part of the causal
problem, and an effect among linked records may differ from an effect in the
original population. A record-link score is an observed proxy; it is not
verified ownership. The observation fixture deliberately retains a latent
ownership variable, a selection node and an unresolved population choice.

CausalDS provides a useful literature distinction here: its conceptual SCM
variables and its separate observation model are not interchangeable. The
paper's narrated synthetic scenes can test how an agent handles that
distinction, but they do not supply authentic banking semantic or assignment
truth.\cite{v12_la_2607_08093}

\section{The handoff to formal analysis}

The assistant's useful output is a reviewable declaration and a record of
what remains unresolved. A selected declaration contains one explicit target,
its population measure, the intervention and comparator, clocks, feasible
actions, outcome and loss. An ambiguous declaration retains candidate targets
without covertly selecting one. A contradicted assumption cannot be left as
an inconsequential note while the calculation proceeds as if it held.

The local project validator exercises these distinctions with four synthetic
banking cases and adverse contract tests. It checks declared identities,
types, references and selected clock/graph conditions. It does not authenticate
an institution, certify a reviewer, determine whether a causal assumption is
true, or implement every MAG/PAG/CPDAG validity condition. A declaration ready
for formal analysis is ready for the next conditional operation, not a
qualified bank recommendation.

This boundary also explains the limited scope of the executable operation
tested with these declaration fixtures. A declaration can describe a dynamic
regime while that selected operation supports only a static binary population
ATE. The correct handoff then reports unsupported target mapping. Later
fitted-summary and servicing studies have their own declared regimes; their
existence does not qualify this particular mapping. Translating that request into a
static regression would produce a result at the cost of changing the user's
question. The appropriate remedy is to qualify a longitudinal operation or
obtain an explicit new target decision, with the original question preserved.

\(\tau(x)=E[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x]\). A weighted target can be written
\begin{equation}
 \theta_w=\frac{E[w(X)\tau(X)]}{E[w(X)]},\qquad E[w(X)]>0.
 \label{la:weighted-target}
\end{equation}
Uniform, treated-population, overlap and trimmed targets use different
weights. Under the conditions that make a propensity \(e(x)=\Pr(A=1\mid X=x)\)
appropriate for the intended population, familiar choices are \(1\),
\(e(x)\), \(e(x)(1-e(x))\) and
\(1\{a\leq e(x)\leq b\}\), respectively. The formula records which average
is wanted. It does not establish exchangeability, support, estimation rates
or coverage.

An exact project example makes the distinction visible. Let two strata have
equal population probability, with propensities \(0.2\) and \(0.5\), and
effects \(0\) and \(10\). Trimming to \([0.1,0.9]\) keeps both strata, so
the trimmed-population effect is \(5\). Overlap weights are \(0.16\) and
\(0.25\), giving
\[
 \theta_{\mathrm{overlap}}=
 \frac{0.16(0)+0.25(10)}{0.16+0.25}=\frac{250}{41}
 =6.09756\ldots.
\]
Both calculations can be exact and still answer different questions. A label
such as ``overlap population'' is insufficient if its underlying weighting
rule is not retained.

This issue is directly relevant to the inspected OCI agent paper. Chou and
colleagues describe a principal/actor/critic workflow, reproducible notebooks,
point-in-time estimation and overlap diagnostics. The inspected trimming
passage uses a target label that must be reconciled with the actual weighting
rule before mapping it to conventional overlap weighting. The proposed
architecture is informative, but an assistant should not inherit a target
label without checking its definition. \cite{v12_la_2607_22443}

Changing the target to remove unsupported accounts can be scientifically
reasonable, but it is a new decision question. A bank owner may care about
precisely those accounts for which treatment support is weak. An honest report
can say that a narrower target is estimable under the supplied assumptions
while the original target remains unresolved. It should show the excluded
population, the new averaging rule and the implications for the decision.

\section{Information is governed by an availability clock}

The date on which an event occurred differs from the date on which an analyst
or policy could observe it. For a recorded variable \(V\), write \(e_V\) for
event time and \(a_V\) for availability time. The finite project fixtures
require \(e_V\leq a_V\), and a policy acting at time \(t\) can use the value
only if \(a_V\leq t\). A derived feature becomes available no earlier than
its required inputs. These rules prevent an apparently historical feature
from leaking future information into a decision.

In the servicing fixture, an account condition occurs at day ten but becomes
available at day eleven. A rule acting on day eleven may use it; a rule acting
on day ten may not. The distinction matters even when both values later appear
in the same warehouse table. A language assistant should request the recording
and availability convention, rather than infer it from a field name or a
sorted timestamp.

Advance announcements and forecasts require different variable definitions.
A forecast observed today of next month's condition is a current forecast
variable, not a measurement of a future realized condition with an impossible
availability time. Revised historical data similarly require a vintage or
revision convention. The project's finite validator does not implement every
revision protocol. It checks the stated recorded-value contract and leaves
more complex clocks as explicit extensions.

Equal timestamps do not determine direction. Two columns aggregated to the
same day may hide a finer action sequence or a common cause. The assistant
can propose a finer clock and identify the evidence needed to support it.
It cannot establish temporal precedence by placing one variable first in a
diagram. When the granularity is insufficient, the ambiguity should survive
into the model class.

\section{An available covariate is not automatically an adjustment variable}

In a sequential servicing model, \(A_0\) changes an intermediate condition
\(L_1\), which affects both a later action \(A_1\) and the outcome \(Y\).
The same \(L_1\) is a mediator for the first action and a common cause of the
second action--outcome relation. Its appropriate use depends on the target.
Including every available column in one regression does not preserve all
possible total, direct and policy effects.

The project declaration therefore distinguishes a policy-history purpose
from an ordinary adjustment purpose. A simple directed-path diagnostic flags
a post-treatment descendant proposed as an ordinary total-effect control.
It does not declare all post-treatment conditioning invalid. Controlled
direct effects and longitudinal procedures need their own question and
formal analysis. A warning from a declaration validator is not a replacement
for an adjustment criterion or an identification algorithm.

Observation processes can alter the target in a similar way. Suppose only
successfully linked records enter an analysis and both action and repayment
affect successful linkage. The selection indicator is part of the causal
problem, and an effect among linked records may differ from an effect in the
original population. A record-link score is an observed proxy; it is not
verified ownership. The observation fixture deliberately retains a latent
ownership variable, a selection node and an unresolved population choice.

CausalDS provides a useful literature distinction here: its conceptual SCM
variables and its separate observation model are not interchangeable. The
paper's narrated synthetic scenes can test how an agent handles that
distinction, but they do not supply authentic banking semantic or assignment
truth. \cite{v12_la_2607_08093}

\section{The handoff to formal analysis}

The assistant's useful output is a reviewable declaration and a record of
what remains unresolved. A selected declaration contains one explicit target,
its population measure, the intervention and comparator, clocks, feasible
actions, outcome and loss. An ambiguous declaration retains candidate targets
without covertly selecting one. A contradicted assumption cannot be left as
an inconsequential note while the calculation proceeds as if it held.

The local project validator exercises these distinctions with four synthetic
banking cases and adverse contract tests. It checks declared identities,
types, references and selected clock/graph conditions. It does not authenticate
an institution, certify a reviewer, determine whether a causal assumption is
true, or implement every MAG/PAG/CPDAG validity condition. A declaration ready
for formal analysis is ready for the next conditional operation, not a
qualified bank recommendation.

This boundary also explains the limited scope of the executable operation
tested with these declaration fixtures. A declaration can describe a dynamic
regime while that selected operation supports only a static binary population
ATE. The correct handoff then reports unsupported target mapping. Later
fitted-summary and servicing studies have their own declared regimes; their
existence does not qualify this particular mapping. Translating that request into a
static regression would produce a result at the cost of changing the user's
question. The appropriate remedy is to qualify a longitudinal operation or
obtain an explicit new target decision, with the original question preserved.

\section{A complete translation example: the incentive question}
\label{v13:la-dose}

Suppose a manager asks an agent to ``find the incentive uplift and choose the
best offer.'' The sentence leaves at least three mathematical objects open:
a binary offer effect, a continuous local slope, and a finite-dose policy value.
The agent can help by presenting these alternatives with their populations,
units and action constraints. It should not select whichever object happens
to be exposed by the first available package.

Let $A$ be incentive intensity in a declared unit and let $Y$ be retained net
value over a fixed horizon. The finite question is
$\Delta(a_1,a_0)=\mathbb E\{Y(a_1)-Y(a_0)\}$. A local derivative, where it
exists, is $\mu'(a)$. A covariance slope averages features of the response
under an exposure distribution and need not equal either object. The inspected
grf and dose-response interfaces make this a practical interoperability issue,
not merely a linguistic distinction.\cite{v13_sw_grf,v13_sw_causaldrf}

For the stipulated curve $\mu(a)=20a-3a^2$, a uniform exposure on $[0,2]$
gives covariance slope 14, while moving from dose one to dose two changes the
mean by 11 CNY. An agent that labels 14 as the value of the specified change
has mistranslated the problem even if it calls its numerical tool correctly.
The exact project calculation makes the error detectable without a live model
experiment.\cite{v13_project_exact}

A useful translation record would therefore state: eligible existing customers;
the information available before the offer; current dose one and feasible dose
two; a fixed retention horizon; treatment and outcome currency units; and
whether incentive expense is already included in $Y$. If expense is excluded,
the decision value is $\Delta(a_1,a_0)-\{c(a_1)-c(a_0)\}$. Subtracting it again
when $Y$ already measures net value would double-count cost. The record also
needs account closure/default definitions and a sampling unit for uncertainty.

The agent's role can be useful at each handoff. It can flag unspecified units,
find source definitions, propose alternative causal questions and generate
typed requests. Formal checks can verify that a numerical result matches the
declared query. Domain owners must still confirm the feasible intervention and
measurement meanings; neither fluent prose nor a schema establishes them.

\section{A servicing policy is a rule with an information boundary}

For sequential servicing, an action rule uses $H_t$, the information actually
available at decision time. A data field recorded later may describe an earlier
event while remaining unavailable to the operating policy. An agent assembling
history features must preserve both event and availability times. Otherwise
the proposed policy uses information the bank would not possess when acting.

The causal query should distinguish evaluating a specified rule, choosing among
rules and claiming an optimal hidden-state policy. A longitudinal simulator can
evaluate supplied regimes under its assumptions. Its ability to accept a custom
history function does not identify private customer states or make an unknown
logger known. The inspected pygformula class exposes useful histories, event
and regime options, but its source interface alone establishes neither policy
optimality nor uncertainty under arbitrary dependence.\cite{v13_sw_pygformula}

A concrete policy-selection hazard can be shown without an asymptotic argument.
Suppose two equally valuable policies each have independent evaluation error
equal to minus one or plus one with equal probability. The maximum of the two
errors is minus one only when both are minus one, and plus one otherwise.
Its expectation is therefore $\tfrac34-\tfrac14=\tfrac12$. Reporting the
selected policy's same-data evaluation is optimistic. If the selected policy
is evaluated with a fresh independent error of mean zero, the evaluation error
has mean zero conditional on the selection. Exact enumeration verifies both
claims.\cite{v13_project_exact}

This example does not prove that a particular split is sufficient for a
dependent servicing panel. It explains why the selection and evaluation laws
must be specified. An agent can preserve the split, freeze candidate rules and
refuse reuse of a held-out set for tuning. A scientific argument must still
justify independence or the required dependence control. Training a policy
and then narrating its favorable development score is not an independent
evaluation.

\section{Translation outputs that deserve abstention}

Some business questions should produce a request for more information or a set
of alternatives. If ``the customer'' may mean the legal entity, the beneficial
owner or a linked household, choosing one silently changes both the population
and interference structure. If the intended action is not operationally
feasible, the mathematically optimal action is irrelevant. If the loss function
and costs are unknown, the agent can compare statistical targets but cannot
assert an investment recommendation.

Abstention should be specific. It should identify the missing definition,
record the alternative interpretations and explain which downstream operation
depends on the answer. That is different from a generic refusal to analyze.
For an incentive query, the missing item may be treatment units or whether
cost is already included. For servicing it may be the information clock or
the policy class. For interference it may be network direction or the allocation
policy. These are concrete commitments that owners can resolve and numerical
tools can then preserve.

\chapter{Variables, diagrams and justified disagreement}
\label{la:diagrams}

The preceding chapter established what definitions and fallible evidence can
contribute. Here those objects enter a reviewable diagram. The argument first
separates graph classes, premises and retrieval outcomes, then develops exact
proxy, collider, clock and disagreement examples. The ontology comparison
connects the diagram to implementable treatment versions and source records.
The final restrictions study follows a premise through both graph and effect
sets, showing why a smaller graph class need not settle the decision.

\section{From vocabulary to measured variables}

A useful causal diagram begins with variables whose meanings can survive
contact with data. A business glossary may contain ``risk,'' ``relationship''
and ``engagement,'' while a dataset contains a risk-score vintage, a set of
linked accounts and an observed click. Those are related concepts, but they
are not interchangeable causal variables. An assistant can propose mappings,
detect inconsistent names and assemble definitions. Each proposed mapping
still needs an operational meaning, a unit and an information clock.

OntoLearner offers relevant modular ideas for ontology loading, typing,
taxonomy and relation-learning tasks. The inspected paper reports
domain-dependent errors and retrieval failures. Its relation-learning
capability is not a guarantee that a relation is causal, or that a concept
has a valid measured proxy in the bank. Ontology alignment should therefore
precede and inform graph construction without being silently promoted into
causal identification.\cite{v12_la_2607_01977}

For example, ``customer owns account'' may describe a legal relation,
``records share an identifier'' an administrative relation, and ``records
have a high linkage score'' a model output. If ownership affects both offer
eligibility and repayment behavior, substituting the linkage score for
ownership leaves a measurement problem. Adding an arrow from the score to
repayment does not resolve it. The diagram should distinguish latent
ownership, observed records, the linkage procedure and sample selection.

Likewise, an ordinal description such as ``high influence'' cannot be used
as an effect size without a scale. An assistant's rating of a proposed edge
may express a preference among textual explanations. It is not automatically
a probability that the edge is present, a posterior over graphs, or a
confidence level. A typed diagram can retain such a rating as explicitly
uncalibrated metadata while refusing to use it as scientific evidence.

\section{What an edge asserts}

An edge proposal should state more than two variable names. The endpoint
marks identify the proposed graphical object. A source and inspected anchor
state what supports the proposal. A scope describes the population, period
and intervention to which that evidence applies. A counterevidence record
states whether contrary evidence was found, absent in the inspected material,
or not successfully searched. A review disposition records acceptance as a
premise, rejection, or unresolved status.

These fields serve different purposes. A source can be authentic but
inapplicable to the current banking action. A study can concern a different
population or a different definition of treatment. A plausible timing argument
can constrain direction without establishing that any causal connection
exists. The assistant should make the supported proposition as narrow as
the evidence warrants and retain the reasons for disagreement.

CausalChat supplies an example of interactive model development: the inspected
paper combines optional CPDAG discovery, model suggestions, graph editing
and structural-equation coefficient updates. Its prompts use ordinal
causal-significance ratings and ask for possible confounders and mediators.
These are useful interaction ideas. The paper's expert feedback also raises
missing citations and uncertainty about the quality of scientific evidence
provided by the model. A coefficient update after adding an edge cannot
establish that the edge itself is true.\cite{v12_la_2410_14146}

The proposed banking workflow retains the interaction but changes the
scientific handoff. An accepted premise is labeled as a premise with a
responsible review, not as a truth certified by the model. A model proposal
alone cannot remove an observationally compatible graph alternative. The
tool responsible for formal identification receives the complete reviewed
graph object and its restrictions, rather than a picture whose uncertainty
has disappeared in editing.

\section{Graph classes and collections of candidate models}

A CPDAG or PAG is a structured representation with its own interpretation.
A list of proposed DAGs is another object. A collection of edges marked
``possible'' is not automatically an enumeration of every combination of
those edges. Confusing these representations can silently exclude models
or include incompatible ones.

The project contract preserves a CPDAG or PAG directly when that is the
appropriate object, including circle endpoints. It also permits explicitly
listed candidate models. An edge marked possible within a candidate describes
the evidence status of that candidate's edge; it does not make all optional
edge combinations an exhaustive graph class. Downstream calculations must
know which interpretation applies.

An exact binary example shows the consequence of retaining alternatives.
In model \(F\), a binary offer \(A\) is Bernoulli with probability one half,
and response \(Y\) equals \(A\) with probability \(0.9\). In model \(R\),
\(Y\) is Bernoulli with probability one half, and \(A\) equals \(Y\) with
probability \(0.9\). Both models produce
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
 &Y=0&Y=1\\\hline
A=0&9/20&1/20\\
A=1&1/20&9/20
\end{array}.
\]
In \(F\), setting \(A\) from zero to one changes \(E[Y]\) by \(0.8\).
In \(R\), intervening on the equation for \(A\) leaves \(Y\) unchanged.
The two compatible constructions therefore imply the effect candidates
\(\{0,0.8\}\). A directional suggestion favoring \(F\) does not provide
new identifying information unless its underlying premise is independently
justified. These finite calculations are project constructions, not a
calibrated confidence set for a learned graph.

More generally, for a declared graph class \(\mathcal G\), one relevant
downstream object is
\begin{equation}
 \Theta(P,Q,\mathcal G)=\bigcup_{G\in\mathcal G}\Theta_G(P,Q),
 \label{la:graph-union}
\end{equation}
where \(\Theta_G(P,Q)\) contains effects compatible with distribution \(P\),
question \(Q\) and the model restrictions for \(G\). A nonidentified member
can make the union broad. A list of estimated points is not automatically
the whole union, and graph-selection uncertainty cannot be replaced with
ordinary coefficient uncertainty after selecting one member.

Equation~\eqref{la:graph-union} also clarifies what a disagreement review
should resolve. If two experts differ only on an edge that leaves the target
functional unchanged, that disagreement may be immaterial for the current
decision while still mattering for another target. If their graphs imply
different effect signs or feasibility, the conflict is decision-relevant.
The assistant can identify that consequence and prioritize the required
evidence. It should not average expert preferences into an unexplained graph.

\section{Retrieval failure and scientific disagreement}

An evidence assistant can fail to find a passage because the document is
unavailable, parsing failed, the query was poor, the retriever missed it, or
the passage is absent from the inspected document. These cases support
different statements. ``No passage was retrieved'' cannot by itself become
``the authors ignored the assumption,'' and neither statement establishes
that the assumption is false in the population.

The inspected ARGUS paper makes this distinction especially useful. It
audits reported evidence concerning DiD identifying assumptions and does
not claim to adjudicate causal truth. Its synthetic flaw study exhibits a
retrieval/abstention tradeoff, and its small human-label pilot reports an
in-sample calibration change that was not tested on unseen papers. These
observations motivate a banking evidence state that is separate from a
scientific risk judgment.\cite{v12_la_2609_30867}

The proposed record contains the source bytes, the query or retrieval
configuration, inspected anchors and the resulting narrow claim. If evidence
is missing, it records the missing step. If two sources conflict, it records
their populations, dates and definitions before treating the conflict as
substantive. The analyst can then determine whether the sources concern
different regimes or whether a genuine contradiction remains.

This process does not require pretending that every edge has a published
study behind it. Some causal premises depend on institutional facts: which
system sets a rate, when a policy becomes visible, how an audit was selected,
or which identifier establishes ownership. Those facts need an accountable
owner and authentic records. Literature retrieval can help formulate the
questions, but it cannot supply an institution's missing assignment truth.

\section{A reviewable editing sequence}

The proposed interaction starts with a question and variable definitions,
then records diagram alternatives. Each edit changes a declared object:
add or remove a variable, refine a clock, replace a proxy, propose an endpoint,
or accept a restriction. The edit retains its predecessor identity and
reason. A reviewer can therefore see whether an apparent improvement in
fit came from a new assumption, a different target, or an actual correction
of an error.

Formal checks can reject a directed cycle in a DAG, impossible declared
time order or an explicitly forbidden direction. They can flag mediator,
collider or common-ancestor patterns in the supported representation. Such
checks help maintain a coherent declaration but do not cover every graph
class or establish that an accepted edge is causally true. In particular,
a diagram with no syntax error can still omit an important common cause or
misrepresent the observation process.

The user should be able to retain an unresolved diagram and ask for analyses
conditional on several alternatives. A refusal to pick one graph can be the
scientifically correct output. The later discovery and identification
operations then need to report what changes across those alternatives and
what remains common. This makes uncertainty operational: it directs the
next information request rather than appearing only as a disclaimer after
a single confident answer.

The following constructions make that consequence explicit. They separate
observational equivalence from sampling precision, measured proxies from
confounders, and a graph edit from evidence that warrants it. Their monetary
comparisons then locate the disagreements worth investigating.

An exact binary example shows the consequence of retaining alternatives.
In model \(F\), a binary offer \(A\) is Bernoulli with probability one half,
and response \(Y\) equals \(A\) with probability \(0.9\). In model \(R\),
\(Y\) is Bernoulli with probability one half, and \(A\) equals \(Y\) with
probability \(0.9\). Both models produce
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
 &Y=0&Y=1\\\hline
A=0&9/20&1/20\\
A=1&1/20&9/20
\end{array}.
\]
In \(F\), setting \(A\) from zero to one changes \(E[Y]\) by \(0.8\).
In \(R\), intervening on the equation for \(A\) leaves \(Y\) unchanged.
The two compatible constructions therefore imply the effect candidates
\(\{0,0.8\}\). A directional suggestion favoring \(F\) does not provide
new identifying information unless its underlying premise is independently
justified. These finite calculations are project constructions, not a
calibrated confidence set for a learned graph.

More generally, for a declared graph class \(\mathcal G\), one relevant
downstream object is
\begin{equation}
 \Theta(P,Q,\mathcal G)=\bigcup_{G\in\mathcal G}\Theta_G(P,Q),
 \label{la:graph-union}
\end{equation}
where \(\Theta_G(P,Q)\) contains effects compatible with distribution \(P\),
question \(Q\) and the model restrictions for \(G\). A nonidentified member
can make the union broad. A list of estimated points is not automatically
the whole union, and graph-selection uncertainty cannot be replaced with
ordinary coefficient uncertainty after selecting one member.

Equation~\eqref{la:graph-union} also clarifies what a disagreement review
should resolve. If two experts differ only on an edge that leaves the target
functional unchanged, that disagreement may be immaterial for the current
decision while still mattering for another target. If their graphs imply
different effect signs or feasibility, the conflict is decision-relevant.
The assistant can identify that consequence and prioritize the required
evidence. It should not average expert preferences into an unexplained graph.

\section{Retrieval failure and scientific disagreement}

An evidence assistant can fail to find a passage because the document is
unavailable, parsing failed, the query was poor, the retriever missed it, or
the passage is absent from the inspected document. These cases support
different statements. ``No passage was retrieved'' cannot by itself become
``the authors ignored the assumption,'' and neither statement establishes
that the assumption is false in the population.

The inspected ARGUS paper makes this distinction especially useful. It
audits reported evidence concerning DiD identifying assumptions and does
not claim to adjudicate causal truth. Its synthetic flaw study exhibits a
retrieval/abstention tradeoff, and its small human-label pilot reports an
in-sample calibration change that was not tested on unseen papers. These
observations motivate a banking evidence state that is separate from a
scientific risk judgment. \cite{v12_la_2609_30867}

The proposed record contains the source bytes, the query or retrieval
configuration, inspected anchors and the resulting narrow claim. If evidence
is missing, it records the missing step. If two sources conflict, it records
their populations, dates and definitions before treating the conflict as
substantive. The analyst can then determine whether the sources concern
different regimes or whether a genuine contradiction remains.

This process does not require pretending that every edge has a published
study behind it. Some causal premises depend on institutional facts: which
system sets a rate, when a policy becomes visible, how an audit was selected,
or which identifier establishes ownership. Those facts need an accountable
owner and authentic records. Literature retrieval can help formulate the
questions, but it cannot supply an institution's missing assignment truth.

\section{A reviewable editing sequence}

The proposed interaction starts with a question and variable definitions,
then records diagram alternatives. Each edit changes a declared object:
add or remove a variable, refine a clock, replace a proxy, propose an endpoint,
or accept a restriction. The edit retains its predecessor identity and
reason. A reviewer can therefore see whether an apparent improvement in
fit came from a new assumption, a different target, or an actual correction
of an error.

Formal checks can reject a directed cycle in a DAG, impossible declared
time order or an explicitly forbidden direction. They can flag mediator,
collider or common-ancestor patterns in the supported representation. Such
checks help maintain a coherent declaration but do not cover every graph
class or establish that an accepted edge is causally true. In particular,
a diagram with no syntax error can still omit an important common cause or
misrepresent the observation process.

The user should be able to retain an unresolved diagram and ask for analyses
conditional on several alternatives. A refusal to pick one graph can be the
scientifically correct output. The later discovery and identification
operations then need to report what changes across those alternatives and
what remains common. This makes uncertainty operational: it directs the
next information request rather than appearing only as a disclaimer after
a single confident answer.

The following constructions make that consequence explicit. They separate
observational equivalence from sampling precision, measured proxies from
confounders, and a graph edit from evidence that warrants it. Their monetary
comparisons then locate the disagreements worth investigating.
