\section{Equal observed laws can imply different intervention answers}
\label{v13:la-equivalence}

A diagram assistant must recognize when available observations cannot determine
the requested direction or effect. Consider two project-constructed binary
models. Let $U$ be fair Bernoulli and $A=U$. In model one $Y=A$; in model two
$Y=U$. Both observed datasets contain only $(A,Y)=(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$ with equal
probability. Under an intervention setting $A=a$, model one has mean outcome
$a$ while model two has mean outcome $1/2$. Their average effects are one and
zero. Exact enumeration establishes the discrepancy.\cite{v13_project_exact}

Estimating the observed marginal propensity as $1/2$ does not solve the
problem: exchangeability given the available information is precisely what is
missing. A model that recognizes a plausible causal story may prefer one graph,
but that preference is not identification from these data. Expert knowledge,
measurements or experiments could distinguish the worlds; those inputs need
their own evidence and should remain visible in the result.

A continuous version shows why effect sets can be unbounded. Let independent
standard Gaussian variables $U$ and $\varepsilon$ generate
\[
 X=U,\qquad Y=bX-bU+\varepsilon.
\]
The factual law is $X=U,Y=\varepsilon$ for every real $b$. Under
$\operatorname{do}(X=x)$, however, the mean of $Y$ is $bx$. Therefore every
real intervention slope is compatible with the same observed distribution
within this allowed model class. More observations estimate that common law
more accurately; they do not select $b$. A discovery tool or language model
cannot remove this ambiguity without an additional restriction.

This is a useful evaluation case for agentic discovery. A high-quality response
retains the competing models, explains their observational equivalence and
identifies the information that could separate them. An overconfident single
graph should be scored as a substantive error even if its prose is convincing.
A refusal or whole-line effect set can be the scientifically correct output;
its lack of immediate decision usefulness should be reported separately.

\section{Prior knowledge needs a typed evidence record}

The inspected DirectLiNGAM interface distinguishes a directed path, no directed
path and unspecified prior knowledge. The y0 identification dispatcher requires
a supplied graph rather than eliciting its truth. These interfaces make the
translation from narrative evidence to formal restrictions consequential.
An agent saying ``A is likely relevant to Y'' has not supplied a justified
directed-path constraint.\cite{v13_sw_lingam,v13_sw_y0}

For each proposed restriction, a useful record distinguishes a temporal order,
an intervention mechanism, a measured association, a domain assertion and a
formal exclusion. It binds the variables, their measurement/availability clocks,
the source passage, the supporting scope and any disagreement. A source about
one population or intervention need not justify a hard exclusion in another.
The record should preserve which conclusions change if the assertion is removed.

Suppose a manager states that a rate change cannot be caused by next month's
withdrawal. That supports a temporal ordering when the rate decision was fixed
before the withdrawal. It does not rule out an earlier expectation of withdrawal
affecting the rate, or a common market shock affecting both. A diagram assistant
can expose the omitted expectation variable and the common-cause alternative.
It should not convert the temporal statement into unconfoundedness.

An analogous issue arises in network diagrams. MossSpider's selected source
uses a directed influence convention that requires explicit checking, while a
bank may draw arrows from guarantor to beneficiary. A language model can produce
the correct-looking graph but an incorrectly oriented adjacency representation.
A two-node semantic test with known distinct attributes is more informative
than a visual similarity score.\cite{v13_sw_mossspider}

\section{Set-valued reasoning should survive verbal reporting}

If uncertainty concerns several graphs or nuisance parameters, the effect
object may be a union of intervals. A project ratio example illustrates the
boundary. Let a numerator lie in $[1,2]$ and an audit multiplier in
$[-1/2,1/2]$, with the relation $m=r\theta$. Excluding division by zero while
retaining all feasible nonzero multipliers gives
\[
 \Theta=(-\infty,-2]\ \cup\ [2,\infty).
\]
The gap around zero and the unbounded tails are substantive. Replacing this
object by its hull loses the exclusion of zero; replacing it by a finite
interval loses compatible effects. A monetary transformation should be applied
to each component and preserve endpoint inclusion and infinite endpoints.

The agent should describe why the set is disconnected, what assumptions support
it and what information would make it more useful. It should not translate
``wide uncertainty'' into an invented central estimate. When both zero numerator
and zero multiplier remain jointly feasible, the effect can instead be the
whole real line. The distinction depends on the joint region, not just
separate point estimates.

This reasoning also separates model plausibility from sampling coverage. If a
joint confidence region contains the true observable and nuisance parameters,
its effect image contains the true effect on that event. The implication is
elementary; constructing the valid joint region under the bank's actual
dependence and audit law is the difficult statistical work. An agent can
propagate a supplied region faithfully. It cannot infer that its coverage is
valid merely because the downstream set arithmetic passed a test.

\section{Domain knowledge as evidence for a causal graph}
\label{exec22:domain-scope}

A collections manager considering a payment holiday needs to distinguish a
plausible story from an intervention that improves customer outcomes. A language
model may suggest that financial strain affects delinquency, that servicing
changes financial strain, and that earlier delinquency affects the servicing
offer. Each statement needs a population, a time index, a variable definition
and an evidential basis. Joining the three statements without those qualifications
can create a cycle whose meaning is unclear. A retrieval system can help locate
the underlying evidence, but a retrieved sentence does not by itself establish
an invariant structural mechanism. Two recent clinical studies make the promise
and the limitations of this assistance concrete.

\subsection{Graph elicitation and the meaning of completeness}
\label{exec22:domain-elicitation}

Aziz and Brookhart study a hypothetical comparison of statins with no treatment
for preventing cardiovascular disease. They run four prompting strategies on
GPT-4o and a zero-shot strategy on GPT-o1, with three separate conversations per
configuration. Two author reviewers assess consistency, acyclicity, source
accuracy, completeness and prompt adherence. This is a study of fifteen outputs
in one familiar clinical scenario, rather than an estimate of performance over
a population of banking questions. The original was published on 30 October
2025.\cite{exec22_domain_aziz}

Its completeness criterion asks whether the graph contains seven groups of
variables drawn from an ASCVD risk score. This is a useful check for conspicuous
omissions, but it does not validate the graph's arrows or establish that its
adjustment set identifies the statin effect. Predictors can have different causal
roles: a pretreatment common cause, a mediator and a selection variable cannot
be treated interchangeably simply because each predicts the outcome. In a bank,
a strong arrears predictor measured after a servicing offer may be an outcome
of that offer. Including it in a list is different from correctly deciding
whether to adjust for it.

Table 1 and the article's accompanying text report fourteen acyclic graphs and
seven graphs containing six of the seven criteria. The seven-of-fifteen count
does not support the abstract's ``more than half'' wording. Race is absent from
all fifteen outputs. That is a reproducible observation about the study's
criterion; it does not establish a universal requirement to insert a particular
attribute into every causal model. A social attribute's role needs an explicit
account of the processes it represents and the target population. Blindly
adding a variable to improve a checklist score could conceal the same scientific
problem as omitting it.\cite{exec22_domain_aziz,exec22_domain_reference}

The study also separates producing citations from producing reliable evidence.
One-shot outputs supply sources but include nonexistent references and incorrect
titles, dates or author details. Chain-of-thought outputs give explanations
without sources in all three runs. The GPT-o1 zero-shot configuration consistently
supplies references and code, yet one code output needs manual repair. Its third
run is described as supplying nine sources and then assessed using denominators
of six; the original outputs are needed before aggregating that run's citation
accuracy. The source assessments described in the paper use title and abstract
review, which is weaker than checking that primary methods and results support
a particular causal arrow.\cite{exec22_domain_aziz}

One instruction-based output contains arrows in both directions between statin
use and cholesterol. The authors correctly identify the need for temporally
indexed nodes if feedback is intended. The banking counterpart is
\(D_t\to A_t\to D_{t+1}\), where \(D_t\) is delinquency information available
before action \(A_t\). Collapsing \(D_t\) and \(D_{t+1}\) into a single
``delinquency'' node loses the information clock. A graph assistant should request
that missing distinction rather than silently reverse an arrow to satisfy a
syntactic check. The study supports a brainstorming and source-checking role;
it supplies no validation of a bank effect estimator.

\subsection{Retrieval helps under a particular reference and query}
\label{exec22:domain-retrieval}

Lin and colleagues combine language models, retrieval and observational discovery
for chronic low back pain. Their February 2026 medRxiv original is a preprint,
not a peer-reviewed result. They use baseline observations from 1,868 participants
and a fourteen-variable expert reference. Crucially, the authors explicitly state
that this reference contains cycles and is not a DAG. The reference was developed
from clinical expertise and a literature synthesis; it is a declared comparison
target, not observed intervention truth.\cite{exec22_domain_lin}

The three knowledge systems share Mistral 7B-Instruct v0.3. Ordinary retrieval
supplies document chunks selected by vector similarity. Knowledge-graph retrieval
extracts entities and relations, merges entities, forms communities and retrieves
entities, attached relations, community summaries and supporting text. The paper
describes 600-token chunks with 100-token overlap, an 8,000-token retrieval budget,
and a pipeline involving constrained extraction, a graph database and community
clustering. These are descriptions of the authors' system; they do not establish
that its dependencies are pinned, licensed for the proposed distribution or
operationally integrated here.\cite{exec22_domain_lin}

Both retrieval systems use the same source articles that the experts used to
construct the comparison graph. This is an informative test of reconstructing
an aligned body of knowledge. It does not measure performance when the literature
is incomplete, contradictory, selected by a different team, or independent of the
reference adjudicators. The authors discuss this alignment explicitly. Their
argument that the model predates publication of the expert graph also does not
by itself authenticate the model's training corpus or exclude related earlier
content. The appropriate extension is a deliberately held-out reference and
document design, not a declaration that contamination has been ruled out.

For the data component, the paper describes hill climbing with local generalized
linear models, BIC scores and 500 bootstrap samples. A thresholded consensus graph
forms the initial model. The system then combines its edges with the knowledge
system's proposals and asks a further direction question when both directions
are suggested. Plausibility, association, temporality and a direct causal query
are separate prompt conditions. Their relative performance matters as much as
the strongest result.\cite{exec22_domain_lin}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{p{0.48\linewidth}rr}
\hline
Reported configuration & F1 & Difference \\
\hline
Observational initial model & 0.396 & --- \\
Initial model plus LLM, plausibility & 0.636 & --- \\
Initial model plus ordinary retrieval, plausibility & 0.714 & --- \\
Initial model plus graph retrieval, plausibility & 0.745 & 0.031 over 0.714 \\
Graph retrieval alone after direction resolution & 0.737 & 0.008 below 0.745 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

These are displayed scores against the single expert graph. The improvement
from 0.396 to 0.745 is 0.349, but the extra gain over ordinary retrieval is 0.031,
and the gain from adding observational discovery to the strongest graph-retrieval
configuration is 0.008. None is a paired confidence interval or a measured return
on engineering effort. Before direction resolution, graph retrieval's plausibility
F1 is 0.602, below the LLM-only value of 0.627. After resolution the values are
0.737 and 0.636. In the final combined systems, ordinary retrieval exceeds graph
retrieval for association by 0.060 and for temporality by 0.130. A blanket ranking
of retrieval architectures would conceal these reversals.\cite{exec22_domain_lin,exec22_domain_reference}

The strongest combined configuration still reports FDR 0.360, meaning disagreement
among its predicted directed edges against this reference under the paper's
definition. It is not a certified probability that a proposed bank causal claim
is false. Small differences also deserve care: subtracting the printed 0.396
from 0.636 gives 0.240, whereas Table 5 prints a change of 0.241. Rounding of
unreported underlying values can explain that discrepancy. It supplies a reason
to recover the original edge records, not a reason to invent corrected results.

\subsection{Direct edges, indirect effects and feedback need different objects}
\label{exec22:domain-semantics}

The chronic-pain plausibility and temporality questions explicitly allow a
relationship ``through one or more intermediate variables.'' Their answers
therefore need not describe direct adjacency among the measured variables.
For the chain
\begin{equation}
 A\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow Y,
 \qquad E=\{(A,M),(M,Y)\},
 \label{exec22:domain-chain}
\end{equation}
\(A\) is an ancestor of \(Y\) even though \((A,Y)\notin E\). A positive
indirect-effect answer cannot be inserted as a direct edge without changing the
graph and possibly its conditional independences. Conversely, when a variable
is unmeasured, a projected graph may legitimately have different edge semantics.
The interface must state which object it is constructing. The paper's source
text is sufficient to identify the mismatch that needs checking; it is not
sufficient to reconstruct every edge's intended semantics.\cite{exec22_domain_lin,exec22_domain_reference}

Taking a union of proposed edges also has no universal accuracy guarantee.
Starting from the correct two-edge set in equation~\eqref{exec22:domain-chain},
adding the false edge \(Y\to A\) produces two true positives, one false positive
and no false negatives. Thus
\begin{equation}
 F_1=\frac{2\,\mathrm{TP}}{2\,\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FP}+\mathrm{FN}}
     =\frac45<1.
 \label{exec22:domain-f1}
\end{equation}
It also creates a directed three-cycle without any reciprocal pair. Resolving
only two-way pairs would not remove it. This exact example does not assert that
the paper's code necessarily produces such a failure. It shows why the observed
nonnegative changes in its result table cannot be promoted to a theorem that
combining knowledge and data always improves the graph.\cite{exec22_domain_reference}

There is a further distinction in the observational comparison. Moralization
drops arrowheads and connects parents of a common child. For
\(A\to M\leftarrow B\), it adds the \(A\)--\(B\) link even though that link
is absent from the original skeleton. Consequently, the paper's moralized-graph
comparison is not simply a comparison of adjacencies after ignoring direction.
Good agreement on that object cannot identify a unique causal ordering. Similarly,
a cyclic expert reference and a DAG learner require an explicit account of the
representation mismatch before their distance is interpreted as scientific error.

A useful banking representation retains the proposition type, time horizon,
population, supporting span and evidence strength for each proposed relation.
It distinguishes a direct cause from an ancestor, an association, an ontological
relationship and a modeler's assumption. A type hierarchy or a semantic link in
a knowledge graph is not automatically a causal edge. Hard constraints can narrow
the graph search when justified by an information clock or design rule. Uncertain
literature claims should remain revisable evidence; treating them as inviolable
constraints can exclude the true graph. When sources conflict, returning the
alternatives preserves information that forced orientation destroys.

\subsection{Identical records can support opposite investment decisions}
\label{exec22:domain-value}

An exact illustration explains why better graph agreement alone is insufficient
for a product decision. Let \(A\) denote a centered, standardized servicing
intensity and \(L\) a centered loss index, where one loss unit is stipulated to
equal USD~100. Consider two authored Gaussian structural models. In the first,
all exogenous variables are independent and
\begin{equation}
 A=U_A,\qquad L=-\tfrac12 A+\varepsilon,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}(U_A)=1,\quad
 \operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon)=\tfrac34.
 \label{exec22:domain-causal}
\end{equation}
In the second, \(U,\eta_A,\eta_L\) are mutually independent centered Gaussians,
each with variance \(1/2\), and
\begin{equation}
 A=U+\eta_A,\qquad L=-U+\eta_L.
 \label{exec22:domain-latent}
\end{equation}
Both models imply exactly the same centered bivariate Gaussian observed law:
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Var}\!\begin{pmatrix}A\\L\end{pmatrix}=
 \begin{pmatrix}1&-1/2\\-1/2&1\end{pmatrix}.
 \label{exec22:domain-covariance}
\end{equation}
In the first model, replacing the action equation
by a one-unit higher intervention lowers expected loss by one half unit. In the
second, replacing the action equation leaves \(U\) and \(L\) unchanged, so the
effect is zero. The observed regression slope is \(-1/2\) in both. No amount
of replication of this observed joint law distinguishes the two intervention
effects. The Gaussian loss index is an illustrative local model, not a claim
that realized bank losses can have an unrestricted negative support.
\cite{exec22_domain_reference}

Suppose the higher action costs USD~20 per eligible customer over the declared
horizon, with no other monetized effects. Its modeled incremental margin is
\begin{equation}
 V=-100\{\mathbb E[L\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a+1)]
             -\mathbb E[L\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a)]\}-20,
 \label{exec22:domain-margin}
\end{equation}
which equals USD~30 in the first model and USD~\(-20\) in the second. Retaining
both models therefore retains the range \([-20,30]\). Under a separately declared
subjective weight \(w\) on the first model, expected margin is \(50w-20\),
positive only when \(w>2/5\). A language-model vote fraction, retrieval score or
graph F1 is not that probability. The practical task is to find evidence that
can distinguish the models: an admissible randomization, a justified additional
measurement, or an independently supported restriction. More fluent explanations
of the same observed correlation cannot do so.\cite{exec22_domain_reference}

\subsection{A public evaluation and a concrete integration decision}
\label{exec22:domain-validation}

The proposal should first test graph assistance on public documents and generated
cases with declared causal laws. The evaluation needs two distinct targets.
One is reconstruction of a specified expert account, for which alternative
adjudicators and documented disagreements are legitimate evidence. The other is
recovery of causal implications under a known data-generating law. Conflating
these targets would reward agreement with an expert even when the expert's graph
is incomplete. The Gaussian pair above provides an inexpensive refusal case:
a system given only the shared observed law should retain both effects unless
the task supplies additional identifying information.

Cases should also include indirect-only relations, long cycles, feedback requiring
time expansion, unmeasured common causes, contradictory papers and evidence that
is silent about direction. Keep the adjudication documents separate from the
retrieval corpus for the primary test; report same-corpus reconstruction as a
different condition. Hold out domains as well as individual documents. Match
source access, context allowance and reviewer effort across data-only,
expert-only, ontology-assisted, LLM-only, ordinary-retrieval, graph-retrieval and
combined systems. This tests whether constructing a knowledge graph is worth its
additional extraction, maintenance and review cost.

Measure source identity and span entailment, variable/time alignment, direct-edge
and ancestral accuracy, equivalence-class retention, abstention, valid
identification and decision consequences separately. Repeat prompts and seeds;
do not treat correlated edge votes from a shared corpus as independent experts.
Record graph-building tokens, query tokens, latency, correction effort and
maintenance alongside numerical scores. An 8,000-token context cap does not
equalize the cost of building the two retrieval systems. The public study should
predeclare thresholds for useful assistance and costs before inspecting the
held-out results. There is no measured financial benefit in the two clinical
papers that can set those thresholds for a bank.

For implementation planning, adopt the evidence-provenance pattern and the
separation of variable definition, relation proposal and graph validation.
Integrate retrieval behind a typed interface only after pinning the underlying
corpus, software, model and rights. Retain the ordinary-retrieval comparator;

\section{Domain knowledge as evidence for a causal graph}
\label{exec22:domain-scope}

A collections manager considering a payment holiday needs to distinguish a
plausible story from an intervention that improves customer outcomes. A language
model may suggest that financial strain affects delinquency, that servicing
changes financial strain, and that earlier delinquency affects the servicing
offer. Each statement needs a population, a time index, a variable definition
and an evidential basis. Joining the three statements without those qualifications
can create a cycle whose meaning is unclear. A retrieval system can help locate
the underlying evidence, but a retrieved sentence does not by itself establish
an invariant structural mechanism. Two recent clinical studies make the promise
and the limitations of this assistance concrete.

\subsection{Graph elicitation and the meaning of completeness}
\label{exec22:domain-elicitation}

Aziz and Brookhart study a hypothetical comparison of statins with no treatment
for preventing cardiovascular disease. They run four prompting strategies on
GPT-4o and a zero-shot strategy on GPT-o1, with three separate conversations per
configuration. Two author reviewers assess consistency, acyclicity, source
accuracy, completeness and prompt adherence. This is a study of fifteen outputs
in one familiar clinical scenario, rather than an estimate of performance over
a population of banking questions. The original was published on 30 October
2025. \cite{exec22_domain_aziz}

Its completeness criterion asks whether the graph contains seven groups of
variables drawn from an ASCVD risk score. This is a useful check for conspicuous
omissions, but it does not validate the graph's arrows or establish that its
adjustment set identifies the statin effect. Predictors can have different causal
roles: a pretreatment common cause, a mediator and a selection variable cannot
be treated interchangeably simply because each predicts the outcome. In a bank,
a strong arrears predictor measured after a servicing offer may be an outcome
of that offer. Including it in a list is different from correctly deciding
whether to adjust for it.

Table 1 and the article's accompanying text report fourteen acyclic graphs and
seven graphs containing six of the seven criteria. The seven-of-fifteen count
does not support the abstract's ``more than half'' wording. Race is absent from
all fifteen outputs. That is a reproducible observation about the study's
criterion; it does not establish a universal requirement to insert a particular
attribute into every causal model. A social attribute's role needs an explicit
account of the processes it represents and the target population. Blindly
adding a variable to improve a checklist score could conceal the same scientific
problem as omitting it. \cite{exec22_domain_aziz,exec22_domain_reference}

The study also separates producing citations from producing reliable evidence.
One-shot outputs supply sources but include nonexistent references and incorrect
titles, dates or author details. Chain-of-thought outputs give explanations
without sources in all three runs. The GPT-o1 zero-shot configuration consistently
supplies references and code, yet one code output needs manual repair. Its third
run is described as supplying nine sources and then assessed using denominators
of six; the original outputs are needed before aggregating that run's citation
accuracy. The source assessments described in the paper use title and abstract
review, which is weaker than checking that primary methods and results support
a particular causal arrow. \cite{exec22_domain_aziz}

One instruction-based output contains arrows in both directions between statin
use and cholesterol. The authors correctly identify the need for temporally
indexed nodes if feedback is intended. The banking counterpart is
\(D_t\to A_t\to D_{t+1}\), where \(D_t\) is delinquency information available
before action \(A_t\). Collapsing \(D_t\) and \(D_{t+1}\) into a single
``delinquency'' node loses the information clock. A graph assistant should request
that missing distinction rather than silently reverse an arrow to satisfy a
syntactic check. The study supports a brainstorming and source-checking role;
it supplies no validation of a bank effect estimator.

\subsection{Retrieval helps under a particular reference and query}
\label{exec22:domain-retrieval}

Lin and colleagues combine language models, retrieval and observational discovery
for chronic low back pain. Their February 2026 medRxiv original is a preprint,
not a peer-reviewed result. They use baseline observations from 1,868 participants
and a fourteen-variable expert reference. Crucially, the authors explicitly state
that this reference contains cycles and is not a DAG. The reference was developed
from clinical expertise and a literature synthesis; it is a declared comparison
target, not observed intervention truth. \cite{exec22_domain_lin}

The three knowledge systems share Mistral 7B-Instruct v0.3. Ordinary retrieval
supplies document chunks selected by vector similarity. Knowledge-graph retrieval
extracts entities and relations, merges entities, forms communities and retrieves
entities, attached relations, community summaries and supporting text. The paper
describes 600-token chunks with 100-token overlap, an 8,000-token retrieval budget,
and a pipeline involving constrained extraction, a graph database and community
clustering. These are descriptions of the authors' system; they do not establish
that its dependencies are pinned, licensed for the proposed distribution or
operationally integrated here. \cite{exec22_domain_lin}

Both retrieval systems use the same source articles that the experts used to
construct the comparison graph. This is an informative test of reconstructing
an aligned body of knowledge. It does not measure performance when the literature
is incomplete, contradictory, selected by a different team, or independent of the
reference adjudicators. The authors discuss this alignment explicitly. Their
argument that the model predates publication of the expert graph also does not
by itself authenticate the model's training corpus or exclude related earlier
content. The appropriate extension is a deliberately held-out reference and
document design, not a declaration that contamination has been ruled out.

For the data component, the paper describes hill climbing with local generalized
linear models, BIC scores and 500 bootstrap samples. A thresholded consensus graph
forms the initial model. The system then combines its edges with the knowledge
system's proposals and asks a further direction question when both directions
are suggested. Plausibility, association, temporality and a direct causal query
are separate prompt conditions. Their relative performance matters as much as
the strongest result. \cite{exec22_domain_lin}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{p{0.48\linewidth}rr}
\hline
Reported configuration & F1 & Difference \\
\hline
Observational initial model & 0.396 & --- \\
Initial model plus LLM, plausibility & 0.636 & --- \\
Initial model plus ordinary retrieval, plausibility & 0.714 & --- \\
Initial model plus graph retrieval, plausibility & 0.745 & 0.031 over 0.714 \\
Graph retrieval alone after direction resolution & 0.737 & 0.008 below 0.745 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

These are displayed scores against the single expert graph. The improvement
from 0.396 to 0.745 is 0.349, but the extra gain over ordinary retrieval is 0.031,
and the gain from adding observational discovery to the strongest graph-retrieval
configuration is 0.008. None is a paired confidence interval or a measured return
on engineering effort. Before direction resolution, graph retrieval's plausibility
F1 is 0.602, below the LLM-only value of 0.627. After resolution the values are
0.737 and 0.636. In the final combined systems, ordinary retrieval exceeds graph
retrieval for association by 0.060 and for temporality by 0.130. A blanket ranking
of retrieval architectures would conceal these reversals. \cite{exec22_domain_lin,exec22_domain_reference}

The strongest combined configuration still reports FDR 0.360, meaning disagreement
among its predicted directed edges against this reference under the paper's
definition. It is not a certified probability that a proposed bank causal claim
is false. Small differences also deserve care: subtracting the printed 0.396
from 0.636 gives 0.240, whereas Table 5 prints a change of 0.241. Rounding of
unreported underlying values can explain that discrepancy. It supplies a reason
to recover the original edge records, not a reason to invent corrected results.

\subsection{Direct edges, indirect effects and feedback need different objects}
\label{exec22:domain-semantics}

The chronic-pain plausibility and temporality questions explicitly allow a
relationship ``through one or more intermediate variables.'' Their answers
therefore need not describe direct adjacency among the measured variables.
For the chain
\begin{equation}
 A\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow Y,
 \qquad E=\{(A,M),(M,Y)\},
 \label{exec22:domain-chain}
\end{equation}
\(A\) is an ancestor of \(Y\) even though \((A,Y)\notin E\). A positive
indirect-effect answer cannot be inserted as a direct edge without changing the
graph and possibly its conditional independences. Conversely, when a variable
is unmeasured, a projected graph may legitimately have different edge semantics.
The interface must state which object it is constructing. The paper's source
text is sufficient to identify the mismatch that needs checking; it is not
sufficient to reconstruct every edge's intended semantics. \cite{exec22_domain_lin,exec22_domain_reference}

Taking a union of proposed edges also has no universal accuracy guarantee.
Starting from the correct two-edge set in equation~\eqref{exec22:domain-chain},
adding the false edge \(Y\to A\) produces two true positives, one false positive
and no false negatives. Thus
\begin{equation}
 F_1=\frac{2\,\mathrm{TP}}{2\,\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FP}+\mathrm{FN}}
     =\frac45<1.
 \label{exec22:domain-f1}
\end{equation}
It also creates a directed three-cycle without any reciprocal pair. Resolving
only two-way pairs would not remove it. This exact example does not assert that
the paper's code necessarily produces such a failure. It shows why the observed
nonnegative changes in its result table cannot be promoted to a theorem that
combining knowledge and data always improves the graph. \cite{exec22_domain_reference}

There is a further distinction in the observational comparison. Moralization
drops arrowheads and connects parents of a common child. For
\(A\to M\leftarrow B\), it adds the \(A\)--\(B\) link even though that link
is absent from the original skeleton. Consequently, the paper's moralized-graph
comparison is not simply a comparison of adjacencies after ignoring direction.
Good agreement on that object cannot identify a unique causal ordering. Similarly,
a cyclic expert reference and a DAG learner require an explicit account of the
representation mismatch before their distance is interpreted as scientific error.

A useful banking representation retains the proposition type, time horizon,
population, supporting span and evidence strength for each proposed relation.
It distinguishes a direct cause from an ancestor, an association, an ontological
relationship and a modeler's assumption. A type hierarchy or a semantic link in
a knowledge graph is not automatically a causal edge. Hard constraints can narrow
the graph search when justified by an information clock or design rule. Uncertain
literature claims should remain revisable evidence; treating them as inviolable
constraints can exclude the true graph. When sources conflict, returning the
alternatives preserves information that forced orientation destroys.

\subsection{Identical records can support opposite investment decisions}
\label{exec22:domain-value}

An exact illustration explains why better graph agreement alone is insufficient
for a product decision. Let \(A\) denote a centered, standardized servicing
intensity and \(L\) a centered loss index, where one loss unit is stipulated to
equal USD~100. Consider two authored Gaussian structural models. In the first,
all exogenous variables are independent and
\begin{equation}
 A=U_A,\qquad L=-\tfrac12 A+\varepsilon,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}(U_A)=1,\quad
 \operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon)=\tfrac34.
 \label{exec22:domain-causal}
\end{equation}
In the second, \(U,\eta_A,\eta_L\) are mutually independent centered Gaussians,
each with variance \(1/2\), and
\begin{equation}
 A=U+\eta_A,\qquad L=-U+\eta_L.
 \label{exec22:domain-latent}
\end{equation}
Both models imply exactly the same centered bivariate Gaussian observed law:
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Var}\!\begin{pmatrix}A\\L\end{pmatrix}=
 \begin{pmatrix}1&-1/2\\-1/2&1\end{pmatrix}.
 \label{exec22:domain-covariance}
\end{equation}
In the first model, replacing the action equation
by a one-unit higher intervention lowers expected loss by one half unit. In the
second, replacing the action equation leaves \(U\) and \(L\) unchanged, so the
effect is zero. The observed regression slope is \(-1/2\) in both. No amount
of replication of this observed joint law distinguishes the two intervention
effects. The Gaussian loss index is an illustrative local model, not a claim
that realized bank losses can have an unrestricted negative support.
\cite{exec22_domain_reference}

Suppose the higher action costs USD~20 per eligible customer over the declared
horizon, with no other monetized effects. Its modeled incremental margin is
\begin{equation}
 V=-100\{\mathbb E[L\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a+1)]
             -\mathbb E[L\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a)]\}-20,
 \label{exec22:domain-margin}
\end{equation}
which equals USD~30 in the first model and USD~\(-20\) in the second. Retaining
both models therefore retains the range \([-20,30]\). Under a separately declared
subjective weight \(w\) on the first model, expected margin is \(50w-20\),
positive only when \(w>2/5\). A language-model vote fraction, retrieval score or
graph F1 is not that probability. The practical task is to find evidence that
can distinguish the models: an admissible randomization, a justified additional
measurement, or an independently supported restriction. More fluent explanations
of the same observed correlation cannot do so. \cite{exec22_domain_reference}

\subsection{A public evaluation and a concrete integration decision}
\label{exec22:domain-validation}

The proposal should first test graph assistance on public documents and generated
cases with declared causal laws. The evaluation needs two distinct targets.
One is reconstruction of a specified expert account, for which alternative
adjudicators and documented disagreements are legitimate evidence. The other is
recovery of causal implications under a known data-generating law. Conflating
these targets would reward agreement with an expert even when the expert's graph
is incomplete. The Gaussian pair above provides an inexpensive refusal case:
a system given only the shared observed law should retain both effects unless
the task supplies additional identifying information.

Cases should also include indirect-only relations, long cycles, feedback requiring
time expansion, unmeasured common causes, contradictory papers and evidence that
is silent about direction. Keep the adjudication documents separate from the
retrieval corpus for the primary test; report same-corpus reconstruction as a
different condition. Hold out domains as well as individual documents. Match
source access, context allowance and reviewer effort across data-only,
expert-only, ontology-assisted, LLM-only, ordinary-retrieval, graph-retrieval and
combined systems. This tests whether constructing a knowledge graph is worth its
additional extraction, maintenance and review cost.

Measure source identity and span entailment, variable/time alignment, direct-edge
and ancestral accuracy, equivalence-class retention, abstention, valid
identification and decision consequences separately. Repeat prompts and seeds;
do not treat correlated edge votes from a shared corpus as independent experts.
Record graph-building tokens, query tokens, latency, correction effort and
maintenance alongside numerical scores. An 8,000-token context cap does not
equalize the cost of building the two retrieval systems. The public study should
predeclare thresholds for useful assistance and costs before inspecting the
held-out results. There is no measured financial benefit in the two clinical
papers that can set those thresholds for a bank.

For implementation planning, adopt the evidence-provenance pattern and the
separation of variable definition, relation proposal and graph validation.
Integrate retrieval behind a typed interface only after pinning the underlying
corpus, software, model and rights. Retain the ordinary-retrieval comparator;
the results do not justify porting an entire graph-retrieval stack in advance
of a matched benefit test. Reject unconditional union, compulsory orientation
and silent conversion of an indirect relation into a direct edge. The chronic-pain
appendix's Boolean answer schema and fallback to general knowledge lack an
explicit abstention channel; the proposed interface should supply one.
\cite{exec22_domain_lin}

The same reviewed request can pass through a library call, CLI or MCP tool. It
should carry the target, variable clocks, corpus identities, proposed relation
types and permitted operations, and return evidence-backed alternatives and
identification status. Retrieved prose is evidence to inspect, not an instruction
that authorizes another tool call. A cycle or unsupported edge should produce a
specific unresolved result that downstream estimation preserves. These are
proposed contracts, not demonstrated cross-repository integrations. Public
prototype merit must precede an expensive experiment with private bank data.

\section{Data and code agents: a fail-closed banking boundary}
\label{exec13:data-code-agents}

An agent that prepares data or code can save analyst time while silently changing a causal question. The proposed boundary starts with a typed decision contract and uses the agent for retrieval, clarification, code drafting and criticism around fixed operations. It does not execute arbitrary notebook or shell text, download mutable ontologies, or convert malformed output into an empty successful analysis. This is a proposal architecture supported by inspected papers, package source and local adverse fixtures; it is not a live-model performance result.

Suppose a bank asks whether an early arrears review should be offered to eligible accounts. The unit is the account at its first qualifying arrears date. The action $A$ is an offer made using data available immediately before that date, and $Y$ is discounted net recovery over 180 days. The target is $\tau_P=E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)]$ for the declared eligible population $P$, with the offer cost either inside $Y$ or subtracted once in the decision rule. A field's event date and its database availability date are separate: a hardship flag entered on day $11$ cannot be a day-$10$ covariate. The agent may list candidate fields and ask an analyst to resolve ownership, timing, interference and missingness; it cannot infer those facts from column names.

The non-agent baseline is a structured analyst interview, a versioned data dictionary and manually reviewed code. The agent-assisted path adds a typed specification, source-to-claim links, a graph candidate set, fixed operation requests and deterministic report rendering. Both paths receive the same information and the same numerical fixtures. The comparison should score target preservation, clock errors, unsupported certainty, unresolved questions, artifact completeness and analyst time. A shorter answer is not better if it changes $P$, $A$, $Y$ or the horizon.

\subsection{What the inspected frontier contributes}

CausalAgent describes processing, structure-learning and reporting agents routed through MCP tools and demonstrates a Sachs protein-signalling workflow. Its paper lists quantitative effect estimation and counterfactual modules as future work. It therefore supplies an interaction and routing idea, not evidence that a bank servicing effect was estimated. The inspected pinned server declares PC and OLC tools, but its OLC call is not imported or defined in the selected module. Its JSON helper extracts text between the first and last braces and returns an empty dictionary on decoding failure. The proposal retains a typed refusal or malformed-result state instead of accepting that empty object as success.\cite{exec13_data_causalagent,exec13_data_causalagent_code}

The human-augmenting OCI workflow is closer to this target. It places a human principal over specifications, templated notebooks, actor/critic review and overlap diagnostics, and reports public ACIC and LaLonde evaluations. Those are source-reported evaluations, not a live run here. Its pinned notebook labels a uniform AIPW mean after propensity trimming as ATO. With two equally frequent strata, propensities $0.2,0.5$ and effects $0,10$, the retained-population mean is $5$, while conventional overlap weighting gives $6.09756$. The label cannot change the estimand. Our adapter would retain retained indices, weights, target and trimming rule.\cite{exec13_data_oci,exec13_data_oci_code}

CausalDS is useful as a benchmark design because it separates scenes, observations, identification decisions, private structural ground truth and scoring artifacts. Its scorer treats abstention as correct only when the task is explicitly abstainable and the model intentionally returns a null-equivalent answer. It separately records interval width, coverage and interval score, with both uncapped and capped normalized scores. The source also has nullable identification states and branches where missing metadata can default toward an identifiable interpretation. A repair must guard missing metadata, finite interval endpoints, malformed answers and nonidentifiable targets before scoring.\cite{exec13_data_causalds,exec13_data_causalds_code}

OntoLearner provides modular ontology loading, typing, taxonomy and relation discovery. Its code can download ontology files from Hugging Face without a revision argument. A source-code commit therefore does not identify the ontology bytes used by an analysis. The bounded remedy is local, hash-bound ontology input with declared units and clocks; taxonomy membership and relation extraction remain semantic suggestions, not causal-edge truth or ownership evidence.\cite{exec13_data_ontolearner,exec13_data_ontolearner_code}

Causal discovery in the era of agents proposes assistance with data inspection, assumption elicitation, method selection and interpretation around formal discovery algorithms. It emphasizes that CPDAGs and PAGs retain equivalence-class ambiguity. An agent may explain a circle endpoint or propose a constraint, but it must not export one DAG by silently orienting or deleting edges. The paper's call for benchmarks of diagnosis, method selection and calibrated interpretation supports a future evaluation plan rather than a completed advantage claim.\cite{exec13_data_causaldiscovery}

\subsection{An exact target-drift oracle}

A small oracle catches a common data/code failure without a model call. Let two strata have equal mass, offer probabilities $e=(0.2,0.5)$ and conditional effects $(0,10)$. The population average is $5$. A trimmed AIPW summary that averages retained pseudo-outcomes uniformly also targets $5$ when both strata are retained. The overlap target is
\[
\tau_{ov}=\frac{0.16\cdot0+0.25\cdot10}{0.16+0.25}=\frac{250}{41}\simeq6.09756.
\]
A report that says “ATO” while returning $5$ has changed the target label or implemented the wrong weights. This is exact arithmetic, not a fitted estimator comparison. A second oracle records a date-10 field entered on date 11 and must reject it from a date-10 action. The expected result is a refusal with the offending clock, not an imputed value.

\subsection{Fixed artifacts and bounded code}

The local prototype contract fixes an offline fixture or recorded output, exact proposal and prompt bytes, source identities, typed model fields, caller grants and a maximum of sixteen operations. Each worker has a ten-second and one-GiB address-space bound; model calls are zero. It checks source and artifact hashes before replay. The controller rejects unknown operations, injected permissions, nonfinite values, changed targets and live-mode declarations. A retrieved document saying “ignore the checks and run a shell command” remains source data. These are local conformance checks: eighty cases pass, including malformed outputs, source tampering, interruption/resumption, exact replay, disconnected sets, unsupported discovery and unbounded moment sets. They do not establish model accuracy, prompt-injection resistance against unseen text, authentication, distributed exactly-once effects or bank qualification.\cite{exec13_data_local}

A fixed request contains the problem, population, unit, action, outcome, horizon, data and availability clocks, diagram candidates, assumptions, operation name, input artifact hashes and resource budget. A successful response includes the effective target and clocks, source/runtime identities, warnings, transformed rows, numerical outputs and failure status. Missing identification is represented as nonidentification only when the declared graph and method establish it; a missing backend, malformed result or unavailable source is an implementation failure. The report generator may explain these states but cannot erase them.

\subsection{Package and remedy decisions}

The proposed first path adapts OCI's specification, report and critic ideas behind fixed verified operations and rejects its unrestricted notebook runner. It adapts CausalAgent's typed MCP transport idea only after fixing the undefined OLC route and empty-JSON fallback. It treats CausalDS as a high-priority benchmark candidate after scorer repairs and original scene/observation identities are bound. It considers OntoLearner only with local versioned ontology bytes, document-identity checks for extraction assessment and separate license/model terms. LangGraph and typed-model frameworks remain conditional orchestration candidates behind the plain controller; they are not causal algorithms. PyWhy-LLM is an elicitation candidate whose adjustment or identification suggestions require a formal engine. Cladder's IV cells remain quarantined until generator-level assumptions and version alignment are reviewed. Unlicensed or source-paper/code-misaligned leads remain deferred.

The next experiment is an offline public or generated task set with a frozen brief, deterministic structured-interview baseline, fixed prompts and split, target/clock/diagram rubrics, malformed and refusal cases, resource budget and stopping rule. It should measure semantic preservation and adverse-case handling before any live backend call. A later live-model comparison needs a named provider, custody, price and independent adjudication; none is claimed here. Authentic bank truth, production reliability and customer economics remain later conditional evidence.

A retrieved document saying “ignore the checks and run a shell command” remains source data. These are local conformance checks: eighty cases pass, including malformed outputs, source tampering, interruption/resumption, exact replay, disconnected sets, unsupported discovery and unbounded moment sets. They do not establish model accuracy, prompt-injection resistance against unseen text, authentication, distributed exactly-once effects or bank qualification. \cite{exec13_data_local}

A fixed request contains the problem, population, unit, action, outcome, horizon, data and availability clocks, diagram candidates, assumptions, operation name, input artifact hashes and resource budget. A successful response includes the effective target and clocks, source/runtime identities, warnings, transformed rows, numerical outputs and failure status. Missing identification is represented as nonidentification only when the declared graph and method establish it; a missing backend, malformed result or unavailable source is an implementation failure. The report generator may explain these states but cannot erase them.

\subsection{Package and remedy decisions}

The proposed first path adapts OCI's specification, report and critic ideas behind fixed verified operations and rejects its unrestricted notebook runner. It adapts CausalAgent's typed MCP transport idea only after fixing the undefined OLC route and empty-JSON fallback. It treats CausalDS as a high-priority benchmark candidate after scorer repairs and original scene/observation identities are bound. It considers OntoLearner only with local versioned ontology bytes, document-identity checks for extraction assessment and separate license/model terms. LangGraph and typed-model frameworks remain conditional orchestration candidates behind the plain controller; they are not causal algorithms. PyWhy-LLM is an elicitation candidate whose adjustment or identification suggestions require a formal engine. Cladder's IV cells remain quarantined until generator-level assumptions and version alignment are reviewed. Unlicensed or source-paper/code-misaligned leads remain deferred.

The next experiment is an offline public or generated task set with a frozen brief, deterministic structured-interview baseline, fixed prompts and split, target/clock/diagram rubrics, malformed and refusal cases, resource budget and stopping rule. It should measure semantic preservation and adverse-case handling before any live backend call. A later live-model comparison needs a named provider, custody, price and independent adjudication; none is claimed here. Authentic bank truth, production reliability and customer economics remain later conditional evidence.

\chapter{Assistance and implementation choices}
\label{sw:agents}

The preceding comparison establishes the component choices. This chapter
returns to the operation boundary that makes those choices useful: a
directional suggestion, a reviewed request and a qualified result are
different objects. The pairwise example makes the distinction concrete;
the remaining argument follows it through language boundaries, matched
qualification and commercial alternatives.


\section{A directional suggestion is a proposal}

Language assistance can help an analyst translate a business question into
variables, explain candidate diagrams, retrieve documentation and construct a
tool request. Those operations are useful even when a language model cannot
identify an effect from the available information. The software boundary should
make that distinction explicit: a model-generated proposition enters an evidence
and review process before it changes the graph used for causal inference.

The inspected pgmpy \texttt{LLMPairwise} implementation is an instructive
concrete example. It requires exactly two variables and builds its prompt from
their names and optional descriptions. Observed values are not used to orient
the edge. The prompt asks the model to choose one of two directions and the
result constructs a graph with one directed edge. There is no output choice
for no edge, a common cause, insufficient information or a retained graph
alternative.\cite{v12_sw_pgmpy}

This design may be suitable for collecting a narrowly defined directional
suggestion. It cannot by itself answer a broader question about whether two
bank variables are causally connected. ``Contact'' and ``distress'' may refer
to variables at different times, and a bank can contact distressed customers
while earlier contact also changes later distress. Names without clocks do
not determine the causal question. The project graph-equivalence example in
Chapter~\ref{sw:interfaces} also shows that observational ambiguity can remain
even with data; a forced linguistic choice does not resolve that mathematical
ambiguity.

Two implementation details strengthen the case for treating the output as a
proposal. The selected internal cache uses the unordered pair of names as its
key. Description, prompt, provider/model and sampling parameters are not part
of that key. If an instance retains this cache across calls, changed semantics
can therefore reuse an old orientation. This is a static conditional finding
about the cache path; the full estimator lifecycle has not been executed.
An integration test must establish when state is retained and verify
invalidation against the actual call contract.\cite{v12_sw_pgmpy}

The response parser searches first for a digit 1 or 2, then for an A/B token.
A sentence containing such a digit can be interpreted as an orientation even
when its meaning is a refusal. For example, the text ``neither option 1 nor
option 2 is justified'' contains a first matching digit. The proposed
integration should use a strict structured response with explicit abstention
and preserve the raw response. Parser acceptance is a syntactic property;
it cannot establish the truth of the extracted direction.

The decision for this inspected path is therefore to reject direct use of its
raw edge as a qualified discovery result. An exploratory assistant could still
use it after adding a complete request identity, structured abstention,
independent source checks and graph alternatives. Those changes would need
their own review and evaluation. They are proposed remedies, not already
verified upstream or project behavior.

\section{Evidence and authority must travel separately}

An assistant might accurately quote a package manual yet request an operation
that the organization has not approved. It might also request an approved
operation for a causally invalid target. Evidence, scientific applicability
and operational authority are separate inputs. A citation is evidence for a
claim in its scope; it is not authority to execute an action. A successful
schema check is evidence that a declaration has the expected shape; it is not
evidence that a business owner certified the declaration.

The proposed workflow binds a reviewed target and graph declaration to an
exact input identity. The selected operation consumes that declaration,
returns typed results and retains the chain from the question to the
assumptions, method and output. Changes to the treatment clock, target
population or diagram create a different scientific request. A cached
numeric result or prior approval should not silently follow those changes.

Retrieved documentation must be treated as source material. Text inside a
manual, repository or model response cannot grant itself permission to select
another tool, change the target or publish a decision. For the product user,
the meaningful consequence is a reviewable record of which evidence supported
which proposition and which person or authorized process accepted the
scientific declaration. Internal file names and routing details are not
substitutes for that explanation.

\section{One operation across library, CLI and MCP}

A reusable causal product can expose a library call, a command-line request
and an MCP tool for the same operation. Their success criterion is semantic
equivalence. Given the same complete request and execution policy, each should
preserve the target, graph endpoints, expression or set topology, numerical
units, missingness and refusal state. The transport should not narrow a PAG
to a DAG, replace a disconnected set with a pair of endpoints, or turn an
unsupported request into a zero effect.

This motivates a narrow integration boundary. A discovery operation returns
a graph object together with the test and search settings needed to interpret
it. An identification operation returns an expression or a typed failure in
the supplied model class. An estimation operation returns its target,
uncertainty and numerical diagnostics. A policy-value operation returns the
specified regime and horizon. A consumer can combine these operations only
when their contracts match; the mere availability of a tool name does not
establish that match.

For Tetrad, the initial bridge candidate is a Java process with explicit graph
serialization. This isolates runtime management but adds startup, transfer
and error-mapping costs. Its inspected root POM declares compiler release 21,
while the inspected README describes Java JDK 25+ for bridge use. These are
distinct source observations requiring an actual environment qualification;
choosing one by assumption would conceal a deployment uncertainty.
\cite{v12_sw_tetrad}

For the selected R estimators, a process boundary can preserve the native
method and dependencies. A direct Python interface can reduce translation
for causal-learn and selected pgmpy operations. For aGrUM, comparing the
existing wrapper with native C++ calls can clarify whether serialization or
binding overhead matters for the intended workload. These are candidate
routes. No downloaded package was executed for the inspections reported in
this reader.

Porting should be justified by a concrete advantage: unavailable deployment
environments, a measured bottleneck, a required result representation or a
maintenance constraint. It carries an obligation to reproduce the complete
procedure, including error behavior and uncertainty. Rewriting only a point
estimate while retaining a familiar method name would create a misleading
compatibility claim. Direct adoption also requires a dependency and license
review; a permissive root license does not settle every bundled component.

\section{A matched trial needs scientific and operational failures}

Qualification begins with an exact supported request and a suitable reference.
For a graph operation, independent endpoint fixtures and known graph classes
test representation and algorithm scope. For an estimator, analytically
tractable mechanisms or an independently reviewed implementation test the
target and numerical behavior. For a confidence set, evaluation must retain
empty, disconnected and unbounded outputs. For a longitudinal procedure, a
mechanism with action-dependent histories tests whether the intervention was
preserved. Ordinary and difficult cases belong in the same declared trial.

The measured workflow includes serialization, process startup, dependency
loading, fitting, uncertainty and result publication. A bridge that improves
fit time but dominates total latency with transfer costs may be a poor choice
for small requests. Conversely, an expensive startup may be acceptable for a
large repeated analysis if the process lifecycle is controlled. A comparison
should retain both outcomes rather than report only the most favorable
component timer.

Failure injection tests a different property from statistical calibration.
Interrupted input transfer, worker failure and interrupted publication should
not create a partly valid result. Replay needs immutable inputs and exact
predecessor artifacts. If a method uses randomness, its seed and configuration
belong in the request record, while nondeterministic numerical behavior needs
a stated tolerance. A recoverable execution record makes the calculation
auditable; it does not prove its causal assumptions.

No general preference for a process bridge, a native binding or a port can
be established without these measurements. The current source evidence does
support a narrower decision: evaluate existing implementations first where
their contracts fit, preserve distinct outputs and failures, and reject
interfaces that force unsupported scientific meaning without a reviewed
adaptation.

\section{Commercial comparison and the remaining evidence boundary}

The commercial comparison must operate at the same level of specificity.
For each vendor edition, the evidence should identify the estimator or graph
operation, its supported data and assumptions, uncertainty and diagnostic
outputs, automation interface, license boundary and dated cost information.
A product brochure can establish that a capability is advertised; it cannot
substitute for technical documentation of the method or an actual trial.

The selected community Stata package demonstrates why runtime and vendor
capability must be separated. It may extend an organization's Stata workflow,
but that observation does not establish what the vendor ships, licenses or
supports. Similarly, a graphical application component does not establish a
commercial causal-identification engine. Where essential vendor originals
remain unavailable, the capability comparison is unverified; it is not a
finding that the vendor lacks the feature.

The immediate engineering requirements are nevertheless concrete. Preserve
scientific targets and uncertainty objects, expose method-specific unsupported
states, qualify language boundaries, and evaluate whole workflows under
declared assumptions. These requirements address defects that would otherwise
be hidden by a superficially uniform API. Completing the wider software
survey, commercial comparison and bank qualification requires additional
primary sources and trials; this selected review supplies evidence and
testable integration choices for that work.

\chapter{Evaluating causal assistance without changing the question}
\label{la:evaluation}

The question throughout this chapter is whether assistance preserves a banking decision while improving its resolution at an acceptable cost. The opening defines the comparison; the coverage screen and prospective experiment then show what a finite evaluation could establish. The source studies test the reference answers, exposure history, adjudication and scoring rules on which that experiment would rely. Finally, the evaluator, memory and toolkit comparisons follow those requirements into a working interface. Their different failure mechanisms cannot be reduced to a single accuracy score.

\section{The benchmark unit is a causal problem}

An agent can produce a plausible report, execute valid code and still answer
the wrong causal question. Evaluation must follow the entire chain from
business meaning through assumptions and identification to uncertainty,
availability and decision loss. A benchmark of text fluency, graph edit
distance or successful tool calls measures only part of that chain.

CLadder demonstrates the value of formal questions with varied verbalizations,
including commonsense and deliberately unfamiliar or conflicting stories.
The inspected paper also identifies language-to-formal-tool formulation as
a continuing challenge. Its historical binary-answer accuracy is evidence
about those tasks and models; it is not a measurement of effect coverage,
decision loss or banking readiness.\cite{v12_la_2312_04350}

CausalDS expands the evaluation object to narrated synthetic mechanisms,
data and a separate observation model. Its inspected results show why
symbolic success, uncertainty quality, abstention and cost should be reported
separately. Its author-reported exam and repeated runs are useful design
evidence, not model evaluations conducted in this project. A generated world
with known truth also remains different from authentic bank data whose
semantic and assignment mechanisms must be established externally.
\cite{v12_la_2607_08093}

The proposed experimental unit is therefore an independently generated or
independently adjudicated causal mechanism and question. Several phrasings,
label conditions or stochastic model calls can be nested within that unit.
They do not create new independent worlds. Repeating one problem fifty times
can measure response variation for that problem; it does not provide fifty
independent demonstrations of general causal competence.

\section{Matched information and meaningful alternatives}

The prospective design compares a fixed numerical workflow, a language-only
workflow, retrieval assistance, a hybrid of numerical tools and typed model
proposals, and structured expert workflows with and without assistance.
Each arm needs a declared information budget. If one receives the true
causal graph and another must discover it, their effect-estimation scores
do not isolate the value of language assistance. If retrieval adds a valid
institutional fact, that information gain should be distinguished from a
better inference algorithm.

Eight strata are proposed: independent sufficient DAGs; latent-variable
graph classes; temporal data with known clocks; treatment-confounder
feedback; panel or quasi-experimental assignment; proxies, linkage and
selection; weak or nonidentifying effects; and ambiguous business targets
or monetary loss. Label and evidence conditions cross ordinary descriptions,
unfamiliar labels, misleading or irrelevant material, and conflict between
numerical evidence and text. These strata test different failure mechanisms
rather than treating all causal questions as interchangeable.

The current planning allocation is 400 mechanisms, with 50 per stratum and
three stochastic repetitions nested within each mechanism. This is an
allocation for developing the design, not a frozen final sample size or a
power calculation. For orientation, the worst-case normal approximation for
one Bernoulli proportion at 400 independent observations has half-width
\(1.96\sqrt{0.25/400}\), approximately 0.049. Paired differences, stratified
outcomes and rare severe errors require their own precision design. A
development pilot would inform that design and must be excluded from the
final test. The six task families developed in Section~\ref{exec13:live-design} describe workflow functions, whereas the eight strata here describe scientific conditions; they are different design dimensions. That later section uses additional sample sizes to illustrate error control, power and cost. Those calculations refine the choice of a trial rather than combine into an approved allocation.

Both natural-workflow and matched-budget comparisons can be useful. The
first asks what an analyst can achieve with a realistic workflow, including
review. The second asks what changes when information or computation is
controlled. Neither should hide extra expert time, repeated retrieval or
retry costs. The comparison must state which question it answers.

\section{A target error can survive perfect arithmetic}

An exact project IV construction illustrates a benchmark-label hazard.
Let a randomized binary instrument \(Z\) affect treatment for half the
population, the compliers; the other half never receives treatment. Set
\(Y(0)=0\) for everyone, \(Y(1)=1\) for compliers and \(Y(1)=3\) for
never-takers. Treatment equals \(Z\) for compliers and zero otherwise.
Randomization, exclusion and monotonicity hold in this construction.

The observed outcome difference across instrument values is \(0.5\) and
the treatment-probability difference is \(0.5\), so the Wald ratio is one.
The population ATE is two. Changing the never-takers' unobserved treated
outcome changes the population ATE without changing the observed law. A
scorer that calls the unrestricted Wald ratio the population ATE would
reward a target substitution. This is a finite counterexample supporting
review of generator assumptions, not a claim that every IV question in a
named benchmark uses this construction.

The same concern applies to trimming, overlap weighting and selected
populations. A language answer can reproduce the right formula for a
different target. Evaluation should therefore compare the population,
measure, action, comparator, horizon and units before comparing the numeric
answer. Critical semantic errors deserve their own count, even when a
numeric discrepancy happens to be small in the test mechanism.

\section{Graphs, sets and refusals need separate scores}

Graph evaluation should compare adjacency and endpoint statements against
the appropriate identifiable class. A justified circle or undirected edge
should not be penalized merely because a simulator internally selected one
fully directed graph. Orientation informativeness can be reported alongside
validity. This makes a method that preserves genuine ambiguity distinguishable
from one that returns little information and from one that confidently
overorients the graph.

Identification outcomes also need separate labels. Scientific
nonidentification, unsupported implementation, malformed output, explicit
abstention, timeout and missing input are not the same event. A well-designed
agent can correctly identify a missing premise without successfully computing
an effect. A backend can be unable to implement a valid functional. Combining
these into one ``incorrect'' or ``no answer'' category would obscure the
remedy.

For identified scalar targets, bias and error can be meaningful. For reported
sets, evaluate coverage, topology, finite availability and size. Whole-line
answers can have high coverage and little decision value. A method that
returns short intervals on a selected easy subset needs an all-request
availability denominator. Unbounded and disconnected sets must remain in the
evaluation rather than being replaced by finite plotting limits.

For an eligible finite interval \([l,u]\), one prospective score at nominal
level \(1-\alpha\) is
\[
 (u-l)+\frac{2}{\alpha}(l-\theta)1\{\theta<l\}
       +\frac{2}{\alpha}(\theta-u)1\{\theta>u\}.
\]
The formula balances length with penalties for missing the target. It is
not an instruction to compress a union of intervals into one interval. For
unions, coverage and total Lebesgue length can be reported while retaining
infinite lengths. Raw losses should not be capped simply to make a plot or
ranking convenient. The eligible target type must be stated before the
score is selected.

\section{Contamination, adaptation and selective reporting}

An exposed demonstration cannot become a held-out evaluation merely because
its variables are renamed. The local problem fixtures and replay examples
have already been used to develop and debug the prototype. They can continue
to test conformance, but they cannot provide independent estimates of a
language model's causal accuracy.

The final design needs a frozen development/test split, mechanism identities,
prompts, model/provider revisions, retrieval corpus and ranking rules, numerical
baselines, stopping rules and analysis code. Mechanism families should be
separated where family reuse would reveal the answer. Label novelty and
mechanism novelty should be varied independently. An unfamiliar name attached
to a memorized mechanism is not the same test as an unfamiliar mechanism.

Test outcomes cannot be used to tune prompt templates, choose the best
retriever, strengthen selected priors or discard difficult cells while
retaining a final-test interpretation. A changed method requires a new
reviewed evaluation revision. Failed and unavailable requests remain in the
record. Reporting only the critic-approved subset would confound answer
quality with selection by the critic.

The inspected OCI paper provides a useful refusal example: its critic
declines many replications when overlap is poor. That can be preferable
to an unsupported estimate, but it makes the denominator essential.
The reported successful answers, refused requests, review effort and
remaining target population must all be visible. The external results
are author reports, not a validation of this project's critic.
\cite{v12_la_2607_22443}

\section{Decision value and cost}

The ultimate question is whether assistance improves feasible decisions at
an acceptable total cost. In a known synthetic mechanism, a policy's expected
loss can be calculated under the mechanism and compared with the chosen
baseline. In a bank, the feasible policy, valuation model, risk limits,
operating costs and outcome truth need authentic inputs. Synthetic decision
loss does not establish institutional return on investment.

The prospective cost record includes model calls, input/output/cache tokens,
retrieval, numerical CPU time, wall time, memory, retries and human review
and rework. Actual dated prices are needed to turn these quantities into a
currency total. Unknown prices remain missing; zero live calls in an offline
prototype do not imply a free live workflow. A fast answer that requires
substantial correction can have a worse total cost than a slower transparent
analysis.

No final live-model experiment is reported by this chapter. Five prerequisite
classes remain: an exact live backend and custody terms; actual prices and
a bounded budget; independent held-out mechanisms and original benchmark
bytes; named business/diagram adjudicators and a rubric; and qualified
numerical baselines. These are missing program inputs. No credentials were
read and no provider endpoint was probed to infer that a service is unavailable.
The design provides a route to evaluation once those inputs are supplied;
it provides no current empirical model-performance claim. The remaining studies turn these requirements into inspectable tests: first the probability of passing a coverage rule, then a prospective comparison, and finally the reliability of its references, evaluators and numerical handoffs.
